recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 egg white beaten with 1 tbsp water

steps.text: Combine the flour, yeast, salt and sugar, then add the water and oil and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape each into a tight ball, and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cover and let rise for 30 to 40 minutes until puffy.
Place an empty metal pan on the bottom rack and preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Brush the rolls with egg white, sprinkle with seeds if desired, and cut a deep slash across the top of each with a sharp knife.
Put the rolls in the oven, pour 1 cup of hot water into the empty pan to create steam, and quickly close the door.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped, then cool on a rack.

recipes.photoCredit: fir0002 flagstaffotos [at] gmail.com Canon 20D + Tamron 28-75mm f/2.8 / Wikimedia Commons, GFDL 1.2 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bread_rolls_at_a_bakery_(cropped).jpg

recipes.title: Bubble Tea
recipes.description: Bubble tea is a tea beverage with black tapioca pearls mixed in.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (125 ml) cooked boba tapioca pearls
1 cup (250 ml) very strong chilled black tea
Honey or granulated sugar, to taste

steps.text: Place pearls in a large glass.
Combine all remaining ingredients in a cocktail shaker. Shake vigorously until mixture is frothy.
Pour into glass and serve with large-diameter straws.

recipes.notes: If you don't want the drink to be frothy, simply stir the ingredients together instead of shaking. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Bulgogi
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) beef suitable for grilling, sliced as thin as possible
3 green onions, sliced on the bias

steps.text: Combine all the ingredients in a big bowl. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, but marinating overnight will get the best flavor and tenderization.
Grill the beef.
Serve with rice.

recipes.notes: Use same amount of soy sauce and sugar. If you do this a day ahead, reduce the amount of soy sauce and don't forget to put it in a refrigerator. Use thinly-sliced beef, available specifically for Bulgogi in some grocery stores, for best results. You can grill this on a table top, with a shallow pan. You can also use just a normal fry pan. Grill over medium-high heat and have the juice of beef and vegetables on rice. You may marinate the beef in cola (Coca-Cola works best) instead of using just sugar. The extra liquid helps the meat to absorb the marinade more quickly. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: brappy! (a flickr user) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Korean.food-Bulgogi-01.jpg

recipes.title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken with Pan Gravy
recipes.description: Fried chicken is a Southern main meal in the USA, served often at "Sunday dinner" ("dinner" being the midday meal for many Southerners) or church "suppers" ("supper" being the term for the evening meal). Recipes are legion; every family has one handed down.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Flour seasoned with herbs and spices (e.g. pepper, cayenne, salt, ground coriander, cinnamon, thyme, oregano)
3 cups chicken stock (or 2 cups stock + 1 cup cream)

steps.text: Chicken: Cut the chicken into 8–10 pieces.
Combine the buttermilk and spices, and marinate the chicken pieces for 4 hours in the mixture.

Take each chicken piece out of the marinade and allow it to drip dry for a few seconds. Then, dredge it in seasoned flour. An easy way to dredge involves putting flour and seasonings in a small plastic bag, dropping the piece in, and shaking.
Let the pieces rest (separately; do not stack) for about 10 minutes. Then dredge them again. The first dredging absorbs the buttermilk marinade. The second dredging gives a seasoned flour outer coat.

Heat the oil in a deep, wide pan. When oil is smoking hot, drop chicken pieces into the pan, and be careful to not overcrowd (pieces should not touch; fry in multiple batches). After 3 or 4 minutes, turn the chicken, and reduce the heat. Let the chicken fry for 20–25 minutes, turning the pieces every few minutes. When the chicken is a deep golden-brown, and the juices run clear, it's done. The chicken will continue to cook after being removed from the pan, so err on the side of "just about done".
Drain the chicken on absorbent paper or cloth. If you are not serving the chicken immediately, place it in a lightly-warmed oven, uncovered, separately (not stacked).

Gravy: Pour off the accumulated oil from the pan, reserving 3–4 tablespoons and all the flour and chicken residue. Keeping the pan on medium flame, add the chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for a few minutes. Whisk in 3–4 tablespoons of flour, and keep stirring until the mixture becomes light to medium brown. Do not burn.
Whisk in 3 cups of chicken stock. Simmer over low heat, covered, for 15 minutes. Salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken with rice and some green vegetables. Spoon gravy over rice and chicken.

recipes.notes: The spice mix isn't fixed. You can use more or less as desired. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Buñuelos (Sweet Fried Pastry)
recipes.description: Buñuelos are a type of Latin-American fried pastry.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: In a large bowl combine eggs with 1/4 cup sugar, and beat until thick and lemon-colored. Add the oil.
Combine 1 1/2 cups of the flour, the baking powder, and the salt. Gradually add this to the egg mixture and beat well.
Turn dough out onto a floured board (use remaining 1/2 cup flour) and knead thoroughly until dough is smooth.
Shape dough into 16 balls. Roll each one into a circle about 5 inches (13 cm) in diameter. Let stand uncovered on waxed paper for about 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (175°C). Fry dough circles until golden brown, turning once. Drain on paper towels.
Combine the cinnamon and 1 cup sugar. Sprinkle fried dough with sugar/cinnamon mixture. Store in an airtight container.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Baptiste Pons from Gandia / Burjassot, País Valencià, Spain / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bunyol_de_carabassa.jpg

recipes.title: Cajun Red Beans and Rice
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 pound dry red beans (e.g. kidney or cowpea)
6 ea. (3 1/2–4 pounds / 1.5–2 kg) large ham hocks
3 Tbsp Paul Prudhomme's Seafood Magic, or a similar spice
1 Tbsp tabasco sauce or similar hot sauce

steps.text: Cover beans with water, and let soak overnight. Drain.
Place ham hocks, celery, onions, bell peppers, bay leaves, and seasoning into a large saucepan with 10 cups water. Cover and bring to boil.
Simmer until meat is fork tender, about an hour after boiling starts, stirring occasionally.
Remove ham hocks from pan and set aside. Skim fat from pan and discard.

Remove a significant fraction of liquid from pan, add drained beans, and add back just enough liquid to cover beans. Simmer beans until they just begin to break up and the liquid starts to become creamy, about 45 minutes. Stir frequently. Add back liquid as needed to keep beans covered. If beans begin to scorch, do not stir; transfer mixture to another pan without scraping scorched beans into new pot.
Add ham hocks and cook 45 minutes more, and serve immediately.
On a heated serving platter, mound 3/4 cup rice per serving at one end of platter, place ham hocks at other end, and put 1 cup beans per serving in middle.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Will7777 at en.wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Red_beans.jpg

recipes.title: Camotes Enmielados (Mexican Sweet Yams)
recipes.description: Camotes enmielados, also known as camotes con pilocilo, or camotes enmielados al horno, camotes con piloncilo al horno, is a baked, or stovetop, dessert-style Mexican yam/sweet potato dish. It is traditionally a home-cooked food, not typical restaurant fare. The finished product should have a strong caramel flavor, with a typical hint of bitterness from the molasses component of the sugar used.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 large yam or sweet potato, optionally peeled

steps.text: Place whole or thickly-sliced yams in a large baking dish.
Place piloncilo cone atop the yams, then add water and cinnamon.
Cover dish, and bake for about 60 minutes, basting the yams with the now sweetened cooking liquid as needed.

recipes.notes: Any dark, unrefined sugar may be reasonably substituted for the piloncilo, including turbinado sugar, brown sugar, brown sugar with added molasses, muscovado, and even jaggery. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Candied Yams
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 °F (175 °C).
Boil yams in skins until about half done.
Drain water from yams, remove skins, and cut in cubes.
Place yam cubes in a greased baking dish and dot with margarine.
Make a syrup by boiling brown sugar, water, and vanilla together. Pour over the yams.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, basting frequently with syrup, until yams are tender.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Cantonese Crispy Fried Chicken
recipes.description: Crispy fried chicken is a Hong Kong/Cantonese specialty.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 4 cups oil (or enough for deep fryer)
Prawn crackers/shrimp chips (not the ready made ones)

steps.text: Pepper salt: Put salt and peppercorns in a small pan. Heat on medium to low heat until it barely smokes.
Remove from heat.
Grind well in mortar and pestle, or with a rolling pin.
Add ajinomoto and mix well.
Poaching: Clean and rinse off chicken, discarding the giblets.
Heat enough water to cover the chicken in a pot until boiling.
Put five-spice powder, ginger, and scallions in a cloth and tie it. Add to water, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add chicken, reduce heat, and gently poach for 20 minutes.
When chicken is done, remove from heat, then pat dry with paper towels and air dry for a little bit.
Put vinegar and sugar in saucepan, and heat until dissolved to make a syrup.
Coat the entire chicken on the inside and outside with the syrup.
Let chicken dry in a breeze until very dry.
Frying: Fill deep fryer with oil, and heat oil to 350°F (175°C).
Deep fry chicken about 10 minutes per side until brown and done.
Remove from oil, and chop with a meat cleaver into 1 x 2-inch pieces.
When chicken is done, fry the shrimp chips in deep fryer.
Sprinkle shrimp chips with a little salt.
Serve chicken adorned with shrimp chips, with pepper salt in a small dish on the side.

recipes.notes: Poaching is not the same as boiling, since the temperature is lower, about 160–180 °F instead of at 212°F, and is even lower than simmering. If boiled, the meat will come out tough and dry. Also the lower the poaching temperature, the longer it will take to poach. Drying the skin is important, since it helps the syrup to stick. The second drying also is important, since that is what helps to make skin crispy. It can be done the day before, and the chicken kept in the fridge. The caramelized sugar gives the nice brown color. Vinegar lowers the pH, and helps the caramelization. Oil temperature is important, since it imparts the brown color to the skin. If the oil temperature is too low, the sugar will not caramelize, and the chicken will not be brown. If it is too high, the sugar will burn. If you don't have a temperature controlled fryer, use a frying (or candy) thermometer. A deep fryer  (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Cantonese Roast Duck
recipes.description: This is a recipe for Cantonese roast duck or goose (燒鴨\燒鵝).
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 Tbsp dark soy sauce (optional, can use light soy sauce instead)
2 cups (450 ml) of white wine, sherry, or Chinese cooking wine
3–6 lb (1.3–2.6 kg) whole duck or goose

steps.text: Mix all marinade ingredients together.
Mix all glaze ingredients together.
Brush the marinade mixture all over the duck, inside and outside.
Brush some glaze mixture inside the duck cavity.
Sit duck breast-up on a rack in an open container.
Put in the refrigerator to chill overnight.
Preheat oven to 450°F (220°C)
Put 1/2–1 inch (2.5 cm) of water in a roasting pan—this catches the grease that comes out from the duck while roasting and prevents it from smoking.
Place green onions inside the duck cavity.
Place the duck on a roasting rack in the roasting pan. Roast the duck for 15 minutes.
Turn the duck breast-up, and roast for another 15 minutes.

Turn oven heat to 375°F (190°C), and roast the duck until the internal temperature reaches a minimum of 180°F (test between the thigh, the thickest part of the duck/goose, being careful not to touch the bone)
Brush the duck with glaze, turn oven up to 450°F (200°C), and roast again for about 10 minutes.
Carve and serve!

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: No machine-readable author provided. PX404~commonswiki assumed (based on copyrig / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.5 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:HK_SYP_Ming_Sing_60402_16.jpg

recipes.title: Caramel Squares
recipes.description: Caramel squares (alternatively: caramel slices, caramel shortbread, or millionaire's shortbread) are a wonderfully rich and classic treat, very popular all over Britain and Ireland. They can often be found in cafes, served with morning coffee or afternoon tea. They're perfect for picnics, lunches and your guests will love them! They have a crunchy base with a creamy caramel filling, topped off with chocolate.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 340 g good-quality chocolate (milk or dark), melted

steps.text: Base: Preheat the oven to 180°C (gas mark 4; 350°F). Rub flour, butter, and caster sugar together until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Press into a 25 x 38 x 4 cm Swiss roll pan.
Bake for 20 minutes or till golden.
Cool.
Filling: Melt butter in a heavy-based saucepan over a low heat; add sugar, golden syrup, and condensed milk.
Stir continuously for 40–50 minutes. It should be golden brown in colour when ready to eat. To test, drop a little blob into a bowl of cold water; it should firm up.
Pour this caramel mixture over the base, and let it cool.
Topping: Pour melted chocolate over the top.
Spread the chocolate evenly, and let set.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Aurore D / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Millionaire%27s_shortbread.jpg

recipes.title: Carne Asada
recipes.description: Northern Mexican grilled flank steak marinated in citrus, garlic, and chile, sliced thin for tacos or served with beans and grilled onions.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Whisk together the orange juice, lime juice, olive oil, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Place the steak in a shallow dish or zip-top bag, pour the marinade over it, and refrigerate for 2 to 8 hours.
Preheat a grill to high heat and oil the grates.
Remove the steak from the marinade and pat off excess liquid.
Grill the steak for 4–6 minutes per side for medium-rare, until well charred.
Grill the green onions alongside for 2–3 minutes until softened and blistered.
Let the steak rest for 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Warm the tortillas on the grill and serve with the steak, green onions, and pico de gallo.

recipes.photoCredit: Daniel R. Blume from Toledo, Ohio, USA / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Carne_asada_(4472586086).jpg

recipes.title: Carnitas
recipes.description: Michoacán-style pork shoulder simmered in its own fat with orange and spices until meltingly tender, then crisped for tacos.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks

steps.text: Season the pork all over with the salt, cumin, and oregano.
Melt the lard in a large heavy Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the pork, onion, garlic, bay leaves, orange juice, orange peel, and water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the pork falls apart easily.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium, and cook for 15–20 minutes until the liquid evaporates and the pork begins to fry and brown in the fat.
Turn the pieces gently so they crisp on several sides, then lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Discard the onion, peel, and bay leaves and coarsely shred the pork.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, lime, and salsa verde.

recipes.photoCredit: Mike McCune / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Carnitas.jpg

recipes.title: Carrageen Moss Pudding
recipes.description: A delicate, old-fashioned Irish milk pudding set with carrageen seaweed and flavored with lemon and vanilla.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/4 oz (about 1/2 cup loosely packed) dried carrageen moss

steps.text: Soak the carrageen in lukewarm water for 10 minutes, then drain and pick out any grit.
Place the carrageen, milk, and lemon zest in a saucepan and bring slowly to a simmer.
Simmer very gently for 20 minutes, until the moss swells and the milk thickens slightly.
Beat the egg yolk with the sugar and vanilla in a bowl.
Strain the hot milk onto the yolk mixture through a sieve, pushing through all the jelly from the carrageen, and whisk well.
Beat the egg white to stiff peaks and gently fold it into the mixture.
Pour into a serving bowl or individual glasses and chill for 2 to 3 hours until set.
Serve with poached fruit, berries, or a drizzle of cream.

recipes.title: Carrot Cake I
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 50 g cream cheese or creamy cottage cheese

steps.text: Frosting: Mix all ingredients together.
Cake: Melt the butter and sugar together, then mix in the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg and add it to the batter.
Stir in raisins and nuts until everything is well combined.
Bake at 180°C (355°F) for about 50 minutes in a greased tin with greaseproof paper on the bottom.
When cake has cooled, top with cream cheese frosting.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Carrots Cooked Kinpira Style
recipes.description: Kinpira is a Japanese cooking term that roughly translates to sauté and simmer. The aim is to cook root vegetables such as carrots and burdock root in a minimum amount of water so that they end up tenderly cooked and with none of their flavour or nutritional value lost into discarded cooking water.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 Tbsp vegetable oil, preferably sesame oil
Tamari or shoyu soy sauce, to taste

steps.text: Cut the carrots into thin matchstick pieces (sen-giri, or julienned)
Pour a small amount of oil into a saucepan and sauté the carrot pieces briefly
Add just enough water to half-cover the carrot pieces
Place the lid on the pot and let the carrots simmer briefly on medium-low heat
Add a little tamari or shoyu to enhance flavour. Serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Cauliflower Cheese
recipes.description: Cauliflower cheese or cauliflower gratin (French: Choufleur au Gratin) is a filling and cheesy dish, great as a side to a roast dinner or any other dish.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Cut your cauliflower into small florets, and place them heads down into a bowl of salty water to dress them for an hour.

Drain florets, and add them to a saucepan of salted boiling water. Cook, uncovered, regularly checking the feel of the cauliflower with a knife to see when they are ready. Your knife should go smoothly, but with some firmness to the cauliflower still.
Preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan/390°F/gas 6).

Once the cauliflower has cooked, drain the florets and lay them in a dish of your choice. Combine the white sauce with 2/3 of the parmesan cheese, and pour over the cauliflower. Sprinkle over the breadcrumbs and remaining cheese.
Place your dish into the oven for about 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve immediately.

recipes.photoCredit: AnemoneProjectors - Peter O'Connor (talk; Flickr) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cauliflower_cheese_side_dish.jpg

recipes.title: Century Egg with Ham and Ginger
recipes.description: The century egg (a.k.a. preserved egg, thousand-year egg, hundred-year egg, hundred-year-old egg, thousand-year-old egg; Chinese: 皮蛋; pinyin: pídàn or Chinese: 松花蛋; pinyin: sōnghūadàn) is a Chinese delicacy made by preserving duck (or less commonly chicken) eggs in a mixture of charcoal and lime for (despite the name) around 100 days. It is greenish in color, has a creamy cheese-like flavor, and a strong aroma.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 small bowl of dark vinegar (use for dipping)

steps.text: Wash century eggs clean.
Shell the eggs, and cut each into 4 slices. Cut the pickled stem ginger into thin slices.
Cut the Jinhua ham into thin slices. Soak in water for a while.
Sandwich a slice of ginger with one of ham and a sliced century egg.
Serve with vinegar.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Chalupa
recipes.description: A chalupa is a kind of tostada platter in Mexican cuisine. It is a specialty of South-central regions of Mexico, such as the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca. It is made by pressing a thin layer of masa dough around the outside of a small mold and then deep frying it to produce a crisp shallow corn cup. It is typically filled with shredded pork meat, a slice of onion, and a piece of chipotle pepper.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 6 cups refried beans (pinto beans or black beans may be substituted)

steps.text: In a small skillet, heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil. Test the oil for the correct temperature by putting in a small piece of tortilla. If the oil immediately bubbles frantically and the bread quickly becomes crisp then the oil is at the right temperature. This is important because a low temperature will produce an unpleasantly oily and soggy chalupa shell.

Fry the tortilla completely flat in the oil, on both sides, until very crisp. Drain and keep the fried tortilla warm on a newspaper or paper towel-covered cookie sheet in a warm oven. Spread a layer of refried beans on each fried tortilla, about 1/4 inch thick. Top with a generous amount of grated cheddar cheese and about 1 tablespoon of chopped onion.
Place the assembled chalupas on a cookie sheet and brown under broiler until the cheese melts and begins to bubble. Watch them carefully at this stage, as they can burn quite quickly.
Top with shredded lettuce and tomato, and serve immediately.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: alex lines / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chalupas_(food).jpg

recipes.title: Champ (Irish Mashed Potato with Scallion)
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Boil potatoes in water until done.
Drain the potatoes and mash them.
Pour the milk into a saucepan, add the chopped scallions and cook vigorously.
When cooked, sieve the scallions and set the milk aside.
Add the scallions to the potatoes and mix well.
Add as much of the scallion-infused milk as possible to make a ‘wet’ soft mixture.
Season with freshly ground pepper and salt.
Serve with a central well filled with melted butter.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Champurrado
recipes.description: A thick, warming chocolate atole thickened with masa and sweetened with piloncillo, traditionally sipped alongside tamales in the cold months.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 4 oz piloncillo, chopped, or 1/2 cup packed dark brown sugar

steps.text: Whisk the masa harina into the water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Heat the milk with the cinnamon stick and piloncillo in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming and the sugar dissolves.
Add the chocolate and whisk until melted.
Slowly pour in the masa mixture, whisking constantly.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, whisking often, for 8–10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Remove the cinnamon stick, add the salt, and serve hot.

recipes.photoCredit: Tom White - Toboris at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.5 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Champurrado_thenewplace_sf.jpg

recipes.title: Chapati
recipes.description: The chapati, also known as a roti, is the staple flat bread of Northern India and Pakistan. It can be made from many types of grain, but is most commonly made with finely-ground whole wheat flour. Sometimes it is cooked in a little oil.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Knead together the flour and water, starting with only a slight dribble of water and adding more as you go until the dough becomes smooth but not too sticky.
Cover dough, and let rest for at least 5 minutes.
Divide dough into balls and roll out into disks, slightly thicker than denim material; sprinkle with flour as you roll.
Place a non-oiled pan over moderately high heat and test its surface temperature by holding your hand over it.
When very hot, put a chapati on the pan and press it flat with a spatula or dry cloth to make it rise up.
Flip and repeat so it becomes lightly browned on both sides.
If desired, brush with ghee.

recipes.notes: Regional variations abound in the detail of preparing and cooking roti. In most Indian cooking, for example, the roti is finished by toasting it in the open flame of the cooker. The aim of this process is to encourage the roti to puff up. The hot air which builds inside because the water inside the roti begins to turn into steam and cooks the roti inside out. This may also be achieved under a grill, or by using a microwave (try 30 seconds on high power). Universally, however, the aim in rolling is to get the roti to a perfectly round shape (for aesthetics) and to create uniform thickness, which is vital for successful cooking. There are Caribbean-specific variations of roti, one of which uses boiled and ground yellow split peas in its preparation. Chapatis are usually eaten with cooked dal (lentil soup) or vegetable dishes like Indian curry. Pieces of the chapati are used to wrap and lif (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Claude Renault / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Baking_Chapatis.jpg

recipes.title: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ pork)
recipes.description: Cha shao is a kind of spiced Cantonese honey roast pork. It is often also called by the Cantonese char siu or char siew. Sometimes (usually in America) it is called Chinese BBQ pork. It is very popular, and can be eaten by itself (usually cold), or used as an ingredient for other dishes such as cha shao bao (pork buns), or in noodles or rice.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Slice the meat into strips about 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide by 6 inches (15 cm) long. A long thin strip like this will keep its shape better when hanging.
Pierce the pork all over thoroughly with a fork. This makes the pork more tender and allows the marinade to penetrate the meat to give flavour all the way through.
Mix all other ingredients together to make a marinade.
Place pork strips in a tray and cover with marinade. Ensure strips are covered completely in marinade.
Cover tightly with cling film and place in the refrigerator for several hours (8–24 hours is preferable).
Preheat the oven to 230°C or 420°F and place a pan in the bottom to catch drippings. Line this pan with aluminium foil to make cleaning easier.
Hang the meat on hooks in the oven or lay them on a rack. Depending on the method and the size of your oven, it may be easiest to do this in two or three batches, rather than all at once.

Roast for 20 minutes, until pork is cooked all the way through. Baste at least twice to build up a good layer of marinade on the outside of the meat. The pork should turn a golden-red colour as it cooks.
Allow to cool while still hanging, or lay on wire rack to cool. Avoid laying on top of other meat or on a flat surface until cooled.
Cover and refrigerate until needed.

recipes.notes: Serve cold, or use diced in other dishes. Add 1 tbsp of toasted sesame oil for a nuttier flavour Add red food colouring to the marinade to give the traditional deep red hue. This used to be due to the preservative used for the pork. Also, in China, the red colour generally symbolises good fortune. However, due to the strong colour of the marinade described above, a significant quantity of food colouring will be needed. This dish goes very well with ginger and onion.
recipes.photoCredit: HAO ACKuSANE Husxima / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:HK_%E7%81%A3%E4%BB%94_Wan_Chai_Road_food_barbecue_BBQ_meat_Char_Siu_Yuk_rice_box_%E5%AE%8F%E7%99%BC%E7%87%92%E8%87%98_Wang_Fat_Roasted_Meat_Choi_Sum_February_2021_SS2_04.jpg

recipes.title: Charoset
recipes.description: A sweet apple, walnut and wine relish served at the Passover Seder to symbolize the mortar used by the Israelites in Egypt.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 3 crisp apples, peeled and finely chopped
1/3 cup sweet red wine or grape juice

steps.text: Toss the chopped apples with the lemon juice in a bowl so they don't brown.
Add the walnuts, wine or grape juice, honey and cinnamon and stir well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend.
Stir again before serving with matzo.

recipes.title: Chawanmushi (Savory Steamed Egg Custard)
recipes.description: A silky, delicate egg custard steamed in cups with dashi, shrimp, chicken, and mushrooms.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 oz boneless chicken thigh, cut into small pieces
4 sprigs mitsuba or 1 green onion, chopped

steps.text: Gently whisk the eggs in a bowl without creating foam, then stir in the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and salt.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a measuring cup to make it perfectly smooth.
Divide the shrimp, chicken, and mushrooms among four heatproof cups or ramekins.
Pour the egg mixture into the cups and skim off any bubbles from the surface.
Cover each cup with foil or a lid.
Bring water to a boil in a steamer, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Steam the cups over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the custard is set but still jiggles slightly in the center.
Top with mitsuba or green onion and serve hot.

recipes.title: Cheese Enchilada
recipes.description: This cheese enchilada recipe was handed down from the grandmother and mother of the original contributor.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chili powder and flour in oil in a 10–12-inch (25–30 cm) skillet until emulsified. Add water, bring to a simmer, and then stir for ~5 minutes until slightly thickened. Turn down heat to low.

Soak one tortilla in the chili gravy until softened (20–30 seconds). Remove tortilla from gravy, place flat on a plate, and add ~1 tbsp cheese and ~1 tbsp onion to center of the tortilla. Roll it up, and place with edges facing down in a 9 x 12-inch (23 x 30 cm) baking pan. Repeat this until you have used all the tortillas. If you get low on the gravy at the end, stir in 1/8–1/4 cup of water.
Cover the enchiladas with the remaining cheese, onions, and chili gravy.
Bake in oven for about 5 minutes—longer will toughen the cheese.
Serve hot.

recipes.notes: These freeze well, but defrost completely before reheating. In Tex-Mex cuisine, these are often served with Mexican rice, pinto beans, and guacamole salad. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Jon Sullivan / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Enchilada_Rice_Beans.jpg

recipes.title: Cherokee Bean Bread
recipes.description: Tender cornmeal dumplings studded with brown beans, wrapped in corn husks and boiled—a traditional Cherokee dish from the Southeast.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked pinto or brown beans, drained, with 1 cup cooking liquid reserved
16 dried corn husks, soaked in hot water for 30 minutes

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Mix the cornmeal, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in the boiling water and enough of the hot bean liquid to make a stiff dough that holds together.
Gently fold in the beans so they stay mostly whole.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a flat oblong cake.
Wrap each cake in two overlapping corn husks, fold in the ends, and tie with twine.
Drop the bundles into the boiling water, reduce to a steady simmer, and cook for 1 hour.
Drain, cool for a few minutes, and unwrap; serve warm with butter or alongside greens.

recipes.title: Cherokee Grape Dumplings
recipes.description: Soft dumplings simmered in sweet, purple grape juice, a beloved Cherokee dessert traditionally made with wild possum grapes.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 4 cups unsweetened Concord grape juice, divided
1/2 cup cold grape juice (taken from the 4 cups)

steps.text: Combine 3 1/2 cups of the grape juice with the sugar in a wide pot and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl and cut in the butter until crumbly.
Stir in the reserved 1/2 cup grape juice to form a stiff dough.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to 1/4 inch thick and cut into 1-by-2-inch strips.
Drop the dumplings one at a time into the boiling juice.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until the dumplings are cooked through and the juice has thickened.
Serve warm, with a spoonful of cream if you like.

recipes.title: Cherokee Ramps and Eggs
recipes.description: Wild ramps fried with potatoes and scrambled eggs, a springtime breakfast tradition among the Eastern Band of Cherokee in the Smoky Mountains.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Separate the ramp leaves from the white bulbs and stems and chop each separately.
Heat the bacon fat in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and salt and fry for 10–12 minutes, turning, until tender and golden.
Add the chopped ramp bulbs and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the ramp leaves and cook 1 minute until wilted.
Pour in the eggs and gently scramble with the vegetables until just set.
Season with pepper and serve hot.

recipes.title: Cherry Cobbler in a Crock Pot
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Pour cherry pie filling into a slow cooker, spreading it evenly across the bottom of the crock.
In a medium-size bowl, combine cake mix and butter until the mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle evenly over cherries.
Sprinkle nuts evenly over cake mix.
Set slow cooker on low, cover and allow to cook for 3 hours.
Serve hot, right from the slow cooker, or serve over ice cream, if desired.

recipes.notes: Any fruit pie filling will do. Refrigerate extra portions of this cobbler and mix it into hot oatmeal or yogurt for a breakfast treat. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 10.5 oz canned cream of celery soup

steps.text: Sear the cubed chicken in saucepan.
Place cooked chicken and remaining ingredients into a casserole dish.
Cover with foil and bake in oven at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Serve with rice.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Chicken and Dumplings
recipes.description: Chicken and dumplings is a traditional American comfort food.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Approximately 1 kilogram (2 pounds) cooked boneless chicken meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
Salt, pepper, and liquid seasoning to taste
20 grams (1 1/2 tablespoons) solid fat (such as vegetable shortening, lard or butter)

steps.text: Combine all the stew ingredients in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and allow to simmer while you make the dumplings.
For the dumplings, mix the dry ingredients together and cut in the shortening until the mixture is coarse and grainy.
Add milk and mix just until combined into a dough.
Drop dough by spoonfuls onto the stew.
Simmer 5 minutes with the lid off and 15–20 minutes longer with the lid on.

recipes.notes: You can buy chicken stock in cans or jars if you don't want to make it by hand. The stew portion of the recipe is very flexible. You can use whatever vegetables and flavorings you like and have on hand. To make it kosher, use vegetable shortening or schmaltz for the dumplings, and replace the milk with any plant milk. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Chicken and Leek Pie
recipes.description: A comforting pub-style pie of tender chicken and soft leeks in a creamy tarragon sauce beneath a flaky pastry crust.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
3 leeks, white and light green parts, sliced and washed
1 tbsp chopped fresh tarragon or 1 tsp dried

steps.text: Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in batches for 4 to 5 minutes; set aside.
Add the bacon and leeks to the pan and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until the leeks are soft.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the stock and cream, then add the mustard, tarragon, salt, pepper, and chicken.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken is cooked through, then let cool for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and spoon the filling into a 2-quart pie dish.
Cover with the puff pastry, trim and crimp the edges, cut a steam vent, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Biryani
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 3 cloves of garlic, crushed and chopped

steps.text: Cook soaked and washed rice.
Marinate the chicken in lemon juice, yoghurt, ginger, garlic, salt, turmeric powder, cumin powder, cloves, chillis, chopped tomatoes, and tomato purée.
Heat oil in a pan, add onions, and cook until onions turn golden brown. Add these to the chicken.
Grease a heavy-bottomed deep and wide mouthed pan. Add a layer of rice. Put in the chicken mixture, top with the rest of the rice, and put the saffron on top.
Bake in the oven for 1–1 1/2 hours at 150°C (300°F); cut into a piece of chicken to see if it is cooked.
Serve the biryani with yoghurt on the side.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.description: Chicken cacciatore is a classic Italian chicken dish. It is reddish, and the tomato adds a distinct flavor.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 3 lbs (1350 g), chicken parts with skin removed
14 oz (400 g) can of tomatoes with juice
5 1/2 oz (155 g) can of tomato paste
10 oz (280 g) can of mushroom pieces, drained
1/4 cup (60 ml) of white wine, chicken broth, or alcohol-free white wine

steps.text: Place onion and chicken in 3 1/2 quart (3.5 L) slow cooker.
Combine remaining ingredients in a bowl. Stir.
Pour over chicken and cover the chicken.
Cook on low for 6–8 hours or on high for 3–4 hours.
Discard bay leaf and serve.

recipes.title: Chicken Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
recipes.description: Juicy bite-size chicken thighs marinated in soy, ginger, and garlic, then coated in potato starch and fried until extra crisp.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces

steps.text: Place the chicken in a bowl with the soy sauce, sake, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, and sugar and toss well.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Drain off any excess marinade and toss the chicken pieces in the potato starch until evenly coated, shaking off the excess.
Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until pale golden, then transfer to a wire rack and rest for 4 minutes.
Raise the oil temperature to 350°F (180°C).
Fry the chicken a second time for 1 to 2 minutes until deep golden and very crisp.
Drain on the rack and serve hot with lemon wedges and mayonnaise.

recipes.title: Chicken Katsu Curry
recipes.description: Crispy panko-crusted chicken cutlets served over rice with a mild, sweet-savory Japanese curry sauce full of carrots and potatoes.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into chunks
1 (3.5 oz) box Japanese curry roux (such as Golden Curry), broken into pieces
4 (5 oz) boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts, pounded to 1/2 inch thick
4 cups cooked Japanese short-grain rice, for serving

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the onion, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the carrots and potatoes, stir for 1 minute, then pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, skim any foam, and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Turn off the heat, add the curry roux pieces, and stir until completely dissolved.
Stir in the ketchup and honey, then simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens; keep warm.
Season the chicken on both sides with salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes with the flour, beaten eggs, and panko, then coat each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, and press firmly into the panko.
Heat the frying oil in a deep skillet to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the cutlets two at a time for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Drain the katsu on a wire rack for 3 minutes, then slice into strips.
Spoon rice onto plates, lay the sliced katsu alongside, and ladle the curry sauce over and around it.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie II
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Heat oven to 425°F.
Prepare pie crusts as directed on package for a two-crust pie in a 9-inch pie pan.
In a medium saucepan, melt margarine over medium heat.
Add onion; cook 2 minutes or until tender.
Stir in flour, salt, and pepper until well-blended.
Gradually stir in broth and milk; cook, stirring constantly, until bubbly and thickened.
Add chicken, corn, and peas; remove from heat.
Spoon chicken mixture into crust-lined pan.
Top with second crust and flute; cut slits in several places.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until crust is golden-brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Chicken Teriyaki
recipes.description: Pan-seared chicken thighs with crisp skin glazed in a glossy homemade soy, mirin, and sake sauce.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and season lightly with salt.
Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and place the chicken skin side down.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes without moving, pressing gently, until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more until it reaches 165°F (74°C) inside.
Wipe out the excess fat with a paper towel and pour the sauce into the pan.
Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning the sauce over the chicken, until it reduces to a sticky glaze.
Slice the chicken, drizzle with the remaining glaze, and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onion.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka
recipes.description: Chicken tikka is a chicken dish originating in the Punjab region of the Indian Subcontinent made by baking chicken which has been marinated in spices and yoghurt. It should not be confused with Chicken Tikka Masala (of which it is an ingredient). It is traditionally cooked on skewers in a tandoor and is usually boneless. It is tasty when served with yellow rice and a spicy salad.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 675 g (1.5 lb) skinless and boneless chicken breast, diced into cubes
4 large cloves of garlic, finely chopped
1–4 chopped fresh red chillis (depending on strength of the chillis and the desired strength of the marinade)
1 tsp salt (use rock salt for best results)

steps.text: Add all of the ingredients except the chicken to a non-metallic mixing bowl, and mix well.
Add the chicken and mix until fully coated.

Ideally, the chicken should now be left in a refrigerator to marinate for at least 24 hours. It may not be safe to leave chicken which has previously been frozen for longer than 24 hours, but fresh chicken should be left to marinate for 48 hours for best results. If you do not wish to leave the chicken to marinate, simply continue to the next step.

For best results, place on skewers and cook in a tandoor or ceramic pot oven. The chicken can also be cooked on skewers under a medium grill for 5–8 minutes on each side or barbecued (cooking times depend on the temperature of the barbecue). Always ensure the chicken is cooked throughout before serving. It should come apart easily when pressed down with the side of a fork.
Serve with naan, with rice or use in a Chicken Tikka Masala.

recipes.notes: Mustard seed oil is considered unfit for human consumption in many parts of the world and is therefore not readily available. A poor alternative can be made by crackling 1 tsp of mustard seeds in approximately 2 tbs of very hot vegetable or olive oil. Allow to cool then use in place of mustard seed oil. It is possible to make a tikka with almost any meat, the most commonly used other than chicken being lamb and mutton. Tikka can be served either as main meal or as an appetiser. Powdered or dried ingredients can be substituted for fresh, but at the expense of taste. Some people prefer to make tikka with meat on-the-bone for improved flavour. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.description: Chicken tikka masala is a dish based on chunks of Indian-style roasted chicken (Chicken Tikka) cooked in a tomato curry sauce, originating in India. There is no standard recipe for chicken tikka masala; a survey found that, of 48 different recipes, the only common ingredient was chicken. The sauce usually includes tomato and either cream or coconut cream and various spices.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 4 large cloves of garlic, finely chopped
1–4 chopped fresh green chiles (depending on strength of the chiles and the desired strength of the sauce)
1 tbsp malt vinegar or tamarind extract

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan.
Add the garlic and onions and stir-fry until browned.
Add the curry pastes and mix well, adding a little water or yogurt.
Add the cooked chicken tikka, and stir-fry for two minutes to heat through.
Add the tomatoes, vinegar, tomato paste, and chilies and simmer for five minutes. Add more extra water if needed.
Add the cream, garam masala, and chopped cilantro and simmer for a few times.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with Naan, rice coloured yellow with turmeric, onion bahjis and/or a glass of white wine.

recipes.notes: Mustard seed oil is considered inappropriate for human consumption in many parts of the world and is therefore not always available. A poor alternative can be made by crackling 1/2 tsp of mustard seeds in approximately 2 tbsp of very hot vegetable or olive oil. Allow to cool, then use in place of mustard seed oil. Powdered or concentrated ingredients can be substituted for fresh ones but at the amount of taste. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Chicken Vindaloo
recipes.description: Vindaloo is a hot and spicy dish from the Goa region of India. Its heavy use of vinegar and the traditional meat of pork are due to the Portuguese influence on the area. Vindaloo is a popular Indian restaurant meal, where it is often made with pork, beef, chicken, lamb, prawns, or vegetables such as mushrooms.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Make the onion sauce: Take a thick-based frying pan, and pour into it enough vegetable oil to cover the base, with a little excess. Heat on a stovetop.
Slice the onions into fairly thin slivers. When the oil is very hot, add the onions.
Turn the stove down to a low heat, so the onions just gently sauté. After around 3 minutes they should be starting to caramelize.
Gradually turn up the heat and keep stirring the onions. You want them to brown quite heavily without burning.
Add the white wine vinegar, it will sizzle, and after a while will evaporate. Keep stirring. Fry for several more minutes, until they are very brown, but not burnt.
Remove the onions from the pan into a bowl, taking care to let as much oil as possible drip back into the pan. You should now have a bowl of nicely crisped fried onions.

Add the onions to a blender or food processor. Add around 1 tablespoon of oil, and process for around a minute until you have a fairly thick, dark brown sauce. This is the basic onion sauce from which vindaloo is made. It's also the onion sauce that gives the vindaloo the majority of its 'hot' taste, as it builds up as you eat the dish.
Remove sauce from blender and set aside.

Make the garlic/chili paste: Coarsely chop the garlic cloves (and ginger if you're using it). De-seed the chili peppers and chop in the same way. Add the chopped garlic and chillies to the food processor.

Blend the garlic and chillies until you have a fairly grainy (but liquid) sauce. For this I used an attachment on my blender which is intended to grind coffee beans. It has a much smaller container and so there's less waste.
Add the turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala and cinnamon to the sauce. Stir it until it's well mixed, and set aside.
Gently crush the black peppercorns in a mortar and pestle. Once coarse, add the mustard seed and rock salt. Continue blending until all the spices form a nice coarse powder.
Cook the paste and meat: Pour a little oil into a saucepan. Add the spiced garlic and chili paste to the pan. It needs to be slightly floating on oil, not touching the bottom of the pan.
When the sauce is quite hot and bubbling, add the chopped meat. Keep stirring so the meat absorbs the spice mix, until it is browned and mostly cooked.

Add onion sauce and simmer: Now add the onion sauce to the pan. After stirring for 1 minute, add a little water and stir for another 2 minutes, then turn the heat to quite low. The sauce at this stage should be quite runny, and orange/tan in color. Remember a lot is going to evaporate off as it cooks.
At this stage you can add some vegetables. Half a cup of frozen peas works well.
Place a lid over the pan, and cook for around 30-40 minutes. Keep checking and stirring the pan every 5 or 10 minutes to make sure it doesn't stick or burn.The sauce will darken in color as it cooks.
Towards the last 15 minutes of cooking time, boil 2 cups of pilau, or basmati rice in a pan.
To serve- spoon the curry over the top of the rice. Sprinkle the chopped coriander leaves over the curry, and serve immediately.

recipes.notes: Powdered or dried ingredients can be substituted for fresh, but at the expense of taste. If you don't have fresh ginger use 2 cloves garlic + 1 tsp dried ginger powder. To cook a more intensely spiced but still field tested variation of this recipe consider the following modifications: Double the amount of each of these ingredients: chosen chilies (if you like very spicy curry) garlic (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Carpathia at English Wikibooks / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chicken_Vindaloo.jpeg

recipes.title: Chilaquiles
recipes.description: The following recipe is quite common in most of Mexico as a breakfast item, due to the addition of eggs, but is also eaten throughout the day including during dinner time. The additional recipe for a salsa de chile de árbol will be used as the primary sauce.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Vegetable oil (enough to cover the tortillas to deep-fry them)
2 day-old corn tortillas, cut into strips then squares

steps.text: Salsa de chile de árbol: Roast the tomatillos by wrapping them in heavy duty aluminum foil and placing them on a comal (cast iron skillet) over your stovetop (this does not need to be done in the oven; it never is in Mexico).
After roasting the tomatillos for approximately 15 to 20 minutes, pull them off the heat and reserve.
Roast the dried chilies and garlic directly on the comal. Caution: the dried chilies will roast in less than a minute while the garlic will take longer.

Combine the roasted tomatillos, chilies, garlic, water, salt, and pepper in a blender. Liquefy the mixture thoroughly for a few minutes to ensure that the sauce is smooth and consistent with no large pieces left floating around. You will probably end up with more salsa than you need for this recipe. Use it as a condiment for any other of your favorite Mexican dishes!

Chilaquiles: Heat enough vegetable oil in a frying pan to deep fry the tortillas. It should be hot enough so that when you drop the pieces of tortillas into it they immediately begin to fry at a rapid pace.
Allow the tortillas to fry until they become a chestnut brown, just not too dark or burnt. At this point, drain most of the oil out of the pan leaving only enough to fry the rest of the ingredients.

Crack the egg into the fried tortillas and scramble it, folding the fried tortilla strips into the egg. At this point season this mixture with salt and pepper if desired. Take this mixture out of the pan and let it rest on a plate while you continue with the rest of the dish.

Add some of the oil that was taken out of the pan earlier back into it and heat it up again. To this add the diced onion, and allow it to soften for a few minutes. Add the salsa de chile de árbol to the oil and onions and sauté it for a minute or two. Add a little bit of water to dilute it if it becomes too thick.

Finally, return the fried tortilla and egg mixture to the onion and chili sauce in the pan and allow it cook only for about a minute, enough time to allow the tortillas to soak up some of the sauce. Before plating it, add the cheese and enjoy!

recipes.notes: In Mexico, very rarely is this dish made with tortilla chips but rather day-old tortillas that have stiffened. If you don't have day-old tortillas you can leave out fresh tortillas until they are stiff to get the right texture. The chiles are very hot; adjust to taste. For the cheese, you can use anything that melts well such as Monterey Jack or Manchego The recipe for the chili sauce used in this recipe is of course a red sauce. If you prefer a green sauce, simply substitute the chiles de árbol with fresh jalapeño chilies that you can also roast in the same way. After you have roasted the chilies on the comal and thoroughly burnt the skins, place the chilies in a plastic bag with a small amount of water so as to allow them to steam. After about 5 minutes, remove the jalapeños from the bag and simply rub the skin off of them. Continue to make the sauce as indicated above. This dish can b (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Chris Woodrich / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chilaquiles_at_the_Grand_Cantina,_Windsor,_Ontario,_2025-09-01_04.jpg

recipes.title: Chiles en Nogada (Stuffed Chile Peppers with Almonds)
recipes.description: Chiles en nogada is a Mexican dish of stuffed chile peppers served with a nut-based sauce (nogada). Read the recipe carefully before preparing. Please note that this is a spicy dish.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Chiles: Cut the almonds in 2–4 pieces. Peel the peaches, apples, and pears, and chop them up in very tiny pieces. Set aside.
Fry the ground meat in a pan with garlic and salt (to taste) over low heat in a spoonful of oil.
When the meat is cooked, add the fruit and the raisins, and fry for about 4 minutes. Let cool.
Put the poblano peppers on the stove and let them get toasted.
After toasting them put the peppers in water and cut them on one of the long sides. Wash away the veins and the dark toasted spots on them.
Stuff the peppers with the fruit-meat mixture.
Crack and separate the eggs. Whip the whites until puffy, then beat in the flour and yolks until it reaches a yellowish point.
Dip the whole pepper in the yellowish content that you just prepared and put in a pan to fry until light brown. Do repeatedly until done with all the peppers. Set aside while you make the nogada.
Nogada: Grind the walnuts, milk, cheese, and rum in the blender for about a minute. After it will look white if done right
Pour over the peppers and enjoy!

recipes.notes: To peel almonds yourself, boil them for 60 seconds and then soak them in cold water. You can then slip the skins off. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Jessica Toledo / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chile_en_nogada24.jpg

recipes.title: Chiles Rellenos
recipes.description: Roasted poblano peppers stuffed with melting cheese, dipped in a fluffy egg batter, fried golden, and served in a light tomato caldillo.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 12 oz Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese, cut into thick sticks

steps.text: Roast the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under the broiler, turning, until blackened all over, about 8–10 minutes.
Place them in a covered bowl for 10 minutes to steam, then rub off the skins.
Cut a slit down one side of each pepper, carefully remove the seeds, and stuff with cheese; close with a toothpick if needed.
For the sauce, blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and broth until smooth, then simmer in 1 tbsp oil with the salt for 10 minutes.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold in the yolks one at a time and the salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Dredge each stuffed pepper in flour, shake off the excess, and dip it in the egg batter to coat.
Fry the peppers 2 at a time, spooning oil over the tops, for 2–3 minutes per side until golden; drain on paper towels.
Spoon the tomato sauce onto plates and set the chiles rellenos on top to serve.

recipes.photoCredit: Skyler Lewis (w:en:User:Double.reed) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chile_Rellenos.jpg

recipes.title: Chili Oil
recipes.description: Chili oil is a common ingredient, garnish and condiment in the cuisines of China and Vietnam, both for the complex and spicy flavours it imparts as well as its rich, red colour. While available in jars at most large Asian markets, chili oil is cheap and easy to make at home in whatever quantity is desired.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2–3 whole dried chiles (ancho, guajillo, or thai all work beautifully, though the latter creates a very spicy oil)

steps.text: If a smokey flavour is desired, toast the whole peppers and Szechuan peppercorn separately in a dry frying pan over medium-heat until you can smell them in the kitchen, stirring constantly (this takes only a few minutes). Chop the peppers if used (or cut them with scissors, or crush them in a mortar and pestle). Set aside.
Add your oil to a pot or saucepan over medium high-heat, and allow it to heat until the viscosity of the oil is reduced and the surface shimmers.
To the hot oil, carefully add all remaining ingredients. Stir gently, lowering the heat if required to keep the oil below a simmer.
Remove from heat once the chilis have blackened, and allow the oil to cool (the chilis will sink to the bottom).

In higher-class restaurants in China and abroad, the oil is frequently strained or "poured off" of the layer of solids, which clarifies it somewhat; this step is optional. Many prefer the more rustic look (and texture!) of home-made oil, which will develop a darker colour over time from the solids below.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Chinese Almond Cookies
recipes.description: Crumbly, buttery almond cookies topped with a whole almond, traditionally shared for good fortune at Lunar New Year.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk together the flour, almond flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in the egg yolk and almond extract.
Add the dry ingredients and mix on low until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough into 1 1/4-inch balls, place them 2 inches apart on the sheets, and flatten slightly.
Press a whole almond into the center of each cookie and brush the tops with the lightly beaten egg white.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until the edges are lightly golden.
Cool on the sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.photoCredit: No machine-readable author provided. Mo707 assumed (based on copyright claims). / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Macau_Koi_Kei_Bakery_Almond_Biscuits_2.JPG

recipes.title: Chinese Rice Porridge (Congee)
recipes.description: Congee is a type of rice porridge eaten across Asia. It may also be called juk, zhou, ganji, or other similar variations.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 220 g (7.75 oz) round rice, washed and drained
2.5 L (10 1/2 cups) water or chicken broth
Light soy sauce, to personal preference

steps.text: Put the rice in a pan and add the bouillon or water. Bring to a boil.
Turn down the heat and leave over low heat for 1 hour and 45 minutes to 2 hours, or until all the rice has turned into a mash.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil and flavor with white pepper.
Finally, add the toppings according to personal preference.

recipes.notes: Do not overwash the rice, as doing so will wash out the starch, and the congee will not congeal properly. Congee can be made with most types of rice, to help other types of rice to break up, after washing drain and mix in a tea spoon of vegetable oil, then add the rice to the water after having brought the pot to the boil. If you are in a rush, initially start with about a third of the liquid you need, adding the remainder as you cook. Once the rice had turned into a mush and has released all its starch, a soup can be made by skimming off the top layer of liquid. You will only get one good bowl of this soup per pot of congee, and it is valued as a food for convalescents and babies. Instead of bouillon, a chicken carcass or pork bones can be added to the cooking water, the congee creates its own stock as it cooks. If using bones, blanch and wash under cold water before use. Very hot plain (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Daiju Azuma / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.5 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chinese_rice_congee.jpg

recipes.title: Chip Butty
recipes.description: A Chip Butty is a sandwich made of chips (French fries).
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Chips from a chip shop or homemade
Sliced white bread, or pita bread for kebab-shop style

steps.text: Make sure the chips are not too greasy and have been well drained.
Take two slices of bread (the heel works best) and butter both on one side, then apply ketchup and spread evenly over the bread.
Add chips in a manner akin to herringbone floor tiling, making sure to minimise any gaps. You can add multiple layers.
Put both slices of bread together, then put the assembled sandwich on a flat surface and slap it hard several times with with an open hand to crush the filling. Eat immediately!

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies II
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 pack (6 oz / 170 g) semi-sweet chocolate chips

steps.text: Combine the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Preheat the oven until it reaches 375°F/190°C.
In another bowl, cream the butter and sugars until light and fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla, and beat until smooth.
Mix in the flour mixture until well-blended.
Add the chocolate chips, and stir with a wooden spoon.
Drop the cookies onto a lightly-greased or parchment-lined cookie sheet by teaspoonfuls in 2-inch (5 cm) ball shapes.
Bake for 15 minutes or until the edges are light brown.
Remove the cookies from the cookie sheet with a metal spatula, then let them cool on a wire rack.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Chocolate Lava Cakes
recipes.description: Individual chocolate cakes with a warm, molten center — an easy, impressive Valentine's Day dessert for two or four.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: Butter and cocoa powder, for the ramekins

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Butter four 6-oz ramekins and dust them with cocoa powder.
Melt the chocolate and butter together and stir until smooth.
Whisk in the powdered sugar, then the eggs, yolks and vanilla.
Fold in the flour and salt until just combined.
Divide the batter among the ramekins and set them on a baking sheet.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until the sides are firm but the centers still jiggle.
Let stand 1 minute, run a knife around the edges and invert onto plates.
Serve right away with ice cream or berries.

recipes.photoCredit: FotoosVanRobin from Netherlands / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chocolate_Fondant.jpg

recipes.title: Chocolate-Dipped Strawberries
recipes.description: Fresh strawberries dipped in silky melted chocolate — a simple, elegant treat for Valentine's Day.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 6 oz semisweet or dark chocolate, chopped
1 tsp coconut oil or vegetable shortening

steps.text: Rinse the strawberries and dry them completely — any water will make the chocolate seize.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil in a bowl over simmering water or in the microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring until smooth.
Holding each strawberry by the stem, dip it in the chocolate, let the excess drip off and place it on the parchment.
Melt the white chocolate, if using, and drizzle it over the berries with a fork.
Refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes until set. Serve the same day.

recipes.title: Choctaw Banaha
recipes.description: Corn shuck bread from the Choctaw of Mississippi and Oklahoma: a cornmeal dough mixed with field peas, wrapped in husks, and boiled.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked field peas or black-eyed peas, drained
16 dried corn husks, soaked in hot water for 30 minutes

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Mix the cornmeal, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Pour in the boiling water and stir to make a stiff dough.
Fold in the cooked peas.
Shape the dough into 8 oblong rolls about 4 inches long.
Wrap each roll in two corn husks and tie the ends with thin strips of husk.
Drop the bundles into the boiling water and simmer for 40–45 minutes until firm.
Drain, unwrap, and serve warm with butter or alongside pork and greens.

recipes.title: Cholley (Chickpea Curry)
recipes.description: Cholley, also chole, choley, cholay, white cholay, chana, channa, or chana masala, is a popular and versatile Indian and Pakistani chickpea dish. It is commonly cooked in Northern India (especially Punjab) and Pakistan for breakfast, but it is also regularly served at dinner parties, picnics, wedding receptions and other special events.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Wash the chickpeas, then soak overnight in water, allowing them to soften somewhat. Make sure that the chickpeas are well-immersed with at least a few inches of water above them, as they will expand significantly while soaking.

The next day, drain the water and place the chickpeas in a pressure cooker or large cooking pot. Add the 500 ml fresh water and salt to taste, then cook until the chickpeas are tender (10 minutes at 15 psi in a pressure cooker; if using a regular pot, place the chickpeas in hot water to boil, and then reduce to a simmer for 60–90 minutes).

Heat the oil in a thick-bottomed pan. Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and nigella seeds, cooking them briefly until they crackle. Quickly add the onions and garlic, reduce the heat to medium, and sauté until the onions are transparent.
Add garam masala, tomato, turmeric, and salt and cook for 1 minute.
Add the boiled chickpeas, reduce the heat, and allow the cholley to simmer for around 15 minutes. Check that the gravy has thickened before removing from the heat.
Once done, place the cholley in a serving bowl, add your coriander garnish, and serve with rice or bread.

recipes.notes: Try adding coconut flakes and black pepper to taste. (Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Simon Law (sfllaw) from Montréal, QC, Canada / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chana_masala.jpg

recipes.title: Chow Mein
recipes.description: Chow mein is a generic Chinese term for a dish of stir-fried noodles, of which there are many varieties. Authentic chow mein is generally made of soft noodles, whereas chow mein in Westernized Chinese Cuisine may also be made from thin crispy noodles.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Vegetable oil for frying, as needed
1/4 cup water or low-sodium vegetable broth

steps.text: 1–2 hours before cooking, rinse the mung bean sprouts so that they have time to drain thoroughly.
Cut the seitan into thin strips. Add the marinade ingredients, adding the cornstarch last. Marinate the seitan for 20 to 25 minutes.

The following 3 steps can be completed while the seitan is marinating: To prepare the sauce, in a small bowl dissolve the 1 tablespoon cornstarch with the 4 tablespoons water. Whisk the water or vegetable broth with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, salt, pepper and cornstarch and water mixture and set aside. Soften the noodles by placing them in boiling salted water. Plunge into cold water to stop the cooking process and drain thoroughly. Wash all the vegetables as needed. Cut the celery and the bok choy into 1/2-inch pieces on the diagonal. If substituting broccoli for bok choy, peel the stalks until no more strings come out, and slice thinly on the diagonal. Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth and slice. Cut the red bell pepper in half, remove the seeds and cut into chunks. Peel and chop the onion. Dice the green onion.
Heat a wok or frying pan over medium-high to high heat. Add 2 tablespoons oil. When the oil is hot, add the noodles. Fry in batches until golden. Remove the noodles from the pan.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil. Add the onion and the seitan, keeping remaining marinade aside for later use. Let the seitan brown briefly, then stir-fry until the redness is gone and the seitan is nearly cooked through. Remove the cooked seitan and onion from the pan.

Cook the rest of the vegetables separately, except for the green onion, seasoning each with a bit of salt while stir-frying if desired. When cooking the bok choy or broccoli, add 1/4 cup of water and cover while cooking. Remove each of the vegetables from the pan when finished stir-frying. Add more oil as needed.

Give the sauce a quick re-stir. Add all the ingredients back into the wok, making a "well" in the middle of the wok for the sauce. Add the sauce and any remaining marinade, stirring quickly to thicken. Mix everything together. Stir in the green onions. Pour the cooked vegetable and sauce mixture on top of the noodles. Garnish the chow mein with the toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot.

recipes.notes: For crispy chow mein noodles, add more oil than the recipe calls for and cook the noodles longer to dry them out. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Christmas Cake
recipes.description: Christmas cake is a fruitcake traditionally served around Christmas in the United Kingdom, especially after long walks, to be had with tea.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 300 g lightly-salted soft margarine (The "Stork" brand is traditional)

steps.text: Fruit: Place all the fruit in a large bowl and pour the spirits over the mixture.
Cover the bowl in foil and leave in a cool place.
