Mix and stir the fruit every day for at least three days; after a fortnight most of the alcohol will have soaked in and further soaking has no benefit.
Cake: Beat together the sugar and margarine with the eggs.
Add the almonds and black treacle, and mix further.
Sieve the flours and the mixed spice into the mixture, beating until a smooth mixture results.
Combine with the pre-prepared fruit (above) and place in a cake tin lined with baking parchment.
Bake at a low temperature (140°C / 275°F / Gas mark 1) for at least 4 hours. It may take up to 5 hours, depending on the oven.
Once a knife comes out clean, remove from the oven and allow to cool fully.
Stored in an airtight box the cake should keep for at least four months.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: James Petts from London, England / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Christmas_cake_(6954064737).jpg

recipes.title: Christmas Pudding I
recipes.description: Christmas pudding is a dessert served typically around the Christmas festive period and on Christmas day in the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth countries such as Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and Canada. Outside of this festive period, it is known as a plum pudding which can have further recipe variations as well.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 25 g (0.88 oz / 1/4 cup) candied fruit peel
75 g (2.6 oz / 1/3 cup) unsalted butter plus extra for greasing
40 g (1.4 oz / 1/2 cup) almonds, chopped roughly
3 tbsp brandy, rum, or sherry and some extra for flaming

steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the raisins, currants, candied peel, and apple with zest and juice from the lemon and orange. Stir well and leave in the bowl for an hour for the flavours to combine.
In another bowl, cream together the butter and sugar using a spoon. When fluffy, slowly add in the eggs.
Sift the flour and spice together in another bowl. Add this bit by bit into the creamed butter and sugar, folding it in with the breadcrumbs and almonds. Then fold in the fruit mixture.
Liberally butter the pudding basin and place a small, round piece of baking paper in the bottom of the basin.

Slowly add the mixture into the basin and level the mixture out. Cut a layer of baking paper and foil for the top, leaving a crease in the middle so the pudding can expand, place it on top of the basin, and secure it with string.

Cook the pudding by either: Steaming for 8 hours: put the pudding into a steamer with simmering water. Cover with a lid and top up the water level as needed for 8 hours. Boiling for 7 hours: To boil, place a metal jam lid, or any kind of circular, thin metal object, at the bottom of a large pan to be a trivet. Create 2 strips of large string or foil and place them on the trivet so you can easily pick up your pudding once its cooked. Make sure there is enough to hang over the side of your pot, so its easy to get a hold of. Then, slowly place your pudding onto the trivet and pour boiling water in so that it reaches halfway up the side of your pudding bowl. Cover with a lid and let the water simmer for 8 hours until the pudding has reached a dark deep brown, adding more water as needed.

Remove your pudding and leave to cool for 1–2 hours. Once cool, remove the paper and foil and replace it with fresh paper and foil. Store in a cool, dry area. The pudding can be frozen for up to 1 year.
To serve, steam or boil your pudding for two hours to reheat. Once reheated, turn it out onto a serving plate.

To flame, warm a small amount of brandy in a pan, pour it over the hot pudding once at the table and light it with a matchstick or other easily used flame. Place your bowl of brandy butter on the table for people to enjoy with your pudding.

recipes.photoCredit: Matt Riggott from Edinburgh, Scotland / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Christmas-pudding-flames.jpg

recipes.title: Christstollen (Christmas Stollen)
recipes.description: A rich, buttery fruit bread studded with rum-soaked raisins, candied peel and almonds, coated in powdered sugar.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Soak the raisins and candied peel in the rum overnight or for at least 2 hours.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, spices and lemon zest, then add the milk, egg and softened butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth dough.
Knead in the drained fruit and the almonds, cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 hours.
Divide the dough in half and roll each piece into an oval about 10 x 8 inches.
If using marzipan, roll it into two logs and lay one down the center of each oval.
Fold one long side over past the center to form the classic stollen shape and press the edge lightly.
Place the loaves on a lined baking sheet, cover and let rise for 45 minutes while you preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 190°F (88°C).
Brush the hot loaves generously with melted butter, dust heavily with powdered sugar, and repeat once they cool.
Wrap tightly and let the stollen mature for at least 3 days and up to 3 weeks before slicing.

recipes.title: Churros I
recipes.description: This is a very simple recipe for plain churros. Makes one plateful, suitable for about 4 people. It can easily be doubled or halved, but be warned that attempting to mix more than double this recipe at once is very hard work.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Sift the flour, baking soda, and salt into a large mixing bowl.
Add the boiling water gradually to the flour, mixing constantly until you get a very thick, smooth paste.
Allow to stand for about an hour.
Heat up a deep frying pan of oil until it shimmers.

Using an icing bag, or a freezer bag with the corner cut out to give a hole about the size of your little finger, squeeze the paste into the pan. Use a pair of scissors to cut the sausage-shaped pieces off after about 10 cm.
Fry the churros until golden brown and crunchy. If the pieces are too thick and are still raw in the middle, cut them in half lengthwise and fry again.
Remove churros from oil, and drain on a rack or paper towels.
Serve dusted liberally with sugar or hot chocolate sauce (or both).

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Cincinnati-Style Chili
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Crumble the raw ground beef into the cold water.
Add remaining ingredients and spices. Stir well, breaking the meat up before cooking.
Cover and simmer over low heat for two hours, stirring occasionally.
Cool, then refrigerate and remove solidified grease.
Reheat and serve as desired.

recipes.notes: Serve over spaghetti. Top with cheese to make a Three-way, top with onions and cheese to make a Four-way, top with cooked pinto beans, onions and cheese to make a Five-way. May also be used as hot dog sauce with mustard and minced onions to make a Coney, adding shredded cheese to make a Cheese Coney. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Cioppino (Italian Seafood Stew)
recipes.description: Cioppino is a fish stew descended from the various regional fish soups and stews of Italian cooking. It was developed by the fishermen who settled in the North Beach section of San Francisco. Originally it was made on the boats while out at sea and later became a staple as Italian restaurants proliferated in the city.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 3/4 teaspoon dried crushed red pepper flakes, plus more to taste
2 pounds crabs (any type), cut into pieces
1 1/2 pounds tilapia (or other white, firm-fleshed fish), cut into 2-inch chunks
2 loaves of San Francisco sourdough bread or any other bread with a chewy crust

steps.text: Heat the oil in a very large pot over medium heat.
Add the fennel, onion, shallots, and salt and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste.
Add tomatoes with their juices, wine, water, crabs, celery and bay leaf. Cover and bring to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Simmer, covered, for about 30 minutes to allow the flavors to blend.
Add the mussels to the cooking liquid. Cover and cook until the mussels begin to open.This should take about 5 minutes.

Add the scallops and fish. Simmer gently until the fish and scallops are just cooked through and all the mussels are completely open, gently stirring occasionally. This should take about another 10 minutes.
Check the soup for closed mussels and throw them out. Remove the bay leaf.
Season the soup to taste with more salt and red pepper flakes.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Kelly Sue DeConnick / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cioppino.jpg

recipes.title: Classic American Apple Pie
recipes.description: A classic apple pie is a double-crusted pie filled with sweetened and spiced apples. The exact spices vary by recipe, but cinnamon is traditional.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 8 ounces cold butter, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
5–7 tbsp applejack (apple brandy) or hard cider
6 Honeycrisp apples, peeled, cored, and cut into 12ths

steps.text: Combine dough ingredients to get a mealy dough. Split in half by weight, shape into 2 disks, and chill for 1 hour.
Toss apples with 1/4 cup sugar and place in a colander set over a large bowl. Let drain for 1 1/2 hours.
Transfer liquid from bowl into a saucepan, and bring to a boil over medium high heat. Cook until reduced to 2 tbsp. Set aside.
Toss apples with remaining filling ingredients. Set aside.
Roll out both disks of crust into rough circles. Place one inside a 9 1/2–10-inch tart pan and attach.

Add apples to the crust in a concentric circle, starting from the outside and working to the inside, making the center slightly taller than the outside. Pour any liquid in the bottom of the bowl over the apples.
Top with the second sheet of dough, and seal the edges. Crimp the edges if desired, then snip 3 incisions in the center. Brush top with reduced apple liquid.
Bake at 425°F on the floor of the oven in a half sheet pan lined with parchment for 30 minutes. Transfer to the lower rack, and bake for another 20 minutes.
Remove and cool for 4 hours. Serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Classic Glazed Meatloaf
recipes.description: An old-fashioned American meatloaf made with beef, onion and milk-soaked breadcrumbs, baked under a sweet and tangy ketchup glaze.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the onion and cook for about 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute and let the mixture cool.
In a large bowl, stir together the breadcrumbs and milk and let them soak for 5 minutes.
Add the eggs, 2 tablespoons ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, parsley, salt and pepper to the soaked crumbs and whisk to combine.
Add the ground beef and the cooled onion mixture and mix gently with your hands just until evenly combined; do not overwork the meat.
Shape the mixture into a loaf about 9 x 5 inches on the prepared baking sheet.
Stir together the 1/2 cup ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar and mustard to make the glaze, and spread half of it over the loaf.
Bake for 45 minutes, then brush on the remaining glaze and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Let the meatloaf rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving with mashed potatoes and green beans.

recipes.photoCredit: Renee Comet (photographer) / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:MeatloafWithSauce.jpg

recipes.title: Classic Pot Roast
recipes.description: This pot roast recipe is even better than your mom made.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 ea. (2 1/2 pounds / 1.1 kg) bottom round roast
3 carrots, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch (2 cm) pieces

steps.text: Season roast liberally with kosher salt and freshly-ground black pepper.
In a 6-quart (6-liter) Dutch oven, heat 1/4 cup olive oil over medium-high heat. Add roast and cook until browned on all sides.
Remove roast to a plate and keep warm.
Add remaining oil and vegetables. Cook until onions are lightly browned around edges.
Remove vegetables and keep warm.
Deglaze pan with broth and add remaining ingredients. Reduce heat to low, then add vegetables and beef.
Cover and place into a 225°F (110°C) oven and cook 6 hours.
Serve warm.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Mark Miller / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:American_pot_roast.jpg

recipes.title: Cochinita Pibil (Mexican Braised Pork)
recipes.description: Cochinita pibil (also puerco pibil) is a traditional Mexican slow-roasted (braised) pork dish from the Yucatán.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Banana leaves and/or heavy-duty aluminium foil
White or Spanish rice, taco shells, or tortillas for serving

steps.text: Place the annatto, cumin, peppercorns, allspice, and cloves in a spice grinder and process to a fine powder. You can use an electric coffee grinder for the spices, but it will not be suitable for coffee afterwards.
Remove the seeds and veins from the habanero chiles and chop coarsely. If you want a hotter dish, leave some of the veins and seeds in.
Process the orange juice, vinegar, chiles, salt, garlic, and the spice powder in a blender or food processor until liquefied. Add the lemon juice and tequila.
Cut the pork into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks. Leave the fat on the meat, to keep the pork moist while roasting; you can remove it after cooking if you wish.
Place pork in a large, self-sealing plastic bag with the marinade. Seal bag and turn to evenly coat the meat. Refrigerate for 8 to 24 hours, turning occasionally.

Heat oven to 325°F (160°C). Dump the meat and the marinade in a roasting pan lined with banana leaves or foil, making sure to wrap tightly so no steam escapes. If using banana leaves, an outer wrapping with foil will help seal in the steam.
Bake for 4 hours. Open packet carefully; the meat should shred easily with a fork.
Serve over rice, or shred and serve with taco shells or tortillas.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Popo le Chien / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cochinita_pibil_2.jpg

recipes.title: Coconut Chutney (South Indian)
recipes.description: Coconut Chutney is served as a side dish for a lot of Indian snacks and breakfast items. It can be mild to extra hot depending on the individual preference. This recipe is from South India.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Dry roast the channa dal until browned. Allow it to cool.

Grind the roasated dal, coconut, chiles, tamarind paste, cilantro, ginger paste, and salt in a blender with as little water as possible. For best results the final consistency must be somewhere between a coarse and smooth paste.

For seasoning, heat the oil in a small ladle. Add the mustard seeds to hot oil, and allow them to crackle. When the crackling starts subsiding, add the asafoetida and the curry leaves, and stir for a few seconds.
Add the seasoning mixture to the chutney, and mix well.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Coddle
recipes.description: Coddle is a popular meal in Dublin. It's seen as an economical dish and can be stored in fridge and reheated in microwave. It goes well with soda bread or brown bread.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 250 g bacon, chopped into 3 cm pieces

steps.text: Completely submerge bacon, onions, and sausages in broth, then boil for about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, cutting into bite-sized pieces if necessary, then add the rest of the stock.
Return to the boil and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the potatoes have started to disintegrate, thickening the broth.
Add salt and pepper to serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Colcannon
recipes.description: Colcannon is a rich mashed potato dish with cabbage, butter, and other ingredients. It's very easy to make and is a nice change from ordinary mashed potatoes. Its sloppiness is balanced by the crunch of the cabbage, and it should taste a little peppery.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 450 g potatoes (floury Maris Piper or Golden Wonders are best; leave skin on if you want)
450 g white or savoy shredded cabbage
2 small leeks or 1 bunch of spring onion tops, chopped

steps.text: Boil or steam the potatoes until soft, then shake the drained spuds in a deep pot with the lid on, until they crumble.
Mash the crumbled potatoes up with a fork and season with the salt, pepper, and mace/paprika, before stirring in the cream.
Add 100 g of the butter in pieces and put the lid back on, leaving the butter to melt, then stir. Transfer the mix to a clean bowl.
Blanch the cabbage in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Fry the leeks in the remaining butter for a few minutes, then add the cabbage and toss around for a few more minutes.
Spoon the cabbage into the bowl and mix with the mashed potatoes.
Stir the gouda into the mix, leaving a little to coat the top. Put the bowl in an oven on 2/3 heat for 20 minutes or until the cheese is melted.

recipes.notes: The mixture may be turned into a greased pie dish, sprinkled with grated cheese, dotted with butter or margarine, and browned in a hot oven. Is especially good with dark greens such as savoy cabbage or kale. The Gouda is an innovation—leave it out, if you don't want the dish too rich. The oven heating is ideally done along with the final stage of your roast meat. Seasoning is very important: bear in mind that the cheese has plenty of salt. The perfect colcannon has a butter sogginess at the bottom of the bowl when removed from the oven. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Alison Cassidy / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Colcannon.JPG

recipes.title: Coleslaw I
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 4 tablespoons mayonnaise or 2 dL olive oil

steps.text: If adding cider vinegar, add it to the mayonnaise and mix together well.
Slice or shred the cabbage, as coarsely or finely as desired.
In a large bowl, mix cabbage and onion together with mayonnaise.
Set aside to allow the flavours to merge at least 20 minutes but preferably for a couple of hours.

recipes.notes: Savoy cabbage can be used instead of white cabbage Other vegetables can be added to the coleslaw for greater variety, including: Sliced bell peppers (red, yellow, and orange) Grated carrots Chopped nuts (e.g. almonds, walnuts) Some people prefer to sweeten the dressing by adding up to 2 tablespoons of sugar to the mayonnaise and vinegar (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bowl%27o%27Coleslaw_modified.jpg

recipes.title: Coleslaw II
recipes.description: This is not the watery goop you knew as a child! Serve chilled with something Southern, like fried chicken or some ribs.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Toss cabbage with a few big handfuls of kosher salt. Place in a colander in a bowl and let sit at room temperature 2 hours.
Drain cabbage. Rinse with clean water and let them go for a spin in your salad spinner until relatively dry.
Combine vinegar and spices. Microwave on high until mixture comes to a boil.
Fold in mayonnaise and cabbage. Chill until cold.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Conchas
recipes.description: Soft, slightly sweet Mexican breakfast buns crowned with a crackly sugar topping scored to look like a seashell.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/3 cup cold butter or vegetable shortening
1 tbsp cocoa powder (optional, for half the topping)

steps.text: Stir the yeast and 1 tbsp of the sugar into the warm milk and let stand 10 minutes until foamy.
In a stand mixer, combine the yeast mixture with the remaining sugar, eggs, butter, vanilla, and salt.
Gradually add the flour and knead with the dough hook for 8–10 minutes until the dough is smooth and slightly tacky.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll into balls, and space them on two parchment-lined baking sheets.
For the topping, mix the flour, powdered sugar, butter, and vanilla into a smooth paste; knead cocoa into half if you like.
Divide the topping into 12 portions, flatten each into a thin disc, and press one onto each bun.
Score the topping with a knife in a curved shell pattern.
Cover loosely and let rise for 45 minutes until puffy.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 18–20 minutes until the bottoms are golden, then cool on a rack.

recipes.title: Corn Chowder I
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups diced, pared potatoes, cut in 1/2-inch cubes

steps.text: In a medium saucepan, melt butter; add onion and celery and cook until tender.
Add potatoes, corn, salt, pepper, water, bouillon cubes, and thyme.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until potatoes and corn are tender.
Add milk and cream.
Heat through.

recipes.notes: If cooking outdoors, you can substitute evaporated milk or powdered milk. Paprika or pepper can be added for spicier flavor. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Corn_chowder_bowl.jpg

recipes.title: Corn on the Cob with Husks
recipes.description: Corn can be roasted over the fire or on the grill without using tinfoil by simply leaving the husks on. Soaking in advance prevents the husks from burning. Each ear of corn serves 1.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Corn on the cob, with husks left on

steps.text: Carefully peel back husk without detaching it and remove silk.
Replace husks and soak ears in cold water for 1/2 hour.
Place corn on grill or on a rack above an open fire.
Cook for about 15 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Serve with butter and salt.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Willis Lam / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:White_Corn_on_the_Cob_with_husk_(27000745034).jpg

recipes.title: Corn Pone
recipes.description: Corn pone is a small simple corn cake, similar to a johnnycake. It was originally cooked in ashes, and introduced to early European settlers by indigenous Americans.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Put on the water in a pot, and as soon as it boils stir in enough cornmeal to make a very thin batter.
Beat it frequently while it is boiling for 10 minutes; remove from the heat, pour it in a pan, and add the butter and salt to taste.
When the batter is lukewarm, stir in enough corn meal to make it quite thick.
Let rise overnight.
Pat the dough out into small cakes.
Butter a baking tin and bake in a moderate oven or butter a cake pan, fill it 3/4 full, and bake.

recipes.notes: This recipe did not originally have an oven temperature; 350°F is probably safe. To prevent lumping, mix some cool water into corn meal first, before adding boiling water. See details at Mixing flours or dry meal with hot liquids. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Cornbread I
recipes.description: Cornbread is a type of quick bread made of cornmeal and sometimes supplemented with wheat flour. Some variations may include whole corn kernels.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/4 cup (55 g / 1.9 oz) white granulated sugar (optional)
1/2 of a 15 oz can whole corn kernels, drained (optional)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425°F. Grease an 8 inch baking pan.
Combine cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Add egg, milk, and shortening.
Beat until fairly smooth (about a minute).
If using corn and/or onion, fold in these ingredients.
Pour the mixture into the baking pan.
Bake for 20–25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. If corn is added to batter, increase time by ~50%
Serve hot!

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Corned Beef Pie
recipes.description: Corned beef pie is a traditional British pie. It can be eaten hot or cold, making it good for picnics and also as a 'winter warmer'.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F, GM 6).
Sift the flour into a bowl. Rub in the lard and margarine.
Add enough water to bind the mixture into a dough.
Roll out half the dough and use it to line a large flan or quiche dish.
Boil the potatoes. Drain, add the butter, and mash.
Add the chopped onion and corned beef.
Spoon potato mixture into the lined dish.
Roll out the other half of the pastry mixture.
Lay it over the dish sealing at the edges, forming a lid to the pie.
Cut some slits in the top of the lid. Brush with a little milk.
Cook until golden brown (about 35–40 minutes).
Serve with vegetables, gravy, chips, peeled plum tomatoes, waffles, anything you like really.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Ed Bierman / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Corned_beef_pie.jpg

recipes.title: Cornmeal-Crusted Walleye
recipes.description: Freshly caught walleye fillets dredged in cornmeal and pan-fried, a lake-country favorite among the Ojibwe and other Great Lakes nations.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Soak the walleye fillets in the milk for 10 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, salt, pepper, and paprika in a shallow dish.
Lift each fillet from the milk, let the excess drip off, and press it into the cornmeal mixture to coat both sides.
Heat the oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the fillets for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and the fish flakes easily.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve with lemon wedges and wild rice.

recipes.photoCredit: Thérèse Ottawa / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Okacic_saso.jpg

recipes.title: Coronation Chicken
recipes.description: Coronation chicken was apparently created by Florist Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume for the banquet of the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II in 1953—see Wikipedia's article on Coronation Chicken for more information. Although prevailingly more recent preparations often prescribe the addition of raisins, with which many will be more familiar, the following recipe is based on the "official" recipe published in 1956:
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 ea. (2.3 kg / 5 lb) chicken, poached (or other cooked chicken)

steps.text: Skin the chicken if needed, and cut it into small pieces. Traditionally the chicken is cooked whole in advance, but alternatively you can use raw chicken and grill the chicken pieces at this point.
In a small saucepan, warm a small amount of vegetable oil.
Add the onion to the pan and cook gently until soft (about 3 minutes).
Add the curry paste, tomato puree, wine, bay leaf and lemon juice. Simmer uncovered for about 10 minutes until well-reduced. Strain and leave to cool.
Purée the chopped apricots in a blender or processor. Beat the cooled sauce into the mayonnaise with the apricot purée.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks, and fold into the mixture.
Season with salt and pepper, and a little lemon juice if necessary.
Fold in the chicken pieces, garnish with watercress, and serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: James F. Carter / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.5 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Coronation_Chicken.jpg

recipes.title: Crab Cakes
recipes.description: This recipe is a modified version of a crab cake recipe found at Chefs.com.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) crabmeat or imitation crabmeat

steps.text: Combine crabmeat, Italian style breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, egg, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl for the cakes.
In a separate bowl, combine remaining ingredients, except the oil, to make the sauce.
Shape crab cake mix into 3-inch (7.5 cm) patties (about 2 per serving) or smaller for appetizer-size.
Add oil to a skillet.
Pan fry the cakes for 3–4 minutes on each side or until golden brown.
Remove from skillet and drain on paper towels.
Serve cakes topped with the sauce.

recipes.title: Crab Dip
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Drain, rinse, and pick over crab meat to remove any bits of shell and cartilage.
Combine all ingredients, blending well.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.

recipes.notes: Serve before dinner with chips and crackers. For color and variety, mixed nuts and colorful vegetables can be laid out. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Crispy Potato Latkes
recipes.description: Golden, lacy potato pancakes fried in oil for Hanukkah, served with applesauce and sour cream.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour or matzo meal
Applesauce and sour cream, for serving

steps.text: Grate the potatoes and onion using the coarse side of a box grater.
Wrap the mixture in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Mix the potatoes and onion with the eggs, flour, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Heat about 1/4 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop heaping tablespoons of the mixture into the oil and flatten them slightly.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a little more salt. Add more oil to the pan between batches as needed.
Serve hot with applesauce and sour cream.

recipes.title: Crock Pot Beef Stew
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 pounds (900 g) stew beef, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
1 whole clove or 1/2 tsp ground cloves

steps.text: Trim all fat from meat.
Put all ingredients in crockpot; mix thoroughly.
Cover and cook on low 12 hours or on high 5 to 6 hours.
Remove bay leaves before serving.

recipes.notes: You can use the cheapest beef in the market; it will get tender in the pot.

recipes.title: Crock Pot Potato Soup
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: In a slow cooker, combine potatoes, onions, water, parsley, celery, salt, pepper, chicken broth and butter.
Cook until done -- on low heat, 9 to 11 hours, or on high heat, 3 to 4 hours.
When done, add milk and reheat.
Serve plain or use an immersion blender/put mixture in blender for a smoother soup.
Reheat if necessary.

recipes.notes: Garnish each serving with a dollop of sour cream and chives, if desired. If you don't have evaporated milk on hand, it's possible to mix 1.5 cups of cold milk with flour to form a thick slurry to mix it in with good results. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Cullen Skink (Haddock and Potato Soup)
recipes.description: Cullen skink is a soup from Cullen in Morayshire using smoked haddock for a rich flavour.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 large (2 lb) smoked haddock, preferably Finny haddock

steps.text: Cover the haddock with water in a shallow pan with skin side down.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes, turning once.
Take the fish from the pan and remove the skin and bones.
Flake the fish and return to the stock.
Add chopped onion, bay leaf, salt and pepper.
Simmer for a further 10 minutes.
Strain the stock and keep it ready. Discard the bay leaf and keep the fish warm.
Add the milk to the fish stock and bring to the boil.
Add mashed potato to make a rich and thick soup.
Add the fish and check the seasoning—add more if needed.
When serving, add the butter in small pieces so it runs through the soup.
Serve with chopped parsley on top, and toast by the side.

recipes.notes: If smoked haddock is unavailable, smoked kippers have been known to serve in its place. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Cumin Lamb Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Xinjiang-style lamb stir-fried with whole and ground cumin, dried chilies, and onions for a bold, smoky dish.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless lamb shoulder or leg, thinly sliced

steps.text: Toss the lamb with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat until it just begins to smoke.
Add the lamb in a single layer, sear for 1 minute, then stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until browned; remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the cumin seeds, ground cumin, red pepper flakes, dried chilies, and Sichuan pepper and stir-fry for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the onion is just softened.
Return the lamb to the wok, sprinkle with salt and sugar, and toss for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, toss in the cilantro, and serve with rice or flatbread.

recipes.title: Currywurst
recipes.description: Berlin's iconic street food: sliced fried sausage drenched in a sweet, tangy curry-ketchup sauce and dusted with curry powder.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 tsp curry powder, plus more for sprinkling

steps.text: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and paprika and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ketchup, tomato sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire, honey and water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with an immersion blender if you like and keep it warm.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the sausages for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and heated through.
Slice the sausages into thick coins, pour the warm sauce over them and dust with more curry powder.
Serve with French fries or a crusty roll.

recipes.photoCredit: Ziko van Dijk / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:20220430_currywurst.jpg

recipes.title: Daifuku (Sweet Filled Mochi)
recipes.description: Daifukumochi (大福餅), or Daifuku (大福) (literally "great luck"), is a Japanese confection consisting of a small round mochi (glutinous rice cake) stuffed with sweet filling, most commonly anko, sweetened red bean paste made from azuki beans.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Prepare anko filling as directed. Shape into 12 small, marble-sized balls and set aside.
Prepare a smooth surface, such as a cutting board, by coating with potato starch; be generous, as the dough will be very sticky.

Heat water and sugar together in a microwave until sugar is dissolved. Add rice flour and stir completely. Microwave for 2 minutes, remove and stir. Microwave for 2 more minutes, or until dough begins to expand. Remove from microwave, stir again, and remove the dough to the potato starch-coated surface. The dough, called mochi, will be very hot.
Spread or roll the mochi dough out until thin. Using a knife, cut into 12 even sized pieces.
Coat the palms and fingers of your hands in potato starch. Spread each piece out as thin as possible.
Place an anko ball in the middle of each mochi piece, then wrap the mochi around the ball, forming a bigger ball.
Roll shaped daifuku in potato starch, and set on a plate dusted with potato starch or a piece of wax paper.
Serve warm or cool. Store in an airtight container. Very perishable.

recipes.notes: Chocolate ganache may be substituted for anko paste. Food coloring may be added to the water before the rice flour is mixed in. Cocoa powder may be used instead of potato starch in the final step. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Daigakuimo (Japanese Candied Sweet Potato)
recipes.description: Daigakuimo (Japanese: 大学芋) is a dish of Japanese candied sweet potato.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Cut sweet potatoes into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the oil and fry the sweet potatoes at 350°F (175°C) until brown.
Mix water, sugar, and soy sauce in a saucepan. Put the pan on low heat.
When the liquid turns sticky, remove from the heat and add fried sweet potatoes. Quickly mix the potatoes with the sticky sugar.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over the coated sweet potatoes.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Dal Makhani (Black Gram with Cream)
recipes.description: Dal makhani is a delicacy from Punjab, India. Traditionally this dal was cooked slowly, for hours, on charcoal. This gave it a creamy texture. It had ‘malai’ (cream) or fresh butter added to it. When cooked at home these days, more moderate amounts of cream or butter are used. When prepared in restaurants, it is cooked slowly on low heat and often has a large amount of cream and butter added.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 cup whole dried urad dal (skinless black gram)

steps.text: Wash and soak black urad dal and red kidney beans overnight in an adequate amount of lukewarm water.
Cook the soaked dal, kidney beans, and chickpeas in 5–6 cups of water with the salt, red chili powder, turmeric, and grated ginger until soft.
Keep the cooked dal aside.

Heat oil or butter in a thick bottomed pan. Add hing, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, and chopped onions and cook until light golden brown in color. When the onion turns brown, add ginger garlic paste, and sauté.
Add chopped tomatoes. Sauté and add coriander powder. Sauté until tomatoes are well mashed.
Add cooked dal and water as needed.
Mix it well and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Add fresh cream and clarified butter, and let it simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Garnish with coriander leaves before serving.
Serve hot with naan, paratha or rice.

recipes.notes: You can substitute cream with sour cream or low-fat yogurt. Use olive oil instead of ghee or butter, and omit cream. You can make this recipe in a slow cooker, but make sure that you boil it briskly in a pan for the last 10 minutes, to neutralise the toxins in kidney beans. This dal generally requires more salt than usual for other dal, so it should be added as per taste. Soaking the beans overnight reduces cooking time. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Dampfnudeln (Steamed Yeast Dumplings)
recipes.description: Fluffy yeast buns steamed in a covered pan with milk and butter until they form a golden caramel crust on the bottom, served with vanilla sauce.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm milk, egg and butter, and knead for 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape them into smooth balls, cover and let rise for 20 minutes.
In a wide heavy pan with a tight-fitting glass lid, heat the milk, butter and sugar until the butter melts.
Place the dough balls in the pan, cover tightly, and cook over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes without lifting the lid, until the liquid is absorbed and you hear crackling.
Meanwhile, whisk 1/2 cup milk with the cornstarch and yolks, heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the cornstarch mixture and cook until thickened, then add the vanilla.
Remove the lid, loosen the dumplings and serve them caramel side up with the warm vanilla sauce or stewed plums.

recipes.photoCredit: Oliver s. at German Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CDampfnudelnWP6.jpg

recipes.title: Dan Dan Noodles
recipes.description: Sichuan street noodles topped with crispy seasoned pork and a spicy, nutty sesame and chili oil sauce.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped Sichuan preserved vegetable (ya cai), optional
3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste or tahini

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the pork for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and slightly crispy.
Add the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and preserved vegetable and cook for 1 minute more, then set aside.
Whisk the sesame paste, soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, chili oil, Sichuan pepper, and garlic together in a bowl.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch the bok choy for 1 minute, then remove.
Cook the noodles in the same water according to the package until just tender, reserving 1/4 cup of the cooking water.
Thin the sauce with the hot noodle water and divide it among four bowls.
Add the drained noodles and bok choy to the bowls and top with the pork, green onions, and peanuts.
Toss everything together at the table before eating.

recipes.photoCredit: Steven G. Johnson / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dan-dan_noodles,_Shanghai.jpg

recipes.title: Dashi (Japanese Soup Stock)
recipes.description: Dashi is a traditional Japanese broth that forms the foundation of many Japanese dishes. It is made by extracting umami compounds from ingredients such as kelp (kombu), bonito flakes (katsuobushi), and dried sardines (niboshi). Dashi adds depth and subtle flavor to soups, stews, and simmered dishes.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Granulated or powdered instant dashi (optional for quick preparation)

steps.text: Kombu dashi: Wipe kombu gently with a damp cloth (do not wash under running water).
Soak the kombu in water for about 30 minutes.
Heat slowly and remove kombu just before the water boils.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, then strain.
Katsuobushi dashi: Lightly rinse bonito flakes.
Bring water to a boil, add flakes, and simmer for about 1 minute.
Remove from heat; once the flakes sink, strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth.
Niboshi dashi: Remove heads and guts from sardines or anchovies.
Place in a pot with water and bring to a boil.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, then strain.
Awase dashi: Prepare both kombu and katsuobushi dashi separately.
Combine in desired proportions for a richer flavor.
Instant or Granulated Dashi: Dissolve the desired amount of granulated or powdered dashi in hot water according to package instructions.
Adjust seasoning as needed for taste.

recipes.notes: Both kombu and fish flakes are available in most Asian supermarkets or online. Katsuobushi is often sold in small single-serving packets or mesh bags for easy removal. An 80 g bag yields roughly 4 L of stock. Instant dashi provides convenience but may be saltier than homemade stock. Adjust seasoning accordingly. Homemade dashi results in a richer, more complex flavor than most instant varieties. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Sakurai Midori / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Katsuobushi_02.jpg

recipes.title: Date Bars
recipes.description: Date bars have crumbly upper and lower surfaces with a date filling in the middle. Also see the Date Squares recipe.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Mix the dates, sugar, and water in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly for about 10 minutes or until thickened. Cool.
Cream together the butter, shortening, and brown sugar in a separate container.
Mix the flour, salt, baking soda, and oats into the crumble crust mix.
Grease a 13x9-inch pan.
Evenly press half of the crumble mixture into the bottom of the pan.
Spread the date filling on top.
Evenly place remaining crumble mixture into the pan, pressing lightly.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 400°F, or until light brown.
Cut into bars while still warm.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CookbookDatebar.jpg

recipes.title: Deep Dish Pizza
recipes.description: Pizza is a traditional Italian fare that was introduced by immigrants to America in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. In America it has evolved to unique variations, including this Deep Dish Pizza variety. What makes this pizza special is the thicker raised crust which is baked with the pizza. The pizza itself is filled with sauce, cheese, and other ingredients.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 tsp active dry yeast (fast-rising yeast is acceptable)
1 or more (170–225 g) can(s) of prepared or homemade pizza sauce

steps.text: Crust: In a mixing bowl or dough mixer, mix the yeast and 3/4 cup (185 ml) warm water. Let this stand for a few minutes to activate the yeast.

Mix in the 1 cup (140 g) flour, oil, sugar, salt into a smooth batter. Add the remaining flour and water. Mix this until you get a dough with a slightly sticky consistency. Add additional water or flour to adjust the consistency. Knead the dough until it springs slightly when touched.
Let this rise in a warm location in a greased bowl until doubled. Punch down the dough in the bowl.

Transfer dough to a floured flat surface. Roll or shape the dough to the shape of a pizza pan and make an edge up the side of the pan for the crust. Roll the dough thicker for Deep Dish Pizza and thinner for a crisper and more traditional pizza crust.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Spread the pizza sauce on the dough, leaving the edge crust uncoated. Add any optional toppings (pepperoni, sausage, green pepper, etc.). Sprinkle the grated mozzarella cheese evenly across the pizza, leaving the edge crust untouched. If desired, sprinkle the grated Parmesan and Romano cheeses evenly over the toppings.

Bake the pizza on a rack of the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes or until the crust and cheese are lightly brown. If the pizza is browning on the outer crust and not in the middle, line the edge with aluminum foil to prevent burning. This rarely happens except on larger diameter pizzas of 40 cm or more.
When removing from the oven, cut into about 8 triangular, pie shaped slices for serving. A pizza cutter with a circular wheel does this nicely.

recipes.notes: A black pan will cook the crust faster and crisper than a light pan. Use a heated baking stone. This is a flat stone which sit in the oven and preheats to the oven temperature. It accelerates the baking and makes the crust more consistently brown. Decrease the baking time by removing the pizza when the crust and cheese center is light brown. Use a professional pizza oven or wood fired stone hearth. This is generally a professional pizza kitchen option. Cornmeal may be used to flour the pan. It provides a unique characteristic to the crust and dries it a bit. It may omitted, or substituted with flour. The olive oil may be substituted by vegetable oil or butter for a different crust characteristic or for oiling the pan. Olive oil makes an Italian bread type of raised crust. If the crust is left to rise 15–30 minutes before it is baked, it will be thicker and more like an Italian bread crus (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pepperoni_pizza.jpg

recipes.title: Deep Fried Chickpea Dough Curry Snacks (Pakoda)
recipes.description: Pakoda is a savoury South Indian fried snack made from gram flour, spices and onions. This simple recipe is for Pakoda as made in Tamil Nadu, India. A different version called "pakora" is famous in the other parts of India. The difference is that for making pakora, the batter/mix can be a bit more liquidy like for making pancakes, and different vegetables like spinach or potatoes may be used.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 cup (240 g) besan or gram flour
2 tsp green gram flour (optional, for added crunch)

steps.text: Combine all the dry ingredients except the salt, peanuts, and onions. Mix well.
Add the onions, peanuts, 1 tsp oil, and salt. Mix well, then keep aside for about 10 minutes. The moisture from the onions will ooze out into the batter.

Adding a little bit of water at a time, make a dough that will form chunks but break into pieces with a little bit of pressure. The consistency should be the same as when making scones. Too much water and the pakoda will not be crunchy.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed cooking vessel.
Shape the dough into chunks, and deep-fry them in medium-hot oil until golden-brown and crispy. Too much turmeric might give it a darker color.
Serve hot or room temperature.

recipes.notes: Store at room temperature for about 3–4 days. Avoid refrigerating to maintain the crunchy texture. The pakoda may be served with ketchup or any style of chutney. A tradition during the monsoon season is to serve piping hot tea after pakodas. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Babu iyer / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Onion_pakora_-_a.jpg

recipes.title: Deluxe Burgers
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 6 strips of bacon, cooked well done and crumbled

steps.text: Mix beef, garlic salt, onion, and pepper thoroughly in a bowl.
Shape hamburger mixture into 6 patties, about 3/4-inch thick.
Mix bacon, cheese, mayonnaise, and mushrooms together and store in the refrigerator or cooler.
Cook burgers on the grill, covered, for 5 or 7 minutes on each side.
During the last 3 minutes, put 1/4 cup cheese mixture on top of each burger.

recipes.notes: Serve on buns, if desired. And of course, garnish with lettuce and tomato slices. Have available the usual: ketchup, mustard, and pickle relish. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Denver Omelet
recipes.description: The Denver omelet is a bit like the Spanish omelet, but with different non-egg ingredients.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 8 slices cooked bacon, drained and crumbled
a couple drops of your favorite hot sauce (optional)

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet or on a griddle.
Sauté onion, bell pepper, ham and bacon in the butter until the onion starts to become translucent.
In a small bowl, whip the eggs lightly. Add salt, pepper, and hot sauce if desired.
Slowly stir the eggs into the mixture in the skillet.
Lightly brown on one side.
Flip over and lightly brown other side.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Guilhem Vellut from Annecy, France / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gorgonzola_%2B_Bacon_Omelette_@_Omelegg_@_Amsterdam_(16600947041).jpg

recipes.title: Deviled Eggs
recipes.description: Serve these deviled eggs for any occasion, whether it be a wedding feast, a picnic in the park, or for lunch or dinner!
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 6 Large Hard-boiled eggs, halved lengthwise (if not already prepared, add 10-15 mins to prep time.)
3 tbsps of mayonnaise or creamy salad dressing

steps.text: Extract yolks from the halved eggs and place the yolks in a bowl, being careful not to break the whites.
Mash yolks with a fork and mix in the remaining ingredients.
Spoon the mixture back into the egg white halves.
(Optional) Garnish with a light sprinkling of paprika.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Dhokla (Steamed Black Gram Bread)
recipes.description: Dhokla is a Gujarati snack that is made with black gram. It is not to be confused with khaman, a variant made from besan (chickpea flour). It is eaten as a side dish with the main meal and is usually tangy and slightly sweet in taste.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Toast the rice and the dal in a pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes.
Allow it to cool, then grind into a semi-coarse powder. Put the powder in a bowl.
Mix yoghurt and warm water into the powder. Mix thoroughly so that no lumps are formed and the batter is of pouring consistency.
Add salt and let it ferment for 8–10 hours.
Make a paste of ginger and green chillies.
Once fermented, mix the ginger-green chilli paste with the batter.
Grease a dhokla platter, thali, or other dish/tin.
Boil water in the steamer/boiler.
Set half the batter aside.

In a small bowl, combine 1/4 tsp soda bicarbonate, 1/2 tsp oil, and 1/2 tbsp lemon juice. Add this to the batter and mix well. Repeat this for the remaining batter just before putting it in the steamer.
Transfer the risen batter to the greased container, and place in the steamer. Steam for 8–10 minutes. Check by poking with a knife—if the knife comes out clean, it is cooked.
Sprinkle with coriander leaves and serve hot with green chutney.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Dingle Pies
recipes.description: Traditional Kerry hand pies of spiced minced mutton or lamb in hot-water pastry, once made for fair days and Lammas.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder, finely diced or coarsely ground

steps.text: Mix the lamb, onion, carrot, cumin, salt, pepper, and parsley in a bowl and set aside.
For the pastry, mix the flour and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the center.
Heat the water, lard, and butter in a saucepan until the fat melts and the mixture boils.
Pour the hot liquid into the flour and stir quickly to form a dough, then knead briefly until smooth while still warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll out two-thirds of the pastry and cut six 6-inch rounds; roll the remaining pastry and cut six 4-inch rounds for lids.
Spoon the filling onto the large rounds, moisten each with a spoonful of stock, then gather up the edges and top with the lids, pinching firmly to seal.
Cut a small hole in each lid and brush the pies with beaten egg.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until deep golden, pouring a little hot stock through the holes halfway through if the filling looks dry.
Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Dorayaki (Red Bean Pancakes)
recipes.description: Two fluffy honey pancakes sandwiched around sweet red bean paste, a beloved Japanese snack.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar, and honey in a bowl for 2 minutes until pale and slightly fluffy.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and stir just until smooth.
Cover and let the batter rest for 15 minutes, then stir in water a tablespoon at a time until it flows like thick pancake batter.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and wipe it with a little oil, removing the excess with a paper towel.
Pour about 3 tbsp batter into the pan to form a 3 1/2-inch round.
Cook for about 1 1/2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface, then flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Transfer the pancakes to a plate and cover with a damp towel to keep them soft.
Spread about 3 tbsp red bean paste on one pancake, top with a second, and press the edges gently to seal.

recipes.title: Dry Rub
recipes.description: A dry rub useful for ribs, pork roast or whatever you like. After rubbing on the meat, let it sit in the refrigerator for about an hour.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Combine ingredients in a Zip-Lock bag, shaking thoroughly.
Store in airtight container.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Dry Rub Barbecue Ribs
recipes.description: Ribs of various animals are consumed around the world. This recipe will teach you how to make dry rub barbecue ribs.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Combine liquid ingredients and place in a spray bottle. Spray liberally onto one side of ribs.
Coat moistened side of ribs with Rub. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Place applewood in the firebox of a 250°F smoker or the coal area of a 250°F charcoal grill set for indirect heat.
Place ribs in smoker or grill and cook, spraying often with remaining mixture, for 5–6 hours.
Remove and place on a medium-high heat charcoal grill, seasoned side down, spraying constantly until well-browned.
Remove and let rest for 5 minutes and serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Dublin Lawyer
recipes.description: A luxurious Dublin dish of lobster meat flambéed in Irish whiskey and finished in a rich cream sauce.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil, plunge in the lobsters, and cook for 8 minutes.
Transfer the lobsters to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking, then drain.
Split the lobsters in half lengthwise, remove the meat from the tails and claws, and cut it into bite-size chunks; rinse and reserve the half shells.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the shallot for 2 minutes until soft.
Add the lobster meat and toss for 1 minute to warm through.
Pour in the whiskey and carefully ignite it with a long match, letting the flames die down.
Stir in the cream, mustard, lemon juice, salt, and cayenne and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Spoon the lobster and sauce back into the warmed shells, sprinkle with parsley, and serve at once.

recipes.title: East Frisian Tea
recipes.description: Afternoon tea is an important part of East Frisian culture. Whether at home or when visiting friends, East Frisians try not to miss their teetied (Low German for "tea time").
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: >1/2 liter (2 cups) per person of boiling water, soft if possible
2 tablespoons per liter of water of loose black tea leaves, plus 1 more teaspoon "for the pot"
1 piece per person of rock sugar, locally called kluntjes

steps.text: Rinse out the teapot with boiling water to warm it. Pour the water out, then add the tea leaves.
Fill the pot halfway with water that has cooled slightly from the boiling point.
Put the lid on the teapot and allow the tea to steep for 3–4 minutes.
Add the rest of the water.
Place one piece of rock sugar into each cup.
Pour the tea through a strainer into the cups. The rock sugar will start to crackle in the hot liquid.
Using a cream spoon (shaped like a teaspoon-sized ladle) or teaspoon, gently lower a spoonful of cream into the tea so that it forms a "cloud". Do not stir the tea.

recipes.notes: A strong black variety of tea such as Assam or Ceylon should be used. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Eastern North Carolina Barbecue Sauce
recipes.description: This recipe is initially from the original contributor's friend and brother, Chip Crumpler.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Start with apple cider vinegar in saucepan over medium heat.
Add salt, ground black pepper, crushed red pepper, molasses, and honey.
Let mixture heat up, but not quite boil.
Mix well.
Return sauce to the jug that the vinegar came in to cool.

recipes.notes: This is the sauce used for authentic barbecue. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
