Pour in the broth, add the bay leaf, marjoram, salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Remove the bay leaf and mash or blend about half of the soup to thicken it, leaving some chunks.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg and sliced wieners and heat for 5 minutes until the sausages are hot.
Adjust the seasoning and serve sprinkled with parsley and with dark bread on the side.

recipes.title: Kashmiri Pulao
recipes.description: This very fancy Kashmiri pulao, or Kashmiri Pallao, is from the Northern Indian state of Kashmir. Although it is a frozen region high in the Himalayas, Kashmir lies along the ancient overland trade routes between India and Central Asia, and the cuisine is famous for using a huge assortment of nuts and dried fruits from all over Central and Western Asia.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 cinnamon tree leaf (or substitute 2 bay leaves)
1/2 kilogram basmati or other long-grained rice, cooked and drained
100 grams dried dates, pitted and sliced thin

steps.text: Heat ghee or butter in a large wide pan or wok.
Add the cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon tree leaf.
Add the chopped onion, and fry until it just begins to turn brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chillies and fry for about 1 minute before tossing in all of the dried fruits and nuts.
Add salt to taste.
Turn the flame down to low.
Soak the strands of saffron in milk, mixing until the milk turns orange.
Pour the cooked rice into the pan and sprinkle the saffron-milk on top.
Stir very carefully so as not to break or mash up the rice grains, mixing the flavourings and saffron colour in uniformly and heating the rice.
Mix in dried fruits and nuts.
Add more ghee according to your preference.
Serve with a gravy such as the basic tomato gravy.

recipes.notes: Try adding paneer fried in ghee to the pulao. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Kedgeree (Rice and Smoked Fish)
recipes.description: Kedgeree (or occasionally kitcherie, kitchari or kitchiri) is a dish consisting of flaked fish (usually smoked haddock), boiled rice, eggs and butter. It originated amongst the British colonials in India hence was introduced to the United Kingdom as a popular English breakfast in Victorian times, part of the then-fashionable Anglo-Indian cuisine.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1–2 cups Basmati or long-grain white rice (see notes)
2–4 cups decent quality low-sodium chicken stock
3 medium shallots or 1 medium onion, chopped fairly fine
As much garlic as you can handle, minced or put through a garlic press
6 hard boiled eggs, chopped fairly fine
At least 3 tsp of prepared English mustard (1 1/2 tsp of dry mustard)
Enough finely-chopped parsley or cilantro to add interest and colour

steps.text: Cook the rice in one and a half the amount of chicken stock with the bay leaf. When it is done and keeping warm, discard the bay leaf, fluff the rice with chopsticks, and place the raw smoked haddock slab on top. Close the lid and let the haddock steam on warm for 15 minutes.
Remove the haddock, and flake with forks to get rid of every last trace of bone. Place the haddock back with the rice.
Sauté the shallots in excess butter until light brown. Add the garlic, and cook for 1 minute more, making sure to not brown it. Transfer mixture to the rice.

Add the eggs, mustard, parsley, pepper, curry powder, and enough cream to make everything just slightly creamy. Mix it all up, gently and thoroughly (chopsticks are perfect for this). Season with salt to taste.
Serve immediately or later—it keeps well.

recipes.notes: A rice cooker is not essential, but makes the whole thing brainless. 1 cup of rice will yield a dish that is dense with egg and haddock; 2 cups will give you a dish with a more Asian proportion of rice. The addition of 3–4 cloves and a few cardamom seeds to the rice whilst it is cooking, plus the addition of a level teaspoon of cumin powder to the finished product, gives the rice a wonderful aroma. Leftovers may be served in kedgeree omelettes with a dribble of soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce. Haddock is traditional. Smoked anything can substitute it. Cartoned organic stock is much superior, but home-made still beats all comers. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Keralan Vegetable Stew
recipes.description: This coconut-flavoured vegetable stew is a famous dish of the South Indian coastal state of Kerala. It is often served with appam (rice pancakes). Though frequently made with chicken, this recipe is for the purely vegetable version of the stew.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups boiled vegetables (carrots, green beans, potatoes, peas, etc.)
1 very small piece of ginger, chopped
1 Tbsp flour or rice flour or cornstarch

steps.text: Pour 3/4 cup of water into the grated coconut. Squeeze out the milk through a strainer. Set aside; this is first milk.
Pour 1/2 cup of water into the same coconut and squeeze out the second milk. Keep this aside as well.
In a large pan, heat oil and add the cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Add the chopped onion, ginger, chillies and curry leaves. Fry until the onion is slightly browned.
Add the boiled vegetables and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the second milk and boil for about 5–7 minutes.
Add salt. Dissolve the maida/rice flour in a little water and add it to the sauce.
When it boils again, add the first milk.
Remove from the flame when it starts to boil once more.
Season with the pepper, mustard, and shallot.

recipes.notes: You can use cornflour instead of rice/maida flour to thicken the sauce. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Key Lime Meringue Pie
recipes.description: Key lime pie is made of Key lime juice, eggs, condensed milk, and sugar in a pre-baked pie shell. The pie is then baked, and often topped with meringue or whipped cream. Other recipes (with slightly different ingredients) call for it to be chilled or frozen, using an unbaked Graham cracker crust. This makes it a popular summer dessert.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 fully-baked 9-inch (25 cm / 9 oz) graham cracker or pastry pie shell
1 can (14 oz / 400 g) sweetened condensed milk

steps.text: Separate egg whites from egg yolks. Make sure there is no trace of yolk in the whites.
Beat the sweetened condensed milk, lime juice, and egg yolks in a small mixing bowl.
Pour the mixture into the baked pie shell. Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 8 minutes.
While baking filling, whip egg whites in a large, clean mixer bowl on high speed until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in the sugar until meringue forms hard peaks.
Spoon the meringue over the top of the hot pie and use a spoon to form peaks.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 10–15 minutes, or until meringue begins to brown.

recipes.photoCredit: Peter Veldhuizen / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Key_limepie.jpg

recipes.title: Khara Pongal (Rice and Mung Bean Porridge)
recipes.description: Khara pongal is a savoury porridge-like dish that is traditionally prepared in South India for the Makar Sankranti festival that heralds the arrival of summer. The sweet pongal variety differs only in the spices added, and the two are often cooked together from the same batch of rice and dhal.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Cook the rice and dhal together with turmeric powder in a pot or pressure cooker until mushy.
Heat a little ghee in a large pan and brown the cashew nuts. Remove them from the pan.
Add the rest of the ghee and the oil and heat.
Throw in all of the spices, starting with the mustard seed and finishing with the cashew nuts.
Mix in the rice and dhal, warming through. If it is too thick, add a little water.
Add salt and extra ghee to taste. You can also add some grated coconut at the end.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Thamizhpparithi Maari / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aesthetic_Ven_Pongal.jpg

recipes.title: Kheer (Rice Pudding)
recipes.description: Kheer or payasam is a thick rice pudding.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 250 ml (1 cup) long grain white rice

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil. Stir regularly to prevent scorching.
Add rice and simmer slowly until thick (about 20 minutes).
Stir in the sugar, sultanas, and the ground cardamom seeds. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the almonds and rosewater, and cover until ready to serve.

recipes.notes: You can leave the kheer boiling for much longer (several hours), until it has been significantly reduced; this provides a stronger flavour and a light-pink colour. You can use rice flour or vermicelli instead of plain rice. You can add some red soda to give it a nice pinkish-whitish colour. For kheer that is not too thick when cold, use 170 ml (2/3 cup) of rice instead of the amount listed above. If to be eaten cold, it's nicer to use double the quantities of sugar, sultanas, and almonds. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: stu spivack / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kheer.jpg

recipes.title: Killer Queso Dip
recipes.description: Queso (literally "cheese" in Spanish), also known as chile con queso, is a common dip found in southwestern and Tex-Mex cooking.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 10 oz (280 g) canned tomatoes stewed with green chiles (e.g. Rotel brand)
Tortilla chips or fritos for serving

steps.text: Saucepan method: Brown sausage in saucepan and drain grease.
Add cubed cheese, diced tomatoes, and diced chilies.
Heat over low, stirring until cheese is melted and ingredients are well blended.
Slow cooker method: Brown sausage in a skillet and drain grease.
In a slow cooker, melt cheese with tomatoes and chilies, stirring.
Add browned sausage. Stir until well melted and mixed.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Wackyrussell at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chili_con_queso_(cropped).jpg

recipes.title: Kitsune Udon
recipes.description: Thick udon noodles in a light dashi broth topped with sweet simmered fried tofu pouches.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Pour boiling water over the aburaage to remove excess oil, then drain and squeeze gently.
Simmer the aburaage with 1/2 cup dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan over low heat for 10 minutes, turning once, until most of the liquid is absorbed.
In a separate pot, bring the 3 cups dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt to a simmer.
Cook the udon in a large pot of boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes until heated through and loosened, then drain.
Divide the noodles between two large bowls and ladle the hot broth over them.
Top each bowl with two pieces of simmered aburaage, kamaboko if using, and green onions.
Serve immediately.

recipes.photoCredit: 加茂川の民 / Wikimedia Commons, CC0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E9%B6%8F%E5%A4%A9%E3%81%AE%E3%81%86%E3%81%A9%E3%82%93.jpg

recipes.title: Kneel-Down Bread
recipes.description: Fresh sweet corn ground into a moist batter, wrapped in its own husks, and baked—named by the Diné (Navajo) for kneeling to grind corn on a metate.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 8 ears fresh sweet corn in husks

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) or prepare a bed of hot coals.
Carefully remove the husks from the corn, keeping the large inner husks whole, and set them aside.
Cut the kernels from the cobs and scrape the cobs with the back of the knife to collect the milk.
Grind the kernels in a food processor or meat grinder to a thick, wet batter, then stir in the salt and sugar.
Overlap two husks, spoon 1/3 cup of batter into the center, and fold the husks around it into a packet; tie with a strip of husk.
Arrange the packets seam side down in a baking dish.
Bake for 60–75 minutes until firm, or bury in hot coals and ashes for about 1 hour.
Let cool slightly, then unwrap and serve warm.

recipes.title: Kulfi (South Asian Frozen Custard)
recipes.description: Kulfi or qulfi is a popular Indian frozen dessert similar to ice cream but denser and creamier.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Put the milk into a wide, heavy pan, and bring to boil over high heat, stirring constantly.
Lower the heat and cook the milk, stirring constantly until it has thickened and reduced to 3/4 cup—this will take about 40–45 minutes. Stir the sides of the pan constantly to avoid scorching.
Stir in the sugar, nuts, and cardamom powder. Set aside to cool.
Pour the mixture evenly into kulfi moulds or small ramekins. Cover with plastic wrap or foil, and freeze for about 6 hours until set.
To serve, run a sharp knife dipped in hot water along the sides of the moulds, and unmold them onto a serving plate.

recipes.notes: Kulfi can be prepared in many different flavours. This can be done by substituting the ingredients (with the exception of milk and sugar) with rose flavouring or fruits (mango, strawberry, banana, or other tropical fruits). The amount of sugar can also be altered to suit your taste. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.description: Kung pao chicken (gong bao in Mandarin) is a spicy Sichuan recipe made with diced chicken, chili peppers and peanuts, named after a court official. It is a popular dish served at Chinese restaurants throughout the United States and the UK.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 green bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch dice
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch dice
1 can (5 oz) sliced bamboo shoots (optional), drained
4 green onions, cut into 1/2-inch pieces, including green tops

steps.text: Measure and prepare all ingredients before cooking.
Mix all chicken/marinade ingredients in a bowl, stir well, and allow to marinate for 1/2 hour.
Mix sauce ingredients in another bowl and set aside until needed. Stir out any lumps.
Heat wok or large frying pan until water drops bead up and dance on the hot surface.
Add cooking oil to wok. Wait a few seconds for oil to heat up.
Add remaining spice ingredients to wok and stir fry for 30 seconds.
Add chicken mixture to wok and stir fry for about 4 minutes (until chicken is cooked through).
Add vegetables to wok and stir fry for about 2–3 minutes.
Stir sauce and add to wok. After the sauce comes to a boil, cook for about 1 minute (until sauce thickens).
Stir to coat other ingredients with thickened sauce.
Pour onto large platter and serve immediately.

recipes.notes: Serve with steamed or fried rice.
recipes.photoCredit: Steven G. Johnson / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kung-pao-shanghai.jpg

recipes.title: Käsekuchen (German Cheesecake)
recipes.description: A light, tangy German cheesecake made with quark on a simple shortcrust base, less dense than the American style.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 lb quark (or 1 1/2 lb whole-milk ricotta plus 8 oz cream cheese, blended smooth)

steps.text: Rub the flour, sugar, salt and butter together until crumbly, then mix in the egg yolk and knead briefly into a dough.
Press the dough into the bottom and 1 1/2 inches up the sides of a greased 9-inch springform pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Beat the quark, sugar, egg yolks, melted butter, sour cream, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest and vanilla until smooth.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the cheese mixture.
Pour the filling into the crust and smooth the top.
Bake for 65 to 75 minutes until the top is golden and the center is just set, covering loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
Turn off the oven, prop the door open and let the cake cool inside for 1 hour to prevent cracking, then chill for at least 4 hours before slicing.

recipes.title: Käsespätzle (Cheese Spaetzle)
recipes.description: Swabian and Allgäu comfort food: homemade egg spaetzle layered with melted mountain cheese and topped with crisp fried onions.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/2 cup water or milk, as needed

steps.text: Whisk the flour, salt and nutmeg in a bowl, then beat in the eggs and enough water to make a thick, sticky batter, and beat with a wooden spoon until bubbles form; let rest 10 minutes.
Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onions slowly, stirring often, for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a baking dish.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and press the batter through a spaetzle maker or the holes of a colander into the water in batches.
When the spaetzle float to the surface (1 to 2 minutes), lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain well.
Layer one third of the hot spaetzle in the baking dish, sprinkle with one third of the cheese and some pepper, and repeat twice.
Dot with the remaining butter and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with the fried onions and chives and serve immediately with a green salad.

recipes.title: Königsberger Klopse (Meatballs in Caper Sauce)
recipes.description: Tender poached veal and pork meatballs in a creamy white sauce sharpened with capers and lemon, a beloved dish from old East Prussia.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 stale white roll or 2 slices white bread

steps.text: Soak the bread in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl.
Add the ground meats, chopped onion, egg, anchovies, salt and pepper and mix well.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 12 to 16 meatballs about 2 inches across.
Bring the water to a boil with the bay leaf, halved onion and 1 teaspoon salt, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Add the meatballs and poach for 15 minutes, then remove them with a slotted spoon and strain and reserve 3 cups of the broth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the reserved broth and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, capers, lemon juice and sugar, then remove from the heat and whisk a little sauce into the egg yolk before stirring it back in.
Return the meatballs to the sauce to warm through without boiling, then season to taste.
Serve with boiled potatoes and pickled beets.

recipes.photoCredit: Rainer Zenz at German Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Koenigsberger.jpg

recipes.title: Lancashire Hotpot
recipes.description: Lancashire hotpot, originating from England, is a very easy but delicious baked dish consisting of lamb, onions, potatoes, and herbs.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 lb (900 g) neck of lamb or mutton
1 large or 2 small white onions, diced

steps.text: Dice the lamb and set aside. Preheat oven to 325°F / 170°C / Gas mark 3.
Add a layer of the potatoes to the bottom of a casserole dish, and cover with a handful of the diced onion. Layer the diced lamb on top of this, sprinkling with the herbs.
Repeat these layers until the dish is full. Top with a final layer of the potatoes.
Pour boiling water into the dish until filled—if more water is needed, continue to add until topped.
Bake for at least 1 hour, though traditionally the dish was left baking all day. Mutton will require a longer cooking time.

recipes.notes: A handful of mixed vegetables such as parsnips, turnips, leek or carrots can be added to the dish. It is worth experimenting to find out what combination of flavours you prefer. The dish has occasionally been known to be cooked with oysters or with small birds such as snipe, when they were available. Flavour can be improved by adding a stock cube or instant gravy granules to the boiling water. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Mike Fleming / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lancashire_Hotpot_square.jpg

recipes.title: Lancashire Parkin
recipes.description: Lancashire parkin is a traditional cake eaten onFifth of November in parts of Greater Manchester. Like many gingerbreads, it is baked into a hard slab. It then softens due to the hygroscopic properties of golden syrup.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 220 g (1 cup or 8 oz) caster sugar
440 g (2 cups / 16 oz / 1 lb) tin golden syrup (Tate & Lyle's brand preferred)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F or gas mark 2).
Warm the tin of golden syrup in a bowl of hot water.
Mix together all the dry ingredients.
Empty the golden syrup into a saucepan, and warm it gently without boiling. You can balance the tin over the pan by using two chopsticks.
Melt the margarine into the syrup.
Use the margarine wrapper to grease a 12-inch square baking tray (an 11x13 inch pan will also work). Line the tin with baking paper.
Mix the hot syrup and fat into the dry ingredients. Stir thoroughly but quickly.
Spread the dough into the baking tray. Put it on the bottom shelf of the preheated oven, and bake for 2 hours.

Remove from oven, and turn the slab out from the tray onto a cooling grid. After an hour, cut into four, and store in a sealed tin for 48 hours to reach correct consistency. It can be eaten while warm, but it is better if it is stored at least overnight.
Cut into long strips, getting between 8 and 12 slices from each quarter.

recipes.photoCredit: Clem Rutter, Rochester, Kent / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lancashire_Parkin_5022.JPG

recipes.title: Lemon Curd
recipes.description: Lemon curd is a custard-like dessert sauce made with eggs, lemon juice and zest, sugar, and butter. It keeps for up to a week in the refrigerator, and it is excellent on shortbread, biscuits, scones, and English muffins. It can also be used in a variety of other dessert preparations.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 pinch salt (optional, to bring out sweetness and flavor of finished product)

steps.text: Cut the butter into small chunks.
Put eggs, zest, sugar, and salt into saucepan.
Whisk ingredients in pan until frothy and light in color (1–2 minutes).
Add lemon juice and whisk for 30 seconds.
Add butter chunks.
Set pan on stove burner, turn on heat to medium-to-low, and start whisking contents so they don't coagulate or stick to bottom of pan.
Whisk constantly until butter melts and mixture thickens, then whisk another two minutes. Do not let mixture boil. It should be quite steamy (about 185°F / 85°C).
If desired, pour the mixture through the strainer to remove the zest and any other solids. Work the mixture through the strainer with the spatula; rake mixture off bottom of strainer into bowl.
Pour mixture from bowl into jar to within 1/4 inch (0.75 cm) from top, taking care not to get mixture on rim, then seal jar with lid.
Refrigerate to thicken the product further. Store in the refrigerator.

recipes.notes: Grate only the yellow lemon zest, avoiding the bitter inner white pith. The curd can also be stored in any other suitable container. Livre de cuisine/Crème de citron (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Lemonade
recipes.description: Lemonade is a sweetened beverage made from lemons, sugar, and water. It is popular in the United States during the spring and summer, when it is generally served chilled with ice. In some countries, the word 'lemonade' is also used to describe any clear carbonated drink; in others, it means any fruit-flavored soda.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 cup (250 ml/8.5 oz) fresh lemon juice
3/4–1 cup (160–225 g/5.6–7.9 oz) white or turbinado sugar

steps.text: Combine the lemon juice and sugar in a pitcher or jug. Stir until the sugar is dissolved.
Stir in the water.
Chill and/or serve over ice.

recipes.notes: Using turbinado sugar will result in a golden-brown color and mild caramel flavor. Because sugar dissolves easier in warm liquid, you may want to heat some of the water and dissolve the sugar in it before combining with the remaining ingredients. Hard lemonade incorporates an alcoholic spirit, such as tequila, gin, or vodka to the lemonade. Various fruits, such as strawberries and raspberries can be added for color and flavor. A small amount of beet juice results in pink lemonade with little change in flavor. Herbs such as mint, borage, lavender, and lemon verbena can change the aroma of the drink. Including the lemon peels, bruised and sliced, gives more bite and a stronger aroma. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Lentil and Sausage Stew
recipes.description: This lentil and sausage stew is intended for eating with spätzle. It is a slightly modified recipe; the traditional one has no tomato and honey. But, as with many "national meals," there are different opinions. Try different variations until you get your own taste for it; the most important things for a traditional taste are the vinegar and the bay leaves.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 litre water for the lentils (needed for the sauce; don't use more)
2 pairs of scalded sausage, whole or in pieces
1 large piece of smoked pork belly

steps.text: Lentils: Wash the lentils in sieve and cook them over low heat in the 1 litre of water for 40–50 minutes.
About 20 minutes before the end of the cooking, add the carrot, onion, potatoes, garlic, sausages, bay leaf, and pork belly.
After cooking, put the pot on the side and keep it warm.
Roux: Melt the butter in the little pot, add the flour, and cook carefully until brown, stirring the whole time.
Slowly and gradually add the 1/3 litre water, and bring to a boil.
Add the tomato paste, vinegar, and honey. Season with salt and pepper to your liking.
Stir the sauce into the lentils, mix well, and keep warm.

recipes.notes: Perhaps at first you will think, "how can vinegar go in this stew?"; you will be surprised how well it fits, so don't be shy with it. You can also serve additional vinegar along with the meal. Before eating, pick out the bay leaves. Like many stews, lentil stew should be re-heated and tastes better the next day. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: K. Jähne, cooking by B. Gross, Merops image editing / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Linsen_Spaetzle_2.jpg

recipes.title: Lion's Head Meatballs
recipes.description: Large, tender pork meatballs braised with napa cabbage in a light soy broth, a classic Shanghai family dish.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 lb napa cabbage, cut into large pieces

steps.text: Combine the pork, water chestnuts, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, salt, white pepper, egg, and cornstarch.
Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture is sticky and springy.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 4 to 6 large meatballs, slapping them between your palms to compact them.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat and brown the meatballs on all sides for 6 to 8 minutes, turning gently; remove them.
Add the cabbage stems to the pot and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Lay the meatballs on the cabbage stems and cover them with the cabbage leaves.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, sugar, and ginger and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer gently for 40 to 45 minutes until the meatballs are very tender and cooked through.
Serve the meatballs in bowls with the cabbage and plenty of broth.

recipes.photoCredit: 三猎 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E7%8B%AE%E5%AD%90%E6%A5%BC%E7%8B%AE%E5%AD%90%E5%A4%B4.jpg

recipes.title: Liverpool Lamb and Vegetable Soup (Scouse)
recipes.description: This is a traditional recipe for Liverpool scouse, also known as "lobscouse". The sauce is not thickened, and it is usual to serve with preserved beetroot or red cabbage and white bread with butter. An even more impoverished variety of this dish is 'blind Scouse', which features no meat.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: A cheap cut of lamb or mutton (such as breast or forequarter)

steps.text: Remove the meat from the bone (if needed), and dice it.
Heat a little oil in a large saucepan. Add the meat, and brown it.
Add the chopped onions, carrots, and water or meat stock, and as many potatoes as possible.
Simmer until everything is cooked.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Radarsmum67 from Liverpool, UK. / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Posh_Scouse_at_Liverpool_Maritime_Museum_-_Flickr_-_Radarsmum67.jpg

recipes.title: Low Country Shrimp and Grits
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 3–4 strips thick smoky bacon, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 lb large shrimp, peeled (use peels to make stock)
1 recipe coarse grain hominy grits, timed to finish when shrimp are ready to serve

steps.text: Fry bacon in a pan until not too crisp; remove and reserve.
Sauté onion and garlic in bacon fat until just softened (about 2–3 minutes).
Lightly season shrimp with salt and add to the pan; sauté until about half-cooked and just turning pink. Remove and reserve with the bacon.
Deglaze pan with sherry.
Add 1 cup (250 ml) cream, bring to boil, and reduce.
Add 1 cup shrimp stock, bring to a high simmer, and reduce. The liquid should thicken; if necessary, add floured butter at this point (beurre manié).
Season sauce with salt, pepper, chili flakes, cayenne, and paprika
Add bacon and shrimp to the sauce, and cook gently until shrimp are just done.
Add lime juice.
Serve over grits, and garnish with scallions.

recipes.notes: Make the shrimp stock with shrimp peels and parts, dried shrimp flakes, mirepoix, and peppercorns. The scallions can be replaced with minced chives. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Jason Riedy / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shrimp_and_grits_at_the_Green_Goddess.jpg

recipes.title: Macaroni and Cheese (Baked)
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large pot of boiling, salted water, cook the pasta until it is al dente.
While the pasta is cooking, melt the butter in a separate pot.
Whisk in the flour and mustard and keep it moving for about five minutes. Make sure it is free of lumps.
Stir in the milk, onion, bay leaf, and paprika. Simmer for ten minutes and remove the bay leaf.
Temper in the egg.
Stir in 3/4 of the cheese.
Season with salt and pepper.
Fold the macaroni into the mix and pour into a 2-quart casserole dish.
Top with remaining cheese.
Melt the butter in a sauté pan, add breadcrumbs, and toss to coat.
Top the macaroni with the bread crumbs.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Jason Lam / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Baked_Macaroni_and_Cheese_-_Rocky_%26_Carlo%27s,_Chalmette,_Louisiana.jpg

recipes.title: Machacado con Huevo (Eggs with Shredded Beef)
recipes.description: Machacado con huevo is a dish which consists of shredded dry beef that is scrambled with eggs. Its name means "shredded with eggs" in Spanish. The shredded dry beef, carne seca, is said to have originated in the town of Ciénega de Flores, about an hour north of Monterrey, Mexico. The early settlers in the area air-cured beef so that it would be preserved.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 10 ea. 8-inch soft taco-size flour tortillas, warmed
2 cups (8 ounces) shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack Cheese

steps.text: Heat butter in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add eggs; cook, stirring frequently, for 2–3 minutes or until eggs just begin to set.
Stir in shredded beef filling. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 minutes or until eggs are cooked and beef is heated through.
Serve eggs with tortillas, beans, cheese, and salsa.

recipes.notes: Machacado con huevo can be served in a big bowl, and with some soft tortillas at hand can be prepared in your plate, can be served in the table as tacos, or can be eaten without using tortillas at all. Queso fundido con chorizo (melted cheese with chorizo) is also something that can be found at the table when eating machacado con huevo. It is usually served at the table in a pan, and added to the taco. [[Category:Meat recipes}]] (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Limbo@MX C / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.5 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Machacado_con_huevo.jpg

recipes.title: Madras Filter Coffee
recipes.description: Traditional Madras filter coffee requires the use of specific fresh-roasted coffee beans and chicory roots, which are not always available outside India. This recipe uses Indian instant coffee that has chicory in it, which is available in some Indian stores and supermarkets. Nestle Bru instant coffee has 30% chicory added and in general has a near enough taste to authentic Madras filter coffee.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/2–2 tsp instant coffee with chicory root

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil, and stir in the coffee. Ensure there are no lumps.
Bring the milk to a boil.
Add the coffee mixture to the milk, and sweeten with sugar to taste.

While the coffee is still boiling hot, pour it into a mug or, preferably, a stainless steel tumbler. While pouring the coffee, slowly raise the saucepan so the coffee falls into the mug from a height of about 1–1 1/2 ft. This will cause the coffee to froth like espresso.
If desired, you can dip a teaspoon in the coffee and lightly spread a few drops of it over the froth in the mug.
Serve piping hot.

recipes.notes: Filter coffee in India is actually made in a closed steel container called a coffee filter. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Indian_filter_coffee_in_Dabarah.jpg

recipes.title: Makizushi (Maki Roll)
recipes.description: Makizushi, also called rolled sushi or maki roll, is a variety of sushi. It is made by layering nori, seasoned sushi rice, and fillings, before rolling up and slicing into individual pieces. The outer layer of the maki roll varies, having either nori or rice on the exterior—the latter is sometimes called an inside-out roll.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Fillings, as desired (this may consist of either raw/smoked salmon, tuna, etc or perhaps cucumber or avocado)
Sesame seeds, if making inside-out rolls with rice on outside (optional)

steps.text: Place the roller on a cutting board. If making inside-out rolls with rice on the outside, wrap the roller in a double layer of plastic wrap to prevent rice from sticking to the roller.
Place a sheet of nori shiny side-down on top of the roller.

Dampen your hands before applying the rice. Grab the rice with one hand and put a fistful on the center of the nori. Spread the rice over the nori approximately 6 mm thick, leaving a 2 cm gap on the side parallel to the bamboo. As a general rule, if you can't see the nori through the rice, you have too much.
If making an inside out roll, flip over the nori and rice quickly onto the sushi roller. The rice should now be on on the surface of the plastic wrap, with the nori facing you.

Place the primary ingredients in a row in the middle. Slowly use the roller to push the nori against itself (rolling it away from you), using your thumbs and heels of hands for stability. Be careful when you reach the row of ingredients, making sure that it goes underneath the roll rather than just being pushed along.

When you reach the end of the nori sheet, use the roller to compact the roll a little, making sure the rice sticking it together. When evening out a bumpy roll, don't squeeze too hard on the sides and don't flatten the roll from the top.
To fix the ends of the roll, poke about 1/2 inch out from one side of mat and while gently holding it in place, press it with the heel of your hand a little.
Remove the maki from the sushi roller, and put it on the cutting board below.

Wet a sharp knife before slicing. Slice the rolls from the center outwards, into sections of 5, 6, or 8 (depending on the roll and your preference). Cutting from the center first ensures that all ingredients will shift towards the outside two pieces. For the rolls of 6 or 8, cut from the center, then put one roll behind the other, and cut each half in half.
If making an inside-out roll, you may garnish the exterior rice with sesame seeds.

Serve with soy sauce for dipping. You may also want chopsticks, pickled ginger, and wasabi if culture allows. Sashimi, miso soup, other sushi, or just general Japanese food is also often served alongside it. Green tea is considered the drink of choice to have with sushi.

recipes.notes: Dampening the hands before handling the rice will prevent clumping and the rice sticking to your hands. However, too much moisture may also make the rice less sticky, so don't go overboard. Common maki rolls include: California roll: avocado, crab meat or imitation crab, cucumber. Tuna roll: Tuna, wrapped in rice and seaweed. This same combination is used to make plain rolls with any other type of fish. Spicy tuna roll: Tuna, spicy sauce (mixture of Japanese mayonnaise and sriracha) Kamikaze roll: Tuna, yellowtail, spicy sauce (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Malvani Chicken Curry
recipes.description: Kombdi vade is a Malvani dish, which is quite popular in Maharashtra. The dish consists of the traditional Malvani chicken curry (including chicken pieces with bones), vade (also known as puri, which is a fluffy, fried bread of wheat and nachni flour), onion, lemon and solkadhi (a drink made from coconut milk).
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 800 g (1.8 lb / 8 ea.) medium-sized pieces of chicken

steps.text: Grind half of the green chillies to a paste and mix it well with the ginger and garlic pastes.
Make cuts on the chicken pieces, rub this mixture on to them well, and marinate for about an hour at least.
Toast coconut shavings in a pan with a little hot oil until light brown. Cool and grind along with half the onions to a paste.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and sauté the onions on medium level for about 2 minute(s) or until they are light brown in color.
Add the remaining chopped green chillies and spice powders and fry for a few seconds. Add the marinated chicken pieces and fry on medium level for about 3 minutes or until they are lightly browned.

Add the paste and salt, then mix well. Add water according to the desired level of consistency and bring to a boil. Cover and cook on low level for about 25 minute(s) or until the chicken pieces are tender and fully cooked.
Garnish with finely-chopped coriander leaves.

recipes.notes: If it is difficult to obtain fresh coconut, it can be replaced by desiccated coconut shavings. For this recipe, there is no need to soak it in warm water. Roast it directly. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Mango Avocado Salsa
recipes.description: ​Refreshingly tasty mango avocado salsa is a crowd-pleasing snack or appetizer with tortilla chips.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 small bunch of cilantro, chopped (about 1 cup, packed)
3 Hass avocados, peeled, cored, and diced
1 ripe mango, peeled, cored, and diced (about 1 cup)

steps.text: Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl.
Mix well with a spoon and serve with tortilla chips or use it as toppings for another dish.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Sharon Chen / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mango_Avocado_Salsa.jpg

recipes.title: Mango Chutney (Chunky)
recipes.description: Mango chutney is a specialty chutney of the South Indian coastal state of Andhra Pradesh. Mango chutney can be made in many different ways and can be served with poppadoms or with the main course.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 200 g (1 cup) packed light brown sugar
1 1/2 tbsp fresh ginger, scraped and minced

steps.text: Dissolve the sugar and salt in the vinegar and boil for 15 minutes.
Add mangoes, raisins, and onion and bring to the boil again.
Reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent sticking.
Add the garlic, ginger and seasoning and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and allow to cool before serving.
Due to the high sugar and acid content, this chutney may be refrigerated safely for 6 months.

recipes.notes: Serve with hot rice or bread. This chutney works as an excellent spread on a sandwich. If it is not too spicy, you can serve it as a dip for tortilla chips. You could also serve with yoghurt/curd. This chutney is typically presented in restaurants in a steel dish with a spoon for serving oneself. Vary amount of salt/spices as needed. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Simon Law from Montréal, QC, Canada, modified by User:Mike Hayes 2008.09.05 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mango_Chutney.jpg

recipes.title: Maple Roasted Sunchokes
recipes.description: Sunchokes (Jerusalem artichokes), a native tuber cultivated by Eastern tribes, roasted with sage and maple until crisp outside and creamy inside.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb sunchokes, scrubbed and cut into 1-inch pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the sunchokes with the oil, maple syrup, sage, salt, and pepper.
Spread in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet.
Roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until browned and tender when pierced.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Maple Sugar on Snow
recipes.description: Hot maple syrup boiled to the soft-ball stage and poured over clean snow to make chewy taffy, a sugaring-season treat from the Anishinaabe and Haudenosaunee maple camps.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 6 cups packed clean snow or finely shaved ice

steps.text: Pack the snow firmly into a large shallow pan and keep it in the freezer or outside until needed.
Heat the maple syrup and butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Boil without stirring until the syrup reaches 235°F (113°C) on a candy thermometer, about 10–15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand 1 minute.
Drizzle the hot syrup in thin lines over the snow.
After a few seconds, roll each strand up onto a fork or popsicle stick and eat right away.

recipes.photoCredit: The original uploader was SimonP at English Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Maple_toffee.JPG

recipes.title: Maple Syrup Planked Salmon
recipes.description: Maple syrup planked salmon mixes the hint of sweetness from the maple syrup with the rich smoky flavour imparted from the cedar plank. Using organic ingredients enhances taste.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 4 salmon steaks or individual fillets (preferably wild-caught)
4 tbsp (60 ml) fresh lemon juice, divided
2 tbsp (30 ml) grapeseed oil (or other neutral oil)
1 1/2 tsp (7 g) chipotle powder (chipotle barbecue sauce may be substituted for this)

steps.text: Completely immerse cedar planks in water for several hours or overnight.
Heat grill to medium-high.

Mix 2 tablespoons (30 ml) lemon juice, the oil, rosemary, maple syrup, and half of the chipotle powder in a small bowl. Coat the salmon with the mixture and let rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Mix the remaining lemon juice with the remaining chipotle powder with a fork and set aside as a garnish.
Place plank(s) on grill and close lid. Allow plank to heat for a couple minutes.
Lightly sprinkle salt on plank(s).
Put salmon on plank, keeping fish at least an inch from the edge of the plank (in the case of fillets, place skin-side down). Reduce heat to low and close lid.

Grill for roughly 15 minutes without turning or moving salmon until desired "doneness" is reached. Generally, salmon should be cooked until the flesh loses its transparency and the meat can easily be broken with a fork. Spray with water to douse any flames that light on the sides of the plank.
When cooked, place the salmon on a serving platter and sprinkle with the scallions.
Immerse the cedar plank in water as a safety precaution.
Serve the salmon with the optional lemon juice/chipotle sauce.

recipes.title: Maple-Glazed BBQ Ribs
recipes.description: Maple syrup and pork just sort of seem to be made for each other.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Combine seasonings and rub on pork ribs.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Place hickory chunks into a 350°F (175˚C) smoker or a charcoal grill set for indirect heat at 350°F.
Combine liquid ingredients and bring to a boil over high heat until reduced by half.
Place ribs in smoker/grill and cook, basting often with maple syrup mixture, for 3–4 hours
Brush ribs with remaining mixture and place on a medium high grill until well browned.
Rest 15 minutes; serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Gunawan Kartapranata / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Balinese_Roasted_Pork_Ribs_-_Iga_Babi_Panggang_Bali.JPG

recipes.title: Maple-Roasted Winter Squash
recipes.description: Winter squash roasted with maple syrup and a pinch of salt, honoring the maple sugaring traditions of the Haudenosaunee and Anishinaabe peoples.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 butternut or 2 acorn squash (about 3 lb total)
3 tbsp melted butter or sunflower oil
2 tbsp toasted sunflower or pumpkin seeds

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Halve the squash, scoop out the seeds, and cut it into 1-inch slices or chunks (peel butternut; acorn skin can stay on).
Toss the squash with the butter, maple syrup, salt, and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet.
Spread it in a single layer and roast for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelized at the edges.
Sprinkle with toasted seeds and serve warm.

recipes.title: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Mápó dòufu (麻婆豆腐), also romanized as mapo tofu, is a classic spicy tofu and meat dish from the Szechuan province of China. It is a very flavourful, easy-to-prepare, and spicy dish.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 small piece of ginger, minced (about 2 tsp)
200 g (7 oz) minced beef, or pork
1 tbsp Szechuan pepper, roasted and ground
3–4 green onions, cut into 2 cm (1 inch) pieces

steps.text: If using dried mushrooms, soak them in hot water for 10 minutes while preparing the rest of the ingredients, then slice before adding later.
Sauté onion with ginger and crushed chili.
Add minced meat and garlic, and fry until brown.
Mix in other ingredients (including sliced mushrooms), lower heat, and simmer for 5–10 minutes.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.notes: Some extra chili pepper can be substituted for Szechuan pepper, but the taste and feeling will be different. Szechuan pepper has a numbing sensation, not heat. A little ground coriander and cumin is very nice in this dish, especially if you cannot find Szechuan pepper easily. A red bell pepper, a tomato, and fresh coriander leaves are all welcome additions, though not traditional. The meal is just as good with whole beans instead of tofu. A vegan/vegetarian version of this meal can be made by substituting the meat with textured vegetable protein (TVP) or ground tofu (e.g. Shiok Food's Vegetarian Ma Po Tofu) (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mapo_tofu.JPG

recipes.title: Masala Chai I
recipes.description: Masala chai is a spiced version of the typical Indian milk tea. As with much of Indian cuisine, the exact mix of dry spices varies greatly and is often handed down in families from one generation to the next.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 60 grams whole cinnamon, broken small, or 40 grams ground cinnamon
3/4 teaspoon dried tea leaves—to be traditional, a strong Indian tea such as an Assam is best.

steps.text: Masala: Combine all of the spices, and blend well in an electric grinder.
Store the powder in a clean container at room temperature; you only need a small quantity for each cup of chai, and a full recipe will keep you stocked full of chai for months.
Chai: Boil water and milk together in a saucepan.
Add sugar, tea leaves, and masala. Boil until the mixture becomes dark (about 5–10 minutes); the longer you boil, the stronger the chai.
Strain into teacups to serve.

recipes.notes: Let the remaining solids cool and sprinkle them on your plants for an excellent fertiliser. Tea masala or garam masala from a store can be used to get around the masala mixture process; however, pre-ground spices lose their flavor over time. When making the chai, boil the water and milk separately, and in step two add the tea leaves and masala to the boiling water, boiling until the tea is as strong as you like. Only then add the milk to the mix. This can speed up the process without affecting the flavor. This method is often used by restaurants to serve chai in large quantities quickly as orders are taken. Optionally turn off the heat in the end, cover, and let sit for about 5 minutes for a richer flavor. Try adjusting the ratio of milk to water. For a richer milky tea, try two parts milk to one part water. Leave out the sugar for a more adult flavor. Sugar can be added while drinking i (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Masala_Tea_and_South_Indian_Filter_Coffee.jpg

recipes.title: Masala Dosa
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 cup uncooked ponni or sona masuri rice
3/4 cup dried urad dal (whole skinless black gram)
6 medium sized potatoes, boiled and coarsely mashed

steps.text: 1/2 cup mixture of ghee and vegetable shortening

Batter: On the day before cooking the dosa, grind all the batter ingredients in a blender or specialized dosa grinder with water. The final consistency of the batter must be similar to pancake batter.

Leave batter overnight in a warm spot and allow it to ferment. This is a very important process and must not be skipped. During fermentation the batter may rise to almost twice its volume, and therefore the container for the batter must allow for this.
Filling: Heat the oil in a wok or other deep pan.
When the oil is hot add mustard seeds, and allow them to splutter.

When the spluttering starts to recede, add chopped green chilies, curry leaves, and channa dal. Stir until the channa dal turns brown. Be careful, as channa dal can go from browned to burnt within seconds.
Add onions and fry until browned. Add turmeric and sauté for 2 minutes. Add ginger and garlic and sauté for a few seconds.
Add boiled and coarsely-mashed potatoes to the preparation, and mix well.
Turn off the heat and add lemon juice and coriander leaves, then mix well.
Dosa can easily be made on a tava, iron frying pan, or non-stick pan. Heat the pan on a medium heat until a drop of water evaporates on contact.
Spread about 1/2 cup of batter on the pan (like for crêpes) slowing spreading it outwards to form a thin, circular dosa.
Allow it to cook for a minute and, using a flat spatula, flip it over to the other side to cook. As the other side cooks, spread a layer of ghee-shortening mixture on the topside.
Flip it over again. As the bottom crisps add 1 teaspoon of onion chutney on the top, and spread it evenly.
Add some of the filling onto one half of the dosa and fold the other side over. Serve with coconut chutney.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Matar Paneer
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 8 oz (200 g) paneer, cut in 1” cubes
3 green chilies, seeded and finely chopped

steps.text: Frying paneer: Heat some oil in a deep pan.
Add paneer cubes in it. Fry on all the sides over medium-low heat until golden brown.
Remove paneer from the pan, and drain on paper towels.
Gravy: Remove excess oil from the same pan, and add ginger-garlic paste.
Add chopped onion to it. Cook, stirring, until onion becomes translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes and mix. Cook well over medium heat.
Turn off the heat when tomatoes have left all the water. Let cool.
Transfer mixture to a blender, and add the chiles.
Blend until smooth.
Matar paneer: Heat oil in a pan.
Add cumin seeds, and fry until they start to crackle.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Mix well over low heat.
Add the blended purée, and mix well over medium heat.
Season with salt, then mix in the peas.
Add some water, cover, and steam until the peas are fully cooked.
Uncover and add the fried paneer. Mix well, adding more water if required.
Tadka: Heat a small pan/tadka pan.
Add 1 tsp oil and 1/2 tsp red chilli powder. Mix well.
Turn off the gas and add to the matar paneer while serving.

recipes.notes: Paneer is a pressed uncured cheese usually made fresh. It can be bought in Indian or specialty grocery stores or substituted by tofu if unavailable. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Sonja Pauen - Stanhopea / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 de — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Matar_Panir_mit_Chapati_-_Mutter_Paneer_with_chapati.jpg

recipes.title: Matcha Latte
recipes.description: Bright green tea whisked to a froth and poured over steamed milk with a touch of sweetness.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 to 2 tsp honey or sugar, to taste

steps.text: Sift the matcha into a wide mug or bowl to remove any lumps.
Add the hot water and whisk vigorously in a zigzag motion with a bamboo whisk or small frother for 30 seconds until frothy.
Heat the milk in a small saucepan over medium heat until steaming, about 3 minutes, without letting it boil.
Froth the milk with a frother or whisk until foamy.
Stir the honey or sugar into the matcha, then pour in the frothed milk and serve immediately.

recipes.photoCredit: John Beans / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Matcha_tea_art.jpg

recipes.title: Matzo Ball Soup
recipes.description: A comforting Passover classic: light, fluffy matzo dumplings simmered in golden chicken soup with carrots and dill.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/4 cup chicken broth or seltzer water

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, schmaltz or oil, and 1/4 cup broth or seltzer in a bowl.
Stir in the matzo meal, salt and pepper until just combined. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes so the matzo meal can absorb the liquid.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
With wet hands, roll the mixture into 1-inch balls (they will double in size) and drop them into the boiling water.
Cover, reduce the heat to a steady simmer and cook for 30 to 35 minutes without lifting the lid, until the balls are fluffy and cooked through.
Meanwhile, simmer the chicken broth with the carrots, celery and onion for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the shredded chicken, if using, and season the soup with salt and pepper.
Lift the matzo balls into the soup with a slotted spoon, sprinkle with dill and serve hot.

recipes.title: Maultaschen (Swabian Filled Pasta)
recipes.description: Large Swabian pasta pockets filled with meat, spinach and herbs, served in broth or pan-fried with onions.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 10 oz frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
4 oz smoked ham or bratwurst meat, finely chopped
1 stale roll, soaked in water and squeezed

steps.text: Mix the flour, eggs, salt and water into a firm dough, knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Melt the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then let cool.
Combine the onion with the spinach, ground pork, ham, soaked roll, egg, parsley, salt, pepper and nutmeg and mix well.
Divide the dough in half and roll each piece into a thin rectangle about 12 x 16 inches.
Spread half of the filling over the lower half of each sheet, leaving a border, then fold the top half over.
Press firmly with the handle of a wooden spoon at 3-inch intervals to seal, then cut into squares along the pressed lines.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and cook the Maultaschen for 12 to 15 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
Serve them in bowls of hot broth sprinkled with chives, or slice leftovers and fry them in butter with onions and egg.

recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Maultaschensuppe.jpg

recipes.title: Meat and Potatoes in Broth (Niku Jaga)
recipes.description: Niku jaga (肉じゃが nikujaga meaning 'meat and potatoes') is a common Japanese household dish served at dinnertime.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Cut potatoes into bite-sized pieces. Set aside to soak in cold water.
Combine mirin, soy sauce, sugar, ginger, and beef in a saucepan. Boil lightly for 2–3 minutes.
Remove beef from pan. Add potatoes, sliced onion, and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered until the broth reduces to about 1/3 by volume.
Replace beef in pan, add shirataki noodles, and simmer for roughly 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and serve.

recipes.notes: Pork can be substituted for the beef. Vary the amount of potatoes to taste. The level of liquid does not need to, and in fact should not, completely cover the potatoes at the start of boiling. They will cook via steam, and the comparatively small volume of the liquid helps to concentrate the flavor. Real mirin is important for preventing the potatoes from crumbling apart, especially when using Russets—it contains certain special sugars that prevent over-softening. Livre de cuisine/Nikujaga (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Yumi Kimura from Yokohama, JAPAN / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Braised_pork_and_potatoes_(3089327692).jpg

recipes.title: Meat and Shrimp Potstickers
recipes.description: Potstickers (锅贴 鍋貼 guōtiē; literally "pot stick") are a Northern Chinese-style dumpling popular as a street food, appetizer, or side order in Japanese and Chinese cuisine. This dish is often served on a dim sum menu, but may be offered independently. The filling for this dish usually contains pork (or chicken), cabbage, scallions, ginger, and sesame seed oil.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/2 pound (about 250 g) ground chicken or pork
1/2 pound ground raw prawn or shrimp
1/2 cup water chestnuts (fresh if possible) peeled and sliced

steps.text: 1 package store-bought gyoza/wonton wrappers
Cornstarch
Vegetable oil
Mix together the filling ingredients.
Place a small bowl of water on the work area. If desired, mix in a little cornstarch to make a glue.
Lay out one of the gyoza wrappers in front of you.
Dip your finger in the water and moisten the edges of the wrapper.
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of the wrapper.
Fold the gyoza wrapper over the filling and pinch the edges to seal it shut.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet or wok.
When oil is ready, carefully add the dumplings and cook on high heat until golden brown (about 1 minute).
Without turning the dumplings over, add 1 cup of water and cover.
Steam for about 1 minute to cook the raw filling and then turn off the heat (this is to keep the bottom from burning).
Let the dumplings cook for a few more minutes with the heat turned off.
Serve the potstickers with dipping sauce or soy sauce.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Potstickers_RTE.jpg

recipes.title: Mediterranean Grilled Tuna
recipes.description: This is a very simple and quick recipe for delicious fresh tuna steaks.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: At least one hour before serving, prepare a marinade with the oil, vinegar or lime juice, tarragon leaves, salt and pepper in a flat container. Pour over the tuna steaks and turn them to make sure all pieces are well coated. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until it is time to grill.
Spray a clean grill or grilling container with non-stick cooking spray.
Drain and reserve the excess marinade from the tuna. Grill tuna for about 4 minutes on each side or until nicely charred on the outside and still a bit pink in the middle.
Place the steaks on individual serving dishes and pour the marinade on the grilled tuna.
Serve with steamed vegetables, steamed rice, or a spinach salad.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Medu Vada (South Indian Savory Lentil Donut)
recipes.description: A vada is a savoury South Indian doughnut made from lentils (or sometimes potatoes). This is a recipe for medu vada. It is commonly accompanied by idli.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Wash and soak urad dal for 6 hours. Grind into a fine paste.
Add salt, asafoetida, curry leaves, cumin powder, and crushed peppercorns to the batter and mix well.
Heat oil in a kadai.
Wet your palms and take batter into the palms.
Shape into balls and make a hole with the thumb in the centre like a doughnut.
Deep-fry this in medium-hot oil until golden brown and crisp.
Serve hot with sambhar and coconut chutney.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Memphis-Style BBQ Ribs
recipes.description: This is a classic U.S. style of BBQ pork ribs.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Season spareribs with rib rub.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Place chunks in smoker or charcoal grill set for indirect heat at 250°F (120°C).
Combine liquid ingredients and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce liquid by 1/3.
Place spareribs into smoker or grill for 4–5 hours, basting occasionally with sauce.
Brush remaining sauce on top of ribs and place on a medium-high grill until browned. The internal temperature of the ribs before removing from the grill needs to be at least 145°F (63°C).
Let rest for 10 minutes, covered, and carve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
