Cut the smashed cucumbers into bite-size pieces.
Toss the cucumbers with the salt and sugar in a colander and let drain for 10 minutes.
Stir together the garlic, black vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and chili oil.
Shake off the excess liquid from the cucumbers and toss them with the dressing.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and cilantro and serve right away, cold.

recipes.title: Smoked Garlic Chicken
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 4 whole chicken leg quarters, skin removed

steps.text: Combine seasonings. Set aside.
Brush chicken with mustard. This will help make a crust. Press seasoning mixture into both sides of meat. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Preheat smoker to 225°F with mesquite. Add chicken pieces and insert a probe thermometer into one of them. Cook, adding wood as needed, until internal temperature reaches 170°F.
Move to a very very high grill and cook until charred and marked. Flip and repeat.
Serve immediately with desired side dishes.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Smoked Pork Roast
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 ea. (4 pounds) boneless pork loin roast, trimmed of excess fat

steps.text: Combine salt, honey, and vinegar in a 6-quart container. Add ice, cover, and shake until ice is mostly melted and brine has cooled.
Add pork roast, toss to coat, and weigh down if needed. Refrigerate 3–3.5 hours.
Take roast out of brine; rinse with cold water. Pat dry with paper towels and set aside.
Combine seasonings and sugar. Press into all sides of meat. Set aside.
Preheat smoker to 200°F with the hickory chunks. Add roast, cover, and cook until internal temperature reaches 135°F for medium rare.
Remove to a plate and cover tightly with foil. Let rest 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon on Brown Bread
recipes.description: A classic Irish starter of silky smoked salmon on buttered brown soda bread with lemon, capers, and red onion.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/4 small red onion, very thinly sliced
2 tbsp crème fraîche or sour cream (optional)

steps.text: Spread each slice of brown bread generously with butter.
Drape the smoked salmon in loose folds over the bread.
Top with a few slices of red onion and a scattering of capers.
Add a small dollop of crème fraîche if using.
Sprinkle with dill and freshly ground black pepper.
Cut each slice in half and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodles IV
recipes.description: Snickerdoodles are sugar cookies lightly dusted with cinnamon. They have a characteristically crackly surface, and can be crisp or soft, depending on preference. Some variants include nutmeg, raisins, or nuts. They are a traditional Christmas cookie in North America.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 344 g (2 3/4 cups or 24 oz) all-purpose flour
300 g (1 1/2 cups or 9 oz) superfine sugar

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix flour, salt, baking soda, cream of tartar. Set aside.
Beat butter, shortening and sugar.
Beat in eggs and vanilla.
Gradually add dry ingredients, mixing fully.
Roll into 1 tbsp balls.
Mix sugar and cinnamon.
Roll balls in sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Bake for 10 minutes or until crisp and light brown.
Let cool completely before eating.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Sofkee
recipes.description: A mildly sour, thin corn drink of the Muscogee (Creek) and Seminole peoples, made from cracked hominy and enjoyed warm or cool with meals.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp baking soda (to stand in for traditional wood-ash lye)

steps.text: Rinse the grits in a strainer.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pot and stir in the grits, baking soda, and salt.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 1 1/2 hours, adding water as needed to keep it thin and drinkable.
The corn should be very soft and the liquid creamy and pourable.
Serve warm, or let stand at room temperature for a day to develop the traditional slightly sour flavor, then refrigerate.

recipes.title: Sopa de Fideo
recipes.description: A homey Mexican noodle soup of toasted thin pasta simmered in a tomato-chicken broth, a favorite comfort food in kitchens across the country.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 7 oz fideo noodles or thin spaghetti broken into 1-inch pieces

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, onion, and garlic with 1/2 cup of the broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the fideo and stir constantly for 3–4 minutes until the noodles are evenly golden brown.
Carefully pour in the tomato purée (it will splatter) and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining broth, cilantro sprig, and salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Remove the cilantro sprig, taste for salt, and serve topped with avocado, queso fresco, and lime.

recipes.title: Soy Sauce Chicken
recipes.description: Soy sauce chicken (醬油雞) is a northern Chinese dish.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Fry the chicken parts in a pan with green onions and oil until the outside of the chicken parts are brown.
Add soy sauce, cooking wine, chopped ginger, and sugar. Add enough water to cover the chicken.
Simmer, uncovered, over low heat until most of the liquid has evaporated.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Dennis Wong from Hong Kong, Hong Kong / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Soy_Sauce_Chicken.jpg

recipes.title: Spaetzle
recipes.description: Spaetzle (German: Spätzle) means literally translated "little sparrow" and is a Swabian specialty from Germany. It is made from flour, eggs, water, and salt. There are different techniques to make spaetzle, such as using a spaetzle-maker or spaetzle-press. The original technique is to use a kitchen board and a grater.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Combine all ingredients using hands or an electrical mixer.
Add enough water to make a dough that is slightly sticky, but still elastic and stiff.
Beat long enough for bubbles to rise.
Boil a large pot with salted water.

If using only a board, sweep a spoon of dough over the kitchen board with the grater. Cut/grate small pieces of the dough with the grater into the hot water. If using a spaetzle-maker, put a spoon of dough into the maker and press through the holes into the water. The spaetzle are done when they rise and swim on the water surface.
Remove spaetzle from the water with a slotted spoon and put into a lightly oiled bowl.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce (Naporitan)
recipes.description: Naporitan or napolitan (ナポリタン) is the name of a pasta dish, which is popular in Japan. It is claimed to originate from Yokohama.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/4 lb (110 g) sausage or ham, sliced

steps.text: Put about 8 cups of water in a large pot, and add 2 tbsp salt. Bring to a boil on high heat and cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Meanwhile, heat vegetable oil in a large skillet and stir-fry onion, bell pepper, and sausage on medium heat until softened. Season with salt and pepper.
Add drained spaghetti in the skillet and stir-fry with other ingredients.
Add ketchup and stir-fry the spaghetti. Mix in butter and stop the heat.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Spice Bag
recipes.description: Dublin's favorite takeaway: crispy chicken strips, chips, peppers, and onions tossed in a spicy salt-and-pepper seasoning.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into strips

steps.text: Mix all the spice mix ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.
Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pot to 325°F (160°C) and fry the potatoes in batches for 5 minutes until soft but pale; drain on paper towels.
Dip the chicken strips in beaten egg, then toss in the mixed cornstarch and flour, shaking off the excess.
Raise the oil temperature to 350°F (175°C) and fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain.
Increase the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry the potatoes again for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and golden; drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat and stir-fry the bell pepper, onion, and chili for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, fries, and scallions to the wok, sprinkle with 2 to 3 teaspoons of the spice mix, and toss well to coat.
Serve at once in paper bags or bowls, with curry sauce on the side if you like.

recipes.photoCredit: Sean Zissou / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Spice_Bag_(cropped).jpg

recipes.title: Spicy Cheddar Dip with Olives
recipes.description: Spicy cheddar dip with olives is the end all-be all of appetizers. People will line up to get another taste of this. It has enough calories to knock you off your feet. Be careful when serving it before a dinner, as it is quite filling. Some people eat so much of this that they can't handle the main course! This would be suitable as the centerpiece while watching the game, or as a wonderful treat during parties.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 8 oz (225 g) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded or diced very small
3 oz (80 g) black olives, sliced into rings
4 oz (110 g) canned diced green chiles
2 tbsp garlic powder, or to taste
2 tbsp hot sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Slice pitas as you would a pizza, into triangles. Separate pita triangles into halves, and place on a cookie sheet, inside surface up.
Toast in oven until golden brown, but not dark and bitter. This results in novel chips used to scoop the dip.
Combine the cheese, mayonnaise, chiles, half the olives, garlic powder, and hot sauce.
Microwave on high until the edges liquefy and bubble, then mix until everything is of the same consistency. Repeat this process until the whole bowl is creamy and a rich orange color.

Garnish the dip with the remaining olives, green onions, and tomatoes. Standard garnishing technique calls for arranging the remaining black olives, green onions, and diced tomatoes into a bulls-eye pattern.
Serve the dip with the pita chips.

recipes.notes: Scaling the recipe up is easy. Just procure a larger bowl, and increase the ingredients. Do NOT use miracle whip instead of mayonnaise—this totally changes the taste of the dip. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Spinach Artichoke Dip
recipes.description: Formal or informal, spinach artichoke dip is a great appetizer at any party. It is quick and easy taking very little time to prepare. The dip may be served with a variety or crackers, breads, or chips.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 3/4 cup (180 ml) heavy cream (use half milk, if desired)
16 ounces (450 g) frozen cut leaf spinach, thawed and well drained
1 can quartered artichoke hearts, rinsed and well-drained
2/3 cup (160 ml) shredded Monterey Jack cheese
Crackers or tortilla chips, for serving

steps.text: In a food processor fitted with a metal blade, process the cream cheese, cream, Parmesan cheese, and garlic powder until smooth and creamy. Add the spinach and process until thoroughly mixed. Add the artichokes and process just until coarsely chopped.
Turn the mixture into a 3 1/2-quart electric slow cooker; smooth the top.

Cover and cook on the high heat setting for 1 1/4–1 1/2 hours, until hot in the center. Sprinkle the top evenly with the Jack cheese and spoon the salsa in a ring around the inside edges of the slow cooker. Cover and continue heating on high 15 minutes longer, or until the cheese is melted.
Reduce the heat to the low setting and serve warm with crackers or tortilla chips for dipping. Refrigerate any leftovers.

recipes.notes: This dip is best served hot but may also be served chilled. If served in a bread bowl, pieces may be broken off and used as dipping tools for further enjoyment. Other condiments that go great with this dip include sides of salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. This is great appetizer for vegetarians, and vegan cream cheese may be substituted if need be. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Spinach Gomaae (Spinach with Sesame Dressing)
recipes.description: Blanched spinach tossed in a nutty, slightly sweet toasted sesame dressing, a classic Japanese side dish.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and prepare a bowl of ice water.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking often, until fragrant and golden.
Grind the warm seeds in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder until about half are crushed.
Mix the ground sesame with the soy sauce, sugar, and mirin to form a thick dressing.
Blanch the spinach for 30 to 45 seconds, then transfer immediately to the ice water.
Drain the spinach, gather it into a bundle, and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Cut the spinach into 1 1/2-inch lengths and toss with the sesame dressing just before serving.

recipes.photoCredit: Alice Seba / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Goma-ae_salad.jpg

recipes.title: Springerle
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Beat eggs until light-colored and almost dry—this takes a long time, and an electric mixer is recommended.
Beat the sugar into the eggs.
Combine the flour and baking powder. Work into the eggs to make a delicate dough.
Grease several cookie sheets and scatter generously with crushed anise seeds.
Roll the dough gently and carefully imprint with springerle mold. Cut into pieces and transfer to baking sheets. Allow to dry overnight.
Bake at 250°F (120°C) for 25–30 minutes.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Springerle_with_typical_foot_swabian_Fuessle.jpg

recipes.title: Spritzgeback (German Spritz Butter Cookies)
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 tsp almond, vanilla, or lemon extract

steps.text: Beat butter and sugar until light.
Beat in egg, egg yolk and extract.
Sift flour, salt, and baking powder together; gradually add flour mixture to eggs.
Chill dough for 1/2 hour.
Press 1/4 of the dough into a cookie press.
Keep remaining dough chilled.
Shape cookies onto a greased baking sheet.
Bake in oven at for 7–10 minutes or until done.
Cool on wire racks and store in airtight tins.

recipes.title: Steak and Ale Pie
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) good beef stewing steak, at room temperature
1 handful fresh thyme, marjoram and chopped parsley

steps.text: Cut the beef into cubes about 2.5 cm square.
Heat oil in a saucepan and fry the onion, without letting it colour.
Add beef, making sure the meat is at room temperature first, and cook until medium brown.
Stir in the flour and cook until dark brown (about 1 minute)
Add Worcestershire sauce, thyme, marjoram, mustard, bay leaf and seasoning.
Slowly add beef stock and ale, then bring to the boil.
Simmer gently until beef is almost tender, approximately 1 1/2 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Remove meat from heat, skim off any fat, adjust seasoning and add fresh chopped parsley.
Place in pie dish or individual dishes. Cover pie dish (or dishes) with the pastry and trim edges.
Bake for 20–25 minutes or until pastry is well-risen and golden brown.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Miia Ranta from Finland / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Making_Steak_and_Ale_pies_for_the_weekend_events_(7318950220).jpg

recipes.title: Steak and Guinness Pie
recipes.description: Tender chunks of beef braised in Guinness with onions and mushrooms under a golden puff pastry lid, a favorite of Irish pubs.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 1/2 cups Guinness or other Irish stout

steps.text: Toss the beef with the flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per batch; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, onions, and mushrooms and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until browned, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the stout, scraping up the browned bits, then add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, thyme, and the beef.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 2 hours until the beef is very tender and the gravy has thickened.
Remove the thyme stems and let the filling cool for at least 20 minutes so it does not melt the pastry.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and spoon the filling into a 2-quart pie dish.
Lay the puff pastry over the dish, trim and crimp the edges, cut a small steam vent, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Steak and Kidney Pudding
recipes.description: This recipe comes from Mrs Beeton's famous Book of Household Management.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Cut the steak into about 2.5 cm (1 inch) squares. Cut each kidney into 8 pieces.
Line the basin with crust, leaving a small piece of crust to overlap the edge.

Then cover the bottom with a piece of the steak and a few pieces of kidney; season with salt and pepper, and then add another layer of steak, kidney and seasoning. Proceed in this manner until the basin is full, when pour in sufficient water to come within 5 cm (2 inch) of the top of the basin.
Moisten the edges of the crust, cover the pudding over, press the two crusts together, so that the gravy does not escape, and turn up the overhanging pastry.

Wring out a cloth in hot water, flour it and tie up the pudding; put it int boiling water and let it boil for at least 4 hours. If the water diminishes, always replenish with hot water from a jug, as the pudding should be kept covered all the time, and not allowed to stop boiling.

When the cloth is removed, cut out a round piece in the top of the crust, to prevent the pudding bursting, and send it to table in the basin, either in an ornamental dish or with a napkin pinned round it. Serve quickly.

recipes.notes: To make the crust, combine 175 g (6 oz) suet per 450 g (1 lb) all-purpose flour, and moisten with milk to make a dough. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Chris Jobling from Swansea, Wales / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SteakKidneyPudding.jpg

recipes.title: Steamed Buns with BBQ Pork
recipes.description: This is a yeast dough bun that is stuffed with a meat filling and steamed until cooked.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 8 ounces (225 g) shredded cooked pork or chicken

steps.text: Bun filling: Place all ingredients in food processor.
Process until ingredients are blended and chopped fine.
Steamed buns: Stir yeast and 1 tablespoon of sugar into 1 1/2 cups of warm water (95°F / 35°C.). Let stand for 15 minutes.
Mix yeast water, 2 more tablespoons of sugar, flour, cooking oil, baking powder, and salt in mixing bowl.
Stir until dough forms. Knead dough for 10 minutes.
Allow dough to rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 hours.
Punch dough down and divide into 12 pieces.
Roll each piece of dough into a ball, then flatten with rolling pin into a 6-inch (15 cm) circle.
Place 1 tablespoon of meat filling in center of each flattened piece of dough.
Lift the edges of the flattened dough up around the filling and bring edges together. Pinch edges closed to form filled bun.
Place buns on parchment paper. Allow to rise in a warm place 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Steam buns in a steamer over boiling water for 20 minutes.
Remove from steamer. When cool enough to handle, remove parchment paper from bottom.
Serve warm.

recipes.notes: Keep leftovers refrigerated. Reheat in microwave for 30–45 seconds.
recipes.photoCredit: City Foodsters / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pork_Belly_Steamed_Buns_-_Duroc_pork_belly,_cilantro,_scallions,_radish,_boiled_egg,_Chinese_black_vinaigrette,_hoisin_BBQ_sauce.jpg

recipes.title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
recipes.description: A whole fish steamed until just tender, then finished with sizzling oil poured over fresh ginger and scallions and a light soy sauce.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 (1 1/2 to 2 lb) whole sea bass, cleaned and scaled
2-inch piece fresh ginger, half sliced and half finely julienned
4 green onions, half cut into 3-inch pieces and half finely julienned

steps.text: Pat the fish dry, make two diagonal slashes on each side, and rub lightly with salt inside and out.
Lay the ginger slices and green onion pieces on a heatproof plate, place the fish on top, and drizzle with the Shaoxing wine.
Bring water to a boil in a wok or steamer large enough to hold the plate.
Steam the fish covered over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the flesh flakes easily at the thickest part near the bone.
Meanwhile, warm the light soy sauce, water, and sugar in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves.
Carefully remove the plate, pour off the steaming liquid, and discard the cooked ginger and onion.
Scatter the julienned ginger and green onions over the fish.
Heat the oil in a small pan until it just begins to smoke, then pour it over the ginger and green onions so they sizzle.
Pour the warm soy mixture around the fish, garnish with cilantro, and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Steamed Pork With Mustard Greens
recipes.description: Steamed pork with mustard greens (梅菜扣肉, pinyin: Méicàikòuròu) or mei cai kou rou is a Chinese dish from the Hakka people. It is very popular and tasty but contains a lot of saturated fat.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 tsp cornstarch combined with 1 tsp cold water
2 tbsp black bean and garlic sauce

steps.text: Wash greens and discard tough stems.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add greens, and cook for 2 minutes.
Drain greens and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking. Drain again, then cut greens into long diagonal strips.
In a medium bowl, combine cornstarch and water. Stir in sugar, soy sauce and rice wine. Cut pork into thin slices and add to the mixture. Marinate about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Heat oil in a preheated wok or large heavy skillet over medium heat. Add black bean sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add mustard greens and water. Mix well and simmer gently about 4–5 minutes, until pork is cooked through and greens are tender.
Season with pepper and serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sichuan-style_Steamed_Sliced_Pork_on_Rice_-_Charming_Spice_(3951774447).jpg

recipes.title: Steamed Sweet Rice
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) sweet glutinous rice (mochi gome)

steps.text: Place sweet glutinous rice in a medium bowl.
Wash rice thoroughly in cool water, rinsing and repeating until water is clear, drain, then return rice to bowl.
Add 3 cups (720 ml) water to the rice. Soak for 6 hours or overnight.
Drain well, spread rice evenly in a round, 8–9 inch (20 cm) shallow baking pan, and add 1/3 cup (80 ml) water.
In a wok, bring about 4 cups (950 ml) water to a boil over medium high heat.
Place a steamer tray in the wok.
Cover the pan of rice and place on the tray over the boiling water.
Steam for 30 minutes. If rice is not tender, sprinkle with 2–3 tablespoons of water, and steam it for 5 minutes more.
When tender, remove steamer tray from wok.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Sticky Toffee Pudding (with dates)
recipes.description: Sticky toffee pudding (STP) is a rich, dense, gooey dessert originating from the United Kingdom that can now be found across the world. Often found on a pub's menu, or in British or Commonwealth schools meals, this is a classic dessert that became popular in the 1970s.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 7/8 stick (100 g) unsalted butter, room temperature
2 1/2 cups (250 g) dates (without stones), finely chopped
2/3 cup (120 g) dark, soft brown sugar

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180°C/360°F.

Cream together the butter, sugar and vanilla. You can do this by beating it in a bowl with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes, taking care to break up the crystals and smooth the mixture out as much as possible. Or, do it using an electric mixer if you prefer.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating after you've added each egg.
Fold in the flour.
Bring the water to the boil and add the dates. Add the bicarb and immediately take the pan off the heat. Let it cool slightly, then add to the batter.
Pour the batter into a greased cake tin—make sure you use one with enough room for the cake to rise.
Bake in the oven for 40 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the cake comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and set aside to cool a little while you make the sauce
Mix the sauce ingredients in a saucepan. Heat gently, stirring often to make sure that the mixture doesn't separate, until it is a smooth sauce—don't allow it to bubble.
Divide the cake into portions and poke holes all over the top with a skewer or chopstick.
Pour the sauce over the top of the cake, making sure it gets in the holes. Serve with cream, custard, or ice cream.

recipes.notes: Finely chopping the dates helps make a really gooey cake, but some people prefer to chop the dates roughly so that they're more obvious in the finished pudding. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Sarah Stierch / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sticky_toffee_pudding_at_the_Black_Swan_-_Stierch.jpg

recipes.title: Stir Fried Seafood with Noodles
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 pack (500 g) Hong Kong-style egg noodles, rehydrated and boiled if needed
100 g cabbage, cut into bite-sized pieces
150 g bean sprouts, rinsed in hot water

steps.text: Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, add the garlic, and fry for about 10 seconds until golden brown.
Add the fishball and shrimp. Stir fry until the shrimp and fishball just begin to change color.
Add the cabbage and scallion, and stir fry at least until all ingredients are hot.
Add the noodles, and stir fry until all ingredients are hot.

Add the bean sprouts, light soy sauce, salt, sugar and pepper. Mix well and stir fry (perhaps on reduced heat) until all ingredients are hot, taking care to not cook so long as to overly wilt the bean sprouts.
Serve immediately with fried onion.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Shrimp with Broccoli
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 300 g broccoli, cut into florets and rinsed

steps.text: Heat a pan, add the oil and garlic, and fry until golden.
Add the shrimp and broccoli. Season with salt and oyster sauce, and add a little water. Stir together.
Put on a plate and serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Mack Male from Edmonton, AB, Canada / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Making_Stir-Fry_(3286445383).jpg

recipes.title: Stir-fried tomato and scrambled eggs
recipes.description: Stir-fried tomato and scrambled eggs (Chinese: 西红柿炒鸡蛋/番茄炒蛋) is a common dish in China, typically served as a main course in Chinese households. Its popularity owes to its simplicity and accessible ingredients. This recipe is a simplified and translated version of 星星糖宝贝's recipe on xiachufang.com.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Make a cross-shaped cut on the top of the tomatoes and blanch in boiling water.
After a short period of time, put the tomatoes in ice water to shock them and remove the skins.
Cut the tomatoes into chunks and set aside.
Whisk together the eggs, season to taste with a pinch of salt, and scramble them in a skillet with a little oil. Set aside after cooking process is finished.
Heat a little oil oil in a separate skillet, add the scallions, and sauté briefly.
Add the tomatoes to the scallions, and stir-fry until the tomatoes release their juices.
Add the scrambled eggs to the pan with the scallions and tomatoes, and let everything simmer to reduce the tomato juice.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: 三島堂 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E7%95%AA%E8%8C%84%E7%82%92%E8%9B%8B2.PNG

recipes.title: Stovies
recipes.description: Stovies is a traditional Scottish dish originating mainly from the North Eastern counties of Angus and Aberdeenshire where even today the dish is still most commonly found and served. Recipes and ingredients vary widely between regions and even families, but the dish usually consists of potatoes and onions and some form of cold meat (especially sausages or leftover roast; mince or corned beef in the east).
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 50 g (2 oz) beef drippings or butter
125–250 g (4–8 oz) cooked beef or lamb (leftovers from a roast dinner)
2–3 tbsp finely chopped parsley, chives, or spring onions

steps.text: Peel potatoes if they are "main crop", but leave the skins on new potatoes. Slice about 5 mm (1/4-inch) thick. Or, slice roughly in different thickness so that the thin make a mush when cooked, while the others stay whole.
Heat fat in a large heavy-base pot (one with a tight-fitting lid) and add the onions. Cook until lightly brown. Add the potatoes and stir well, coating all sides with the fat.
Put the lid on and cook over a very low heat, shaking the pot once or twice to prevent sticking, until the potatoes are cooked.
Add the meat, mix through, and turn up the heat to brown a little.
Serve with brown sauce, parsley, and optional seasonings.

recipes.notes: The same recipe can be adapted to use steak, beef or pork sausages instead of leftover meat. If making stovies this way, brown the sausages with the onions at the start. Recipes vary but mince is used most commonly, not only in the East but all over Scotland (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Mutt Lunker / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Stovies_containing_beef.jpg

recipes.title: Strawberry and Yogurt Eton Mess
recipes.description: Eton mess is a dessert of English origin consisting of a mixture of strawberries, pieces of meringue and cream, which is traditionally served at Eton College's annual prize-giving celebration picnic on the "Fourth of June" (actually celebrated on the last Wednesday in May).
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 280 ml (1 1/5 cup or 9 1/2 fl oz) double cream
150 ml (3/5 cup or 5 fl oz) Greek yoghurt
500 g (2 1/5 cups or 1 lb 2 oz) strawberries

steps.text: Rinse the strawberries, remove the tops, and cut into halves.
Break the meringues into pieces (not too small) and place into a bowl.
Put the double cream, vanilla essence, and icing sugar into a bowl. Whip until reasonably stiff.
Combine the whipped cream, yoghurt, strawberries, and meringue, being careful not to mash the meringue into pieces that are too small.
Serve in bowls.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Stuffed Burgers
recipes.description: Stuffed burgers are gaining popularity because you don't really know what you're gonna bite down on.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add garlic and onion, and cook until garlic is golden.
Combine cheeses, bacon, cooked onion and garlic, and butter. Set aside.

Form meat into 8 equal patties. Make an indentation into the middle of each patty and place a dollop of cheese mixture into dent. Place 1 patty on top of each other, stuffing side down, and push down until patty is about 3/4 inch thick. Set aside while you heat your trusty charcoal grill (not with that solvent stuff).

Brush patties with olive oil and season liberally on both sides with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Set down on grill and cook, turning often, until instant-read thermometer inserted into the meat, not the stuffing, reads desired temperature (at least 160°F).
Brush the cut side of each bun with melted butter. Place a patty on top of a bottom half of a bun and top with a top half of a bun. Serve warm.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Stuffed Squash Blossoms
recipes.description: Delicate squash blossoms filled with a corn and cheese mixture and pan-fried, celebrating a summer harvest prized by the Pueblo peoples and Indigenous farmers across the Southwest.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/2 cup crumbled fresh cheese or ricotta

steps.text: Gently open each blossom, pinch out the stamen, and check for insects.
Mix the corn, cheese, green chile, and salt.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon of filling into each blossom and twist the petal tips to close.
Dip each blossom in beaten egg and roll in cornmeal.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the blossoms for 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

recipes.title: Succotash
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 24 ears of corn cut off the cob

steps.text: If using pork, cover pork with water, and parboil it.
Add beans, then corn, sugar, butter, and pepper to taste. After corn is added, watch carefully to keep from scorching.
Serve.

recipes.notes: A chopped red bell pepper can be added. Note that lima beans that have not been cooked should be thoroughly boiled for at least 10 minutes to rid the beans of phytohemagglutinin, a toxin found in uncooked lima beans. Canned beans are safe to eat without cooking. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Ralph Daily from Birmingham, United States / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Corn_%26_Beans_(15392776377).jpg

recipes.title: Sufganiyot (Jelly Doughnuts)
recipes.description: Pillowy fried doughnuts filled with jam and dusted with sugar — a favorite Hanukkah treat.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Stir the yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar into the warm milk and let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine the flour, remaining sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the yeast mixture, eggs and butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Roll the dough 1/2 inch thick and cut 2 1/2-inch rounds. Place on a floured tray, cover and let rise 30 minutes.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the doughnuts a few at a time for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes per side, until deep golden. Drain on paper towels.
When cool enough to handle, poke a hole in the side of each doughnut and pipe in about 2 tsp of jam.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve the same day.

recipes.title: Sukiyaki
recipes.description: Sukiyaki is a kind of shabu-shabu (a Japanese dish) but it is a bit sweeter.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Wash the vegetables, and cut them into large pieces.
Soak the mushrooms in warm water for 15 minutes.
Mix the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Heat an electric skillet on low heat, and grease with a little bit of oil.
Put a few slices of beef into the skillet, and cook them until brown.
Add sauce (don't add all of them at the same time).
Sort the beef slices to the sides. Add the rest of the ingredients in an organized fashion.
Serve the sukiyaki with bowls of rice, with a raw egg yolk as the dip. Add more ingredients as necessary.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Sumac Lemonade
recipes.description: A tart, rosy cold drink steeped from the red berry clusters of staghorn sumac, long enjoyed by Eastern Woodlands peoples in late summer.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 6 large clusters ripe staghorn sumac berries (red, not white)
1/4 cup maple syrup or honey, or to taste

steps.text: Shake the sumac clusters to remove any insects or debris; do not rinse, as that washes away the tart coating.
Place the clusters in a large pitcher or bowl and cover with the cold water.
Gently rub and crush the berries with your hands to release their flavor.
Let steep at room temperature for 1–2 hours until the water is pink and tart.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth or a coffee filter to remove hairs.
Sweeten with maple syrup or honey and serve over ice.

recipes.title: Summer Pudding
recipes.description: Summer pudding is a quintessentially British dessert made from wonderful fresh ingredients only available in the summer months.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 loaf of white, pappy sort of bread or brioche, crusts removed and sliced
1 bottle of the best quality blackcurrant cordial you can find, in reserve

steps.text: Liberally butter the inside a pudding bowl about 5 inches in diameter. The bowl should preferably not be greater in diameter that the size of your pieces of sliced bread. If you are worried about getting the whole thing out of the bowl in one piece, line the bowl first with some cling film. It's a fiddly job, but ensures you get a perfect shape at the end.

Combine the blackcurrants, redcurrants, mint leaves, lime zest, sugar, and about 3 tbsp water. Poach them for about 5 minutes on the lowest possible heat setting of your stove. Add the strawberries and poach for another minute.
Turn the heat off and add the raspberries. Leave to cool.
Using the prepared bowl as a guide, cut a circle out of the white bread the same diameter as the top of the bowl. Do the same with the bottom of the bowl.

Using a sharp knife, slice the bread into squares or oblongs, roughly the same height as the bowl, which will be used to line the inside of the bowl. This does not have to be an exact science. In simple terms what we are trying to do is to line the bowl with the white bread.

Lay the smaller circle of white bread on the bottom of the bowl. Put the oblongs of white bread up the side of the bowl, overlapping slightly, and pour the fruit mixture into the void right up to the top. The bread should become well soaked in the juice from the cooked fruit. Indeed if there is not enough juice to soak the bread so it turns very red, use the cordial as a top-up.
Place the large circle, or disc, of bread on the top and press it down well.
Top with a weight or something that fits into the top of the bowl so it squashes everything down tight, and place it in the fridge for at least 40 minutes.

When you are ready to serve the pudding, carefully using a knife to release the bread mould from the side of the bowl, and invert the whole thing onto a plate. If things become a little fraught and wobbly at this point, don't panic—just sort of whack everything back into shape using a wooden spoon.
Decorate your plate with some more summer fruit, maybe a couple of mint leaves, and an artistic dollop of fresh whipped cream or crème fraîche, then serve with a flourish.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Sunomono (Japanese Cucumber Salad)
recipes.description: A crisp, refreshing salad of paper-thin cucumbers and wakame in a light sweet rice vinegar dressing.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Slice the cucumbers as thinly as possible into rounds.
Toss the cucumbers with the salt in a bowl and let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, soak the wakame in cold water for 5 to 10 minutes until rehydrated, then drain and squeeze dry.
Squeeze the cucumbers firmly to remove the excess liquid.
Stir together the rice vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce until the sugar dissolves.
Combine the cucumbers and wakame with the dressing and toss well.
Chill for at least 10 minutes and serve sprinkled with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Sushi Rice
recipes.description: Sushi rice, termed sushi meshi or shari in Japanese, is a key ingredient for sushi and a staple of Japanese cooking. It consists of short-grain rice dressed with seasoned vinegar called sushisu. The rice is then cooled and dried for easy manipulation and to give a glistening appearance. The Japanese measure their uncooked rice using a measurement called a Gō.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 gō (300 g) uncooked, washed, short-grain Japanese rice
3 metric tablespoons (45 ml) of rice vinegar
1–2 metric tablespoons (12–24 g) of sugar (depending on how sweet you prefer it)

steps.text: About 30 minutes before starting, fill the hangiri with water and let it stand. The water saturates the wood, which prevents the rice from sticking to it.
Make the sushisu: Mix the vinegar, sugar, and salt. Heat the mixture in a saucepan until everything is dissolved, but do not boil. Set aside to cool.

Rinse the rice. Put the rice in the cooking pot, half filled with cold water, and swirl it around with your hand. The water will turn chalky white. Carefully drain off the water, and repeat the process several times, until the water remains clear.
Allow the rice to stand for 30 minutes. Some recipes say the rice should remain in the cooking pot submerged in its cooking water; others say to transfer it temporarily to a colander to drain.
Add an 8 cm-sized sheet of kombu to the cooking pot, along with the sake if you are using it.
Boil the water in the cooking pot.
Remove the kombu from the cooking pot just as the water boils, and reduce the heat. Simmer the water and rice in the cooking pot for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat but do not remove cover from the cooking pot for 10 minutes (no peeking).
Transfer the rice from the cooking pot to the hangiri; if you do not have one, use a large bowl or cookie sheet.

Cut the sushisu gently into rice with the paddle, trying not to break the kernels. For Western chefs: this "cutting" motion is similar to the cut-and-fold used for gentle treatment of egg whites. When finished, the rice is evenly coated with the dressing, giving it a shiny appearance.
Cover the rice with a cloth for a couple of minutes so the dressing is absorbed.
Cool the rice to body temperature by fanning it, while continuing to cut it with the spatula. A traditional hand fan or modern battery-powered fan may be used.

recipes.notes: A rice-cooker is often used instead of a cooking pot; these generally produce good, consistent results. The manufacturer's directions will generally be similar to the above. The rice and sushisu should be mixed immediately after the rice is finished cooking with sushisu at room temperature. Some sushi chefs prefer natural cooling, rather than fanning, and instead let the rice rest in the hangiri for 15 minutes, then re-cut the rice, and continue with this process until the rice is cool. According to some, the faster the rice cools, the better (but see above about natural cooling, which yields a slightly different texture). The rice is best if used quickly: you can use it to make sushi for a few hours; it certainly cannot be prepared a day early. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: chidorian from Japan / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sushi_platter.jpg

recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs I
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 200–300 ml (3/4–1 1/4 cups) liquid, such as water, milk or cream
1 small onion, finely chopped or grated

steps.text: Combine the liquid and bread crumbs in a bowl, and let it sit for 7–8 minutes.
Mix in the ground beef, ground pork, egg, onion, salt, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into round meatballs, approximately 2–3 centimeters (1 inch) in diameter.

Pan fry the meatballs on medium heat in a frying pan with butter for approximately 3–5 minutes. Fry them on all sides until they are brown and not pink in the middle. Shaking the pan occasionally will help the meatballs cook evenly.
Serve them with mashed potatoes with a veal based brown sauce made with cream and lingonberry preserve or cranberry preserve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Chinese Pork
recipes.description: Jing du or sweet-and-sour pork is a Chinese dish of fried and glazed pork.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 America's cut pork (boneless loin roast) per person, cut in 1-inch squares and pounded flat
3 tbsp dry sherry or Chinese rice wine
1/2 tsp hot pepper or chili-garlic sauce
1/4 cup extra-light olive oil or vegetable oil

steps.text: Mix the marinade ingredients in a large bowl and add the meat. Mix well to cover the meat and refrigerate for 2 hours (or overnight).
Combine sauce ingredients and set aside.
Remove pork from refrigerator and remove excess liquid (if any).
Beat egg and cornstarch and cover meat mixing well.
Place 2 tbsp oil in a wok and cook half the meat until no longer pink when slashed (about 2 minutes).
Remove meat, add remaining oil, and cook remaining meat.
Set cooked meat aside and discard pan drippings.
Add ginger and garlic to wok, stirring and cooking until fragrant.
Return pork to wok quickly stirring and add the sauce (stand back when adding sauce or it will really clear your sinuses).
Stir meat and sauce until meat is well covered, serve immediately.

recipes.notes: Extra light olive oil is used to avoid adding olive oil flavor to the dish. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Sweet Beef
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons bacon drippings or vegetable oil

steps.text: Add the bacon drippings/vegetable oil to a skillet over high heat. Add the beef to the skillet, and brown the meat on all sides. Do not cook completely through. Transfer meat to the slow cooker.
In a skillet, melt the butter. Add the onions, and fry until they begin to become transparent.
Combine all the ingredients except the meat in the skillet. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in a slow cooker. Stir together.
Cook on low for 2 1/2–3 1/2 hours.
Serve with mashed potatoes and honey carrots.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sweet_beef_07.jpg

recipes.title: Sweet Mango Lassi
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 L (4 cups) mango nectar (strained puréed mango)

steps.text: Mix sugar with the mango nectar until dissolved.
Gradually add the milk to the yoghurt.
Mix together the mango and yoghurt mixtures.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Taco Casserole
recipes.description: Taco casserole is a casserole with taco ingredients.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Brown the ground beef in skillet on medium heat.
Drain the ground beef.
Dump the ground beef back in the skillet.
While on medium heat mix in the taco seasoning, the chili powder, the garlic powder, and the tomato sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mix the ground beef mixture, tortilla bits, and the cheese together in a casserole dish.
Bake in oven at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Tacos al Pastor
recipes.description: Mexico City's favorite street taco: thin slices of pork marinated in guajillo chiles and achiote, seared hot and served with sweet pineapple.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 1/2 lb boneless pork shoulder, sliced 1/4 inch thick
1/2 fresh pineapple, peeled, cored, and sliced into rings

steps.text: Toast the guajillo chiles in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes and drain.
Blend the chiles with the pineapple juice, vinegar, achiote, garlic, oregano, cumin, cloves, and salt until smooth.
Toss the pork slices with the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or griddle over high heat and grill the pineapple rings until charred on both sides, then chop them.
Add a little oil to the skillet and sear the pork in batches without crowding, 2–3 minutes per side, until caramelized and cooked through.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then chop it into small pieces.
Fill the warm tortillas with pork and top with pineapple, onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.photoCredit: Matt Saunders / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tacos-al-Pastor.jpg

recipes.title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
recipes.description: A lightly sweet, layered rolled omelet that is a staple of Japanese breakfasts and bento boxes.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, dashi, sugar, mirin, soy sauce, and salt in a bowl until well combined but not foamy.
Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan or 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and wipe it with a little oil using a folded paper towel.
Pour in about a quarter of the egg mixture and tilt the pan to coat the bottom in a thin layer.
When the egg is just set on the bottom but still slightly wet on top, roll it from the far side toward you into a log.
Push the roll back to the far side of the pan and wipe the empty part of the pan with oil again.
Pour in another quarter of the egg, lifting the roll so the raw egg flows underneath it.
When the new layer is nearly set, roll the log back toward you, wrapping it in the new layer.
Repeat with the remaining egg mixture to build up the layers.
Transfer the omelet to a bamboo mat or plastic wrap, shape it into a neat rectangle, and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Slice into 1-inch pieces and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.photoCredit: 極地狐 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E9%B3%A5%E7%84%BC%E3%81%8D%E5%B1%85%E9%85%92%E5%B1%8B_(39394233682).jpg

recipes.title: Tangyuan (Sweet Rice Balls in Ginger Syrup)
recipes.description: Chewy glutinous rice dumplings filled with black sesame paste and served in a warm ginger syrup, eaten for family reunions.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 3 tbsp unsalted butter or lard, softened
1/3 cup brown sugar or rock sugar

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant, then grind them finely with the sugar.
Mix the ground sesame with the softened butter into a paste, chill for 15 minutes, then roll into 16 small balls.
Gradually stir the warm water into the rice flour and knead into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces, flatten each into a cup, wrap around a sesame ball, and roll smooth.
Simmer the water, ginger, and brown sugar in a saucepan for 10 minutes to make the syrup.
Bring a separate pot of water to a boil and add the tangyuan, stirring gently so they don't stick.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until they float, then simmer 1 minute more.
Transfer the tangyuan to bowls and ladle the hot ginger syrup over them.

recipes.title: Taro Fish
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Peel and chop taro into 1-inch chunks. Steam until soft.
Meanwhile soak black beans in a little water.
Mash taro with the vegetable stock powder.
Place 2 sheets of nori on the bench, moistening one to join them together.
Place the mashed taro mixture in the centre of the sheets and roll the nori sheets over the top.
Cut the nori at one end to resemble fish fins.
Slice green pepper, ginger and spring onions into thin strips and stir fry for a few minutes.
Add the Shaoxing wine and black beans.
Make cuts halfway through the taro fish at about 1 inch intervals and pour the sauce over it.
Serve on a platter.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Tater Tot Casserole
recipes.description: Tater tot casserole is another easy and tasty casserole.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 can cream of mushroom soup or cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Brown hamburger and drain.
Mix in cream of mushroom or cream of chicken soup.
Put mixture in casserole dish and cover the top with one layer of tater tots.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour or until done.

recipes.notes: Try adding peas or other vegetables. A can of cheddar cheese soup is also a great way to make a meaty, cheesy casserole! Shortly before the dish is ready, sprinkle the top with some grated cheddar cheese also. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Tattie Scones
recipes.description: Tattie scones, also called potato scones or potato bread, are a regional variant of the savoury "griddle scone" which is especially popular in Scotland. Many variations of recipe exist, however they generally include liberal quantities of boiled Tatties (potatoes) and salt.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Cook potatoes in salted boiling water until tender, drain them well and put them back into the hot pot to dry them out a bit.
Mash them well with lots of butter and salt and pepper, but no milk or other liquid. Let them cool.
When the potatoes are cold, stir in flour and a little more melted butter to make a smooth dough. Roll out to a thickness of about 5 mm, and cut into 3-inch (7.5 cm) wedges.
Cook in a lightly-buttered frying pan until golden, about 1–2 minutes a side.
Serve the potato scones right away with cold butter to spread on top, or store them in the fridge until you want to use them, reheating them in a well-buttered frying pan.
Some people are content to eat them cold with butter, or heat them in a toaster for buttering. They also freeze very, very well.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Tea Eggs
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Bring water and spices to a boil.
Add eggs, and boil for 3 minutes.
Remove eggs from the liquid and roll them gently on a hard surface to crack the shell all over.
Return the eggs to the pot of liquid, reduce to a simmer, and simmer for 1 hour.
Reduce to low heat and allow eggs to sit in brine until served.

recipes.photoCredit: Daniela Eftimova / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tea_eggs_1.jpg

recipes.title: Tekka (Japanese Root Vegetables in Miso)
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Heat a pan and pour in the sesame oil.
Add the greater burdock root, and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Add the carrots and the lotus root and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Add miso and ginger. Turn down the heat and allow to cook over a low heat for 4 hours.
Stir frequently until all water has evaporated and until the mixture appears dry and dark.
Allow to cool and keep in a glass jar.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Tempura
recipes.description: Tempura is one of the fried foods of Japan. Various meats, fish, and vegetables are dipped in batter and then deep fried until lightly golden.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Oil for deep-frying (peanut oil is best)

steps.text: Heat oil in a deep pan to 340–350°F (~171–176°C).
Beat the egg in a bowl and add ice cold water. Warmer water will produce a sticky batter and more oily tempura.
Add flour and mix lightly. Do not overmix batter—a few lumps actually improve the result, adding crispiness.
Dip meat or vegetables briefly in the batter, and fry until brown.
Remove from the oil and drain.
Serve hot.

recipes.notes: If using shrimp, score them a few times crosswise on the underside, to prevent them from curling up during deep frying. Alternatively, skewer them before cooking. Remove the skewers before serving. You may also wish to include 1 tablespoon of cornstarch in the batter. Serve over white rice garnished with black sesame seeds, in a bowl of udon noodle soup, or in a bowl of soba noodle soup. Serving in soup will make the cooked batter get mushy, of course. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Teriyaki Salmon
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 4 ea. (24 ounces) wild salmon filets with skin, pin bones removed

steps.text: Combine all ingredients except salmon in a blender until smooth. Pour into a plastic bag and add salmon. Toss to coat, seal, removing as much air as possible, and refrigerate up to 4 hours.
Remove salmon from marinade and pat dry with paper towels. Brush all sides with oil.
Preheat 4 1/2 pounds charcoal in starter. Once hot, disperse evenly around bottom of grill. Reapply grate and once hot, swab with towel.
Add salmon to hottest part of grill skin side up, and cook 3–5 minutes per side for medium, rotating 90 degrees halfway to make grill marks.
Remove to a plate and cover tightly with aluminum foil. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Teriyaki Sauce
recipes.description: The word teriyaki is a combination of two Japanese words, teri, "luster", and yaki, "to grill or broil". The mirin in the sauce gives a good luster to meat as it is cooked. Traditionally it was used with fish. It can also be used as a marinade for pre-cooked meat and poultry, as well as a delicious baste for items on the grill or rotisserie.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Mix everything in a 1-quart pot over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Use sauce to marinate some raw meat or vegetables overnight in the refrigerator.

recipes.notes: As given, this sauce is thin. Boil 1/2 tsp cornstarch or potato starch or kuzu root starch (for Japanese authenticity) into it if you wish to thicken it. Pineapple juice might be a reasonable mirin substitute. Lime juice may also be added for a tart flavor. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Texas Brisket Sandwiches
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 ea. (8 pounds) beef brisket, trimmed to 1/4 inch of fat

steps.text: Combine hot sauce, molasses, vinegar, and 1/4 cup mustard. Pour into a spray bottle and set aside.
Coat brisket with 1/2 cup of the mustard. Set aside.
Combine seasonings and salt. Press mixture into both sides of brisket. Refrigerate overnight.
The next day, heat up a smoker to 200°F with the mesquite chunks. Add brisket and cook 9 hours, spraying every 3 hours with vinegar mixture, and changing wood as needed to keep temperature at 200°F.
Remove brisket from smoker and let rest 1/2 hour. Separate along the fat line and slice thinly across the grain.
Finely chop slices and toss with remaining vinegar mixture. Place 1/9 into each bun and serve warm.

recipes.notes: If you don't have a smoker, just preheat your oven to 190°F. Place 3/4 cup soaked mesquite chips in the bottom of a roasting pan and add a rack and your rubbed brisket. Cover tightly with foil and cook the same. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Texas Easy Chili
recipes.description: Texas easy chili is a chili powder and tomato juice based sauce combined with cubed or ground beef. Chili originated in Texas in the 1800s. There are many variations of chili. This version does not contain beans.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 3 pounds chuck roast or ground beef, cubed or formed into small meatballs

steps.text: Cut chuck roast into bite-size pieces or form ground beef into small meatballs (1 inch / 25 mm in size).
Fry beef in cooking oil until outside is browned.
Add minced garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Combine chili powder, flour, oregano and cumin in bowl and mix well. Sprinkle mixture over cooking beef and stir until beef is well coated with spice mixture. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato juice and bullion cubes. Stir for about 15 seconds.
Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and add salt and black pepper to taste.

recipes.notes: Cool and refrigerate overnight to develop flavors (if you can wait; if not, enjoy). Heat and serve in bowls with 1 tablespoon of lime juice and 1 tablespoon of sour cream added to top. Serve with cornbread or sourdough bread. For a cool treat, spoon a tablespoon of ranch dressing on top of your chili, along with some cheese! (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Texas Style Barbecue Ribs
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 slabs St. Louis style pork ribs

steps.text: Combine all Mop ingredients and place in a spray bottle. Combine all Rub ingredients and massage into pork. Refrigerate pork overnight.
The next day, place hickory chunks into the firebox of a smoker. Heat to 225°F.
Place ribs in smoker and cook, spraying with Mop often.
Grill ribs on high, turning often, spraying grilled side every time it's turned, until well browned on both sides.
Remove and let rest 7 minutes.
Slice into one rib portions and place in a large stainless steel bowl. Pour in about 1/2 cup of Mop and toss to coat ribs. Serve warm.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Edo de Roo / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Spareribs_20160506_182617113.jpg

recipes.title: Texas Style Chicken Fried Steak
recipes.description: If you've ever been in Texas and tried one of their chicken-fried steaks, you'll know that they are amazing! They're crispy on the outside, tender, smoky, and peppery with a little heat on the inside and smothered in a rich cream gravy. It's just amazing.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/4 cup freshly ground black pepper, divided
1 cup whole milk, combined with 1/4 cup heavy cream

steps.text: Season steaks with salt and 2 tbsp freshly ground black pepper.
In a pie plate, combine eggs with paprika and cayenne. Dip steaks into egg mixture.
In another pie plate, place some all-purpose flour. Dredge battered steaks with flour.
Move to a cooling rack and let rest 10–15 minutes. Wash this once you start frying, or get a clean one.
Heat a 12 inch cast-iron skillet over medium high heat. Once hot, pour in 2 tbsp drippings. Add steaks in a triangle formation around the edges of the pan. Fry for 4 minutes per side.
Remove steaks from pan and drain on a cooling rack above a sheet pan. Keep steaks warm in a 250°F oven.
Add remaining drippings and 3 tbsp flour. Whisk continuously until blonde color is achieved.
Add chicken broth and deglaze pan. Bring to a boil over medium heat until reduced by 3/4.
Add milk mixture and remaining black pepper. Keep over medium heat until gravy coats back of spoon.
Remove steaks to serving platters and drizzle with gravy. Serve warm.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Three Bean Confetti Salad
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (12 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (8 3/4 oz) whole kernel corn, drained
1 can (14 1/2 oz) diced tomatoes with roasted garlic, undrained

steps.text: In a bowl, mix together beans, corn, tomatoes, Italian salad dressing, Italian seasoning and pepper.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Three Sisters Soup
recipes.description: Three sisters soup is a classic Indigenous recipe steeped in the folklore of the three staples of Indigenous cultures in North America: corn, squash, and beans. This hearty and delicious soup pays homage to the rich heritage and agricultural traditions of Indigenous communities. It is wonderful on its own or served with freshly baked Indigenous bread.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 cups drained canned white or yellow hominy corn (can be substituted with regular corn)
2 cups trimmed and snapped fresh green beans
2 cups peeled and cubed butternut squash
1 1/2 cups white or yellow potatoes, peeled and diced (for a sweeter variation, you can use sweet potatoes)

steps.text: In a large pot, combine the hominy, green beans, squash, and potatoes.
Add water and chicken bouillon.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer until the vegetables are soft (approximately 10 minutes).
In a separate pan, melt the butter and whisk in the flour. Stir the mixture into the soup.
Increase heat to medium and cook until the soup thickens (approximately 5 minutes).
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve your delicious three sisters soup. Garnish with fresh herbs or Indigenous spices for added flavor.

recipes.notes: To enhance the Indigenous flavors, consider using traditional Indigenous spices or herbs. Feel free to adjust the vegetable quantities to your preference. See Three Sisters Stew for another variation. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Three Sisters Stew
recipes.description: Three sisters stew is a traditional and contemporary Native American dish. The dish includes the three sister foods of maize, beans, and squash, which are prevalent in many Native American diets. The three traditional ingredients are made together because of farming methods that often included all three crops in the same field with an interdependent relationship.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 ea. (2 lb) small pumpkin or butternut or carnival squash
1/2 medium green or red bell pepper, cut into short, narrow strips
1 can (14–16 ounces) diced tomatoes, with liquid
2 cups cooked or canned pinto beans
2 cups corn kernels (from 2 large or medium ears)
1 cup water or homemade vegetable stock
1–2 fresh hot chiles, seeded and minced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Cut the pumpkin or squash in half lengthwise and remove the seeds and fibers. Cover with aluminum foil and place the halves, cut side up, in a foil-lined shallow baking pan.

Bake for 40–50 minutes, or until easily pierced with a knife but still firm (if using squash, prepare the same way). When cool enough to handle, scoop out the pulp, and cut into large dice. Set aside until needed.
Heat the oil in a soup pot. Add the onion and sauté over medium-low heat until translucent. Add the garlic and continue to sauté until the onion is golden.

Add the pumpkin and all the remaining ingredients except the last 2 and bring to a simmer. Simmer gently, covered, until all the vegetables are tender, about 20–25 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

If time allows, let the stew stand for 1–2 hours before serving, then heat through as needed. Just before serving, stir in the cilantro. The stew should be thick and very moist but not soupy; add additional stock or water if needed. Serve in shallow bowls.

recipes.notes: The protein content of the stew can be increased by adding a cup of quinoa and/or a pound of cooked turkey meat, cut into bite-size pieces. See Three Sisters Soup for another variation. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Tinga de Pollo Tostadas
recipes.description: Shredded chicken stewed in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce from Puebla, piled onto crisp tostadas with beans, crema, and fresh toppings.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
2 to 3 chipotle chiles in adobo, plus 1 tbsp adobo sauce

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the salted water for 20 minutes until cooked through, then cool and shred, reserving 1/2 cup of the broth.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, adobo sauce, and reserved broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the chipotle sauce and oregano and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer 5 minutes more until the sauce clings to the meat; season with salt.
Spread each tostada with refried beans and top with the tinga.
Finish with lettuce, crema, queso fresco, and avocado and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Toad in the Hole
recipes.description: Toad in the hole is a baked Yorkshire pudding or thick pastry round, with sausages or pieces of meat in it. This recipe is for a sausage toad. A further variation is made using fine chopped potatoes in a pudding-basin with a lump of meat in the centre, and then boiling or steaming.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Bake the sausages with the oil in a roasting pan for 10 minutes. This cooks the sausages and allows the pan to heat up.
Add batter to the hot pan. The oil should sizzle as the cold batter is added to the pan.

Bake in the oven for about 40–45 minutes. The oven door must not be opened while the batter is baking; once the crust has risen and browned, you can open the oven. The outside should be crispy and the inside should be firm.
Remove and serve hot.

recipes.notes: Toad in the hole is commonly served with mashed potato, vegetables and gravy, or brown sauce. Some people will add a splash of cold water to the batter before putting in the oven. Putting the pan on the (turned-on) stove/hob can help keep the oil hot while adding the batter. However, this can lead to hot oil splatter, so caution is advised; as long as the dish is quickly returned to the hot oven, the stovetop isn't necessary to achieve a good rise. Ideally use a metal pan. Make the Yorkshire pudding batter ahead of time and store in the fridge to allow the flour to properly hydrate. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Robert Gibert / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Toad_in_the_hole.jpg

recipes.title: Tonkatsu
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 pork cutlets (boneless pork loin chop), about 1 cm thick

steps.text: Sauce: Combine the soy sauce, sugar, Worcestershire, and ketchup. Beat with fork until consistent.
If desired, chill sauce for a half hour to thicken.
Tonkatsu: Pound pork with meat mallet until thin, perhaps 1/4 inch (a little more than 0.5 cm) thick. To reduce splatter you should put the meat in an open ziplock bag.
Season pounded cutlets with salt and pepper on each side.
Put beaten egg, flour, and bread crumbs in separate shallow bowls.
Place pork in the flour, then egg, then crumbs (in that order) so that it is completely coated with each.
Heat oil in a frying pan to about 1/2 inch or 1.25 cm deep. Drop in crumbs to test when the oil is ready—the crumbs should float and sizzle.
Fry pork until deep golden or golden brown, most likely a for a few minutes on either side.
With a sharp knife cut pork into strips.
Serve with Japanese short grain rice and thinly shredded cabbage.

recipes.notes: Pork can be substituted by chicken or beef. Finished tonkatsu can be served as a topping to Japanese curry or simmered with egg and broth and served over rice as katsudon. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
