recipes.photoCredit: yoppy from Tonkatsu Restaurant Houraitei in Shibuya, Tokyo / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tonkatsu_by_yoppy_in_Shibuya,_Tokyo.jpg

recipes.title: Tonkotsu Ramen
recipes.description: Tonkotsu ramen is a dish of ramen noodles served in rich and fatty pork broth usually garnished with a variation of toppings (most of the time pork cutlets, green onions, and hard-boiled eggs split in two). There are many variations to this recipe. Some people add some chicken bones or beef bones to create a unique combination of flavors.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 1/2 tbsp fresh grated ginger or 2 tsp prepackaged ginger paste
500 grams all-purpose flour or medium-strength flour

steps.text: Marinated eggs: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. If desired, use a small thumb tack to prick a pin hole in the base of every egg, then add eggs to the pot. The water should cover the eggs.
Wait for the water to come back to a full boil, then cook for 7–9 minutes. 9 minutes will give you a fully hard boiled egg, while 7 minutes makes a jammier egg.
Drain the pot and eggs and plunge the eggs in ice water to stop the cooking. This also makes the shells a bit easier to peel.

In a small pot, sauté pork, garlic, onions, and ginger until slightly browned. Add soy sauce, cooking alcohol, sugar, and water, and simmer for 10 minutes until pork is cooked through and flavors meld. Remove from stove.

Remove pork to eat separately. Pour everything else into a bowl large enough to hold marinade and eggs. Carefully, peel the eggs, and place in marinade. Try to make sure the marinade covers all of the eggs. If not, try transferring the sauce into a large ziplock bag, and place the eggs in the bag and seal.
Place the bag in a bowl, and put everything in the refrigerator overnight or at least for a few hours.
Soup: Using a butcher knife, separate off the pork hock bones.
Rinse well in running water to wash off the blood. Boil in large pot for 15 minutes and make sure you barely cover the bones with the water.
Skim off as much scum/foam as much possible as it forms.
Drain in colander and use a brush to remove any bloody meat.
Use a saw and cut halfway down the center of the bones. Then use hammer to break bone.
The bones will be filled with marrow. Simmer for several hours until the marrow dissolves out from the bones.
Scum will form at the start. Carefully skim the scum off. Maintain a low boil over medium heat.
After scum has stopped forming, simmer for 6 hours or more. Add more water if the water level drops.

2 hours after the pork bones have started simmering, the soup should become progressively white and cloudy. If tasted at this stage, the soup will not taste good since it will still have a raw flavor.
After the soup has simmered for 6 hours, the inside of the bones should be empty and the soup should have a rich smell just like a ramen place.

Chashu: Brown the meat in a pan and then simmer in a pot for 2 hours in a sauce made from the remaining ingredients. Allow to cool in the pot. The char siu should be a nice amber color. Slice with care since it will be very tender and tend to fall apart.
Noodles: Mix the flour and kansui together, then add the water. It may feel as if the amount of water is insufficient—this is normal.
Mix in bowl until a mealy consistency is achieved. The dough will be very stiff. Use you body weight to form the dough into a ball.
Transfer to kneading surface and knead. Knead vigorously for 10 minutes. It is okay if the dough cracks or does not knead together well.
Form into ball, cover with plastic wrap and allow to rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. Make sure that the dough does not dry out.

After the dough has rested, roll the dough out with a rolling pin to a thickness of 5 mm and then insert into pasta machine. Start out with the highest thickness and then continue on the lower settings until the desired thickness is achieved. If a pasta machine is not used, roll out the dough to the desired thickness with the rolling pin. Take into account that the noodles will expand 1.3 times when boiled.
The dough will not be that sticky, so a small amount of flour or potato (or corn) starch is sufficient for flouring.
A wooden box is best for storing the noodles, but if one is not available, use a metal tray lined with wax paper (to prevent sticking) and store in the refrigerator.

Bring a pot of water to a boil, and add the noodles. Cook the noodles to each person’s preference, then drain. For people who like curly noodles, firmly squeeze the noodles until the desired effect is achieved.
Warm a large soup bowl, and add the drained noodles. Add broth, then top with char siu and marinated egg. Add salt for flavor—use sparingly at first and then add more if desired.

recipes.notes: Kansui is a Japanese mixture of alkaline salts. Try the Koon Chun brand, which comes in a clear glass bottle labeled “potassium carbonate & sodium bi-carbonate solution”. The UPC is 0-20717-80230-8. Any leftover char siu can be eaten with beer. If you ever have trouble slicing soft pork, chill the whole piece in the refrigerator until cold, and it makes slicing easier. Reheating is easy, in either the microwave or oven, even stove top. Make sure you keep up on scooping out the foamy gunk from the broth—you don't want all that stuff all over your ramen. Don't be afraid to experiment with different types and balances of garnishes! (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Guilhem Vellut from Paris, France / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tonkotsu_Ramen_Special,_Hakata_Choten,_Paris_001.jpg

recipes.title: Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: Tortilla soup is a traditional southwestern dish and an excellent way to finish tortillas that have begun to go stale. It works well as a soup before a meal or as the meal itself. Turkey or pork may be used in place of chicken. Alternative garnishes, such as avocado and green onions, also work well.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro or 1 teaspoon dried cilantro
1 jalapeno, seeded and diced, or 1/2 teaspoon dried cayenne pepper (optional, Tabasco sauce can be added to individual bowls to adjust heat to taste)
Grated Monterey Jack or other Mexican cheeses

steps.text: Variation I – Slow cooker: Place oil, chopped onion, minced garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, cilantro, chicken, stock, salt, pepper, and jalapeño/red pepper in a crock pot. Cook on low for 6–9 hours.
When chicken is cooked, remove from soup, coarsely chop, and return to soup.
Serve soup in individual bowls with chips, cheese and olives to garnish.
Variation II – Stovetop: Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil prior to adding other ingredients.
Simmer on medium heat until chicken is cooked thoroughly and otherwise follow slow cooker directions.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Tres Leches Cake I
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp cream of tartar (optional but used for stabilizing the egg whites; increasing their heat tolerance and volume)

steps.text: Sponge cake: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour cake pan.
Using a standing mixer with the whisk attachment, whip egg whites until frothy: Slowly bring the mixer to the fastest speed, stopping for a minute on each speed.
Slowly beat in the sugar and vanilla.
Mix in the egg yolks, and finally the flour.
Transfer batter to prepared cake pan, and bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven.
Remove cake and let cool to room temperature. Poke several holes in the cake.
Milk mixture: Combine the condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream, and vanilla.
Heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly. The idea is just to bring all the flavors together, so don’t overheat the milk.
Let the milk mixture cool to room temperature.
Slowly pour the milk mixture over the cake. Since you greased the cake pan the milk will flow around and under the cake. The cake will absorb most of the milk.
Meringue: Place the egg whites in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment.
Slowly bring the mixer to the fastest speed stopping for a minute or so on each speed.
Add the cream of tartar.
Slowly beat in the granulated sugar.
Spread the meringue on top of the cake.
Use a blowtorch or the oven broiler to gently toast the meringue. Once the meringue starts to change color you have a few seconds before it burns, so stay alert.

recipes.notes: It is very important to separate the eggs correctly when making the meringue. If the yolk breaks and your egg whites contain drops of yolk, the meringue will not form correctly. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Tri-Colored Autumn Rice Balls
recipes.description: Tri-colored autumn rice balls (san-shoku ohagi) is a simple a tea sweet, which was at one time served during the autumn equinox celebration. The name comes from a type of bush clover that only blooms in the fall. Serve these rice balls with your finest cup of tea.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/4 cup toasted black sesame seeds, lightly crushed
1 cup smooth Japanese bean paste (koshi-an), chilled
1/2 cup roasted soybean powder (kinako) or toasted ground pecans

steps.text: Mix sesame seeds and sugar in a small bowl.
Moisten your hands with water and divide warm rice into 12 equal portions.
Shape 4 portions into balls. Moisten a clean dish towel and squeeze it dry.
Place 2 1/2 tablespoons bean paste on towel; pat into a 4-inch circle.
Place 1 rice ball in the centre of the bean paste circle and use towel to mould bean paste around the rice ball.
Repeat this 3 more times, using another 1/2 cup of bean paste and the other 3 rice balls.
Place these on a nice serving tray. Flatten the remaining eight rice portions.
Form the remaining bean paste into 8 balls (about 2 teaspoons per ball). Place a bean paste ball in the centre of each piece of flattened rice and shape the rice around it.
Mould these stuffed rice balls into oval shapes. Roll 4 ovals in the sesame-sugar mixture. Roll the other 4 balls in the roasted soybean powder. Add these to the serving tray.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: 脇山航 / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E5%B0%8F%E6%96%99%E7%90%86%E3%83%90%E3%83%AB%E3%81%95%E3%81%8F%E3%82%89_%E7%89%B9%E8%A3%BD%E3%81%8A%E3%81%AB%E3%81%8E%E3%82%8A.jpg

recipes.title: Trifle
recipes.description: Trifle, also commonly known as sherry trifle, is a traditional layered dessert in many countries. It can be prepared with or without alcohol, and the nonalcoholic version is popular with children.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 swiss roll or similar sponge cake
1 packet/sachet fruit-flavoured jelly (can be found under the brand names "Quick-Jel" or "Jell-O")
Hundreds and thousands, sprinkles, or other sweet topping (optional)

steps.text: Slice the Swiss roll approximately 3/4-inch (2 cm) thick, and line the base of a Pyrex casserole dish with it.
Pour sherry over the swiss roll.
Drain the peaches, keeping the juice/syrup aside and then arrange the peaches over the swiss roll.
Prepare the jelly as per the instructions, you may wish to use the syrup from the peaches for this. Pour the jelly into the casserole dish and allow to set in the fridge.
Make the custard, again as per the instructions (use fresh or powdered as opposed to canned). Allow this to cool to lukewarm, and pour into the casserole. Allow this to set in the fridge.
Whip the cream for the top of the trifle and spread it over the custard. Garnish with hundreds and thousands, sprinkles, or other cake decorations.
Serve!

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Tuna Noodle Casserole
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 cans (drained) or pouches (12 ounces each) tuna
4 cups hot, cooked medium egg noodles
2 cans (21 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
1/4–1 teaspoon Texas Pete or other hot sauce (optional)
3–4 ounces cheese, shredded or sliced to cover casserole

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Shred tuna and stir into 3-quart casserole with milk, noodles, peas, and soup. Add onions and hot sauce if desired.
Bake until hot, about 25–30 minutes.
Remove from oven, and top with bread crumbs mixed with butter or with cheese.
Bake another 5 minutes.

recipes.notes: Replace half of mushroom soup with cream of celery. Try replacing breadcrumbs with crushed potato chips. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: B.D.'s world / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tuna_Casserole2.jpg

recipes.title: Twice-Baked Potatoes I
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Vegetable oil to rub on potato skins
A pinch of ground black pepper

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Rub potato skins with vegetable oil to ensure crispness.
Bake potatoes for 1 hour until done.
Carefully remove potatoes from oven and cool for 10 minutes.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise and scoop out pulp with a small spoon, leaving only a potato shell.
Mash potato pulp with a fork until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients until well combined. It is better if the mixture is a bit stiff, rather than entirely wet. Adjust the amount of milk accordingly.
Spoon (or pipe) the mixture into the empty potato shells.
If desired, top the potatoes with bell pepper, onions, and/or bacon.
Increase oven setting to broil.
Broil potatoes 10 or 15 minutes until spotty brown and crisp.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Ume-shu (Japanese Plum Juice)
recipes.description: Ume juice is extracted by preserving the fruits in sugar. It tastes sweet, smooth, and acidic, and is a refreshing drink, often enjoyed in the summer. The taste and aroma of ume-shu can appeal to even those people who normally dislike the taste of alcohol.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Wash plums and wipe dry.
Cram plums tightly into container with rock sugar. Add liquor if using.
Pour honey into container on top of ume.
Seal container, and leave in a cool, dark place until the plums are shriveled and leathery.
Remove fruit from container.
To drink, dilute the plum liquid with two times as much water.

recipes.notes: Keep in a cool place during summer. (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Unknown author / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Umeshu_on_the_rocks.jpg

recipes.title: Upma (Indian Semolina Porridge)
recipes.description: Upma is a popular South Indian dish made from semolina. Several variations of the dish exist including the use of different varieties of ground wheat, rice and even bread. A simple upma or uppittu takes just about 10 minutes to prepare. It uses very little oil/butter, making it one of the most popular, healthy and filling breakfasts in South India.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1 cup mixed finely-chopped vegetables such as onion, carrots, lima beans, potatoes, capsicum, tomatoes, peas, etc.

steps.text: In a heated saucepan, lightly toast semolina until it changes to a light brown color and gives out a roasted smell. Pour it out onto a dry plate and allow to cool.

To the same pan add 1/2 tbsp oil/ghee and allow it to heat up (about 1 minute). Now add all the seasoning ingredients, starting first with mustard seeds, cumin, black gram, peanuts, and cashews in that order. Wait for the mustard seeds to crackle and then add asafoetida and curry leaves.

Add the chopped ginger, green chillies, and onions. Sauté for 1 minute, then add the remaining veggies and 1 tbsp coconut. Sauté again for about 1 minute, then add 1 1/2 cups of water and salt. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer over medium heat, and cover to let the veggies cook for a few minutes.
After the veggies are cooked, remove cover and stir in the sugar. Lower the heat further and start folding in the roasted and cooled semolina slowly while stirring constantly.
Cover and let it cook for a few minutes.
Garnish with the remaining coconut and chopped coriander leaves.

recipes.notes: Coat the serving spoon with a little bit of the remaining oil/ghee before serving to prevent the dish from sticking to the spoon and give the dish a lustre! To save time, try using the pre-roasted semolina from any Indian grocery store. Cooking veggies like carrots, lima beans, peas, potatoes, etc. separately in the microwave saves time! A general rule of thumb on how much veggies to add is 1:1 ratio of semolina to veggies Try making upma with just one vegetable to bring out the taste of each veggie. Goes well with coconut chutney and sambhar (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Thamizhpparithi Maari / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_photo_of_Upma.jpg

recipes.title: Venison Jerky
recipes.description: Thin strips of venison seasoned and slowly dried, a preservation method practiced by Indigenous hunters across North America for millennia.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 2 lb lean venison roast, trimmed of all fat
1 tbsp maple syrup or brown sugar (optional)

steps.text: Freeze the venison for 1 hour so it is firm and easier to slice.
Cut the meat with the grain into strips 1/4 inch thick.
Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, maple syrup, and water and toss the strips to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 175°F (80°C) and set wire racks over foil-lined baking sheets.
Pat the strips dry and lay them in a single layer on the racks without touching.
Dry in the oven with the door propped open slightly for 4–5 hours, until the jerky bends and cracks but does not snap.
Cool completely and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.photoCredit: Larry Jacobsen from Cheyenne Wyoming / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jerky_(1).jpg

recipes.title: Versunkener Apfelkuchen (Sunken Apple Cake)
recipes.description: A simple buttery sponge cake baked with scored apple halves that sink into the batter as it bakes.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp unsalted butter, softened
4 small apples, peeled, halved and cored

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Cut several shallow parallel slits into the rounded side of each apple half and brush with lemon juice.
Beat the butter, sugar, vanilla and lemon zest until light and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together and fold into the batter alternately with the milk.
Spread the batter into the pan and press the apple halves, scored side up, lightly into the surface.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer inserted in the cake comes out clean.
Brush the warm apples with apricot jam, let cool in the pan, then dust with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.title: Victoria Sandwich
recipes.description: The Victoria sandwich (also known as the Victoria sponge) is a Victorian cake that is popular in the UK.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 170 g (2/3 cup or 6 oz) self-raising flour
170 g (2/3 cup or 6 oz) unsalted butter or margarine
170 g (2/3 cup or 6 oz) caster sugar

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F or Gas Mark 6).
Cream the butter and sugar into a bowl and mix with a wooden spoon until softened.
Add the 3 eggs, the vanilla essence, and the flour and mix until smooth.
Divide the mixture between the two greased cake pans.
Bake in the oven for 20–30 minutes (10–15 in a fan-assisted oven) until firm to the touch.
Leave to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Turn one cake upside down and spread jam and whipped cream over it. Then, place the second cake on top.
Cut into wedges, and serve.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)

recipes.title: Waldorf Salad
recipes.description: Waldorf salad was created by Oscar Tschirky in 1896 at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel, New York, New York, in the United States of America.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 80 g (1/3 cup or 3 oz) chopped walnuts
80 g (1/3 cup or 3 oz) chopped celery

steps.text: Slice the apples into wedges, and place in a bowl.
Pour lemon juice on the apple wedges, and ensure a light coating to prevent browning.
Plump the raisins by placing them in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain well.
Mix celery, raisins, and walnuts into the bowl of apple wedges.
Mix the mayonnaise and sugar together, then pour into the apple mixture, ensuring a light coating on all items.
Chill for at least 30 minutes
Place 3 lettuce leaves on a large plate and three on another, place half of the mixture on each set of leaves, and sprinkle 5 cherries on each salad.
Serve

recipes.notes: Though the original salad only used apples, celery and mayonnaise; walnuts mixed in have become an integral part of the modern version of the salad and cherries are only used as a sweet addition to further the contrasts within the salad. Instead of raisins, try using grapes to create the same sort of taste but more wholly and not as rich. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Wampanoag Clambake in a Pot
recipes.description: The coastal New England appanaug, a feast of shellfish, corn, and potatoes steamed over seaweed, adapted to a large stockpot.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 lb smoked sausage or linguiça, cut into chunks (optional)
4 lb littleneck or steamer clams, scrubbed
2 large handfuls of rinsed rockweed seaweed (optional)

steps.text: Place the potatoes, onions, and sausage in the bottom of a very large stockpot with the water.
Cover with the seaweed, if using, which adds steam and ocean flavor.
Bring to a boil over high heat, cover tightly, and steam for 15 minutes.
Add the corn on top, cover, and steam 5 minutes more.
Add the clams and mussels, cover, and steam for 8–10 minutes until the shells open; discard any that stay closed.
Lift everything onto a large platter or newspaper-covered table.
Serve with melted butter, lemon wedges, and the pot broth for dipping.

recipes.title: Wampanoag Cranberry Sauce
recipes.description: Cranberries, called sasumuneash by the Wampanoag, simmered with maple syrup into a tart-sweet sauce—a native fruit long used for food and medicine in New England.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Combine the maple syrup, water, orange peel, and salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add the cranberries and return to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most of the berries have burst.
Remove the orange peel and let the sauce cool; it will thicken as it stands.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.

recipes.photoCredit: Veganbaking.net from USA / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cranberry_Sauce_(3617909597).jpg

recipes.title: Warm Black Pudding and Apple Salad
recipes.description: Crisp slices of Irish black pudding and caramelized apple over peppery greens with a mustard-cider dressing.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 8 oz black pudding, cut into 1/2-inch slices
2 crisp apples, cored and cut into wedges
5 oz mixed salad leaves or watercress

steps.text: Whisk the dressing ingredients together in a small bowl.
Melt half the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat, add the apple wedges, sprinkle with sugar, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden; remove.
Add the remaining butter to the pan and fry the black pudding slices for 2 minutes per side until crisp at the edges.
Toss the salad leaves with most of the dressing and divide among plates.
Top with the warm apple and black pudding, drizzle with the remaining dressing, and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Welsh Cakes
recipes.description: Welsh cakes (Welsh: picau ar y maen) are a popular cake in Wales that are similar to scones and Cornish Heavy cakes.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 450 g (2 cups or 1 lb) plain flour
170 g (3/4 cup or 6 oz) castor sugar
85 g (3 oz) currants, sultanas, raisins or other dried fruit

steps.text: In a large mixing bowl, sift the flour then rub together with the butter and salt until mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Mix in sugar and dried fruit.
Add eggs one at a time, beating together until mixture forms a thick dough. If dough will not form, add a small amount of milk (i.e. a tablespoon).
Knead for two to three minutes until dough becomes cohesive and slightly elastic.
Roll dough out on a flat surface.
Cut 2–3-inch circles from the dough and fry
Preheat a griddle on high than lower it to medium-low (this is important to stop burning)
Griddle 2-4 minutes on each side until golden brown.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Welsh Fruit Bread (Bara Brith) I
recipes.description: Bara brith, sometimes known as "speckled bread" (the literal meaning of the original Welsh-language name), is a fruit bread which originated in Wales. It is traditionally made with raisins, Zante currants and candied peel. In Wales the fruit is traditionally soaked overnight in cold tea.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 oz (50 g) brown sugar, plus 1 teaspoon
2 lb (900 g) loaf tin, well greased

steps.text: Warm the milk in a small pan until hand-hot. Put it into a bowl with 1 teaspoon of sugar and the yeast. Leave it in a warm place for about 15 minutes until a froth appears.

Sift the flour and place in a large bowl with 2 oz (50 g) sugar and the salt. Rub the fat into the flour until it resembles fine breadcrumbs, then stir in the mixed spice. Add the egg and frothed yeast. Mix to a dough in the bowl before turning it out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic. Place back into a bowl and cover with plastic film or a damp cloth. Leave it to rise in a warm place for about 90 minutes.
After it has been left to stand, 'knock down' the dough and knead again, adding the fruit slowly.
Place into a bread tin and put the tin into an oiled plastic bag. Leave to rise for about 35–40 minutes and preheat the oven to gas mark 5, 190°C (375°F).
When the dough has risen and springs back when pressed, take the tin out of the bag and bake in the centre of the oven for about 30 minutes.
Cover the top of the loaf tin with aluminium foil to stop it burning and bake for another 30 minutes.
Take out of the oven and tap the bottom of the loaf, which should sound hollow—if not, bake it for another 5 minutes.
Brush the honey onto the top of the loaf and cool it on a wire rack. Slice it thinly and serve buttered.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: Matthew R Dunn / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bara_Brith.jpg

recipes.title: Welsh Rarebit
recipes.description: There is no small amount of disagreement about what constitutes Welsh Rarebit. Many contend that it is just cheese on toast. At the other end of the spectrum are a variety of recipes in which the bread is steeped in beer or floated in soup.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 2 fl oz (60 ml) beer such as porter (Guinness will do)

steps.text: In a medium saucepan over low heat, melt the butter and whisk in the flour.
Cook, whisking constantly for 2–3 minutes, being careful not to brown the flour.
Whisk in mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Add beer and whisk to combine.
Pour in cream and whisk until well combined and smooth.
Gradually add cheese, stirring constantly, until cheese melts and sauce is smooth; this will take 4–5 minutes.
Pour over toast and serve immediately.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: stef yau / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Welsh_Rarebit.jpg

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Irish Soda Bread
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C / gasmark 3).
Use cooking spray or grease and then lightly flour a 9x5x3-inch baking pan.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Form a cavity in the middle.
Pour in the buttermilk.
Mix until just moistened. Too much mixing will make it tough.
Gently shape the dough to fit pan.
Cut the top at least three times with a knife.
Bake for 65–70 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the bread comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack.
Wrap in tea-towel or foil several hours or overnight for best flavor.

recipes.notes: If you're in a hurry, bake at 375°F for 35–40 minutes. Buttermilk could be substituted with a tablespoon of lemon juice or vinegar in milk. "Baker's Secret" is a brand of cooking spray that includes the flour. (Prep/cook times are estimates.)
recipes.photoCredit: w:en:User:Canterbury Tail / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ben_W_Bell_Soda_Bread_Farl_05_June_2007.jpg

recipes.title: Wild Rice with Cranberries and Hazelnuts
recipes.description: Nutty Great Lakes wild rice tossed with dried cranberries, toasted hazelnuts, and green onions, a festive side drawing on Anishinaabe foods.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Bring the wild rice, water, and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 45–50 minutes until the grains are tender and many have split; drain well.
While still warm, toss the rice with the oil and dried cranberries so the berries plump.
Whisk the maple syrup and vinegar together and pour over the rice.
Fold in the hazelnuts and green onions and season with pepper and more salt to taste.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Wojapi (Plains Berry Sauce)
recipes.description: A thick, naturally sweet berry sauce made by the Lakota and other Plains nations, traditionally from chokecherries and served warm with fry bread.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 4 cups mixed berries, fresh or frozen (blueberries, blackberries, chokecherries, or juneberries)
2 to 4 tbsp honey or maple syrup, to taste

steps.text: Combine the berries and 1 cup water in a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook for 15–20 minutes, mashing the berries with a potato masher or wooden spoon as they soften.
Stir in honey or maple syrup to taste.
For a thicker sauce, stir the cornstarch into the cold water and whisk it into the simmering berries; cook 2 minutes more until glossy.
Serve warm with fry bread or bannock, or chill and use as a spread.

recipes.title: Wonton Soup
recipes.description: Plump pork and shrimp wontons in a clear, gingery chicken broth with baby bok choy.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 4 oz shrimp, peeled, deveined, and finely chopped

steps.text: Combine the pork, shrimp, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, ginger, green onion, white pepper, and cornstarch and stir vigorously in one direction for 2 minutes until sticky.
Place 1 tsp filling in the center of a wrapper and moisten the edges with water.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle, press out the air and seal, then bring the two bottom corners together and pinch them to seal.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers, keeping the finished wontons covered with a damp towel.
Simmer the chicken broth with the ginger slices for 10 minutes, then remove the ginger and season with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the wontons in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Add the bok choy to the broth and simmer for 2 minutes.
Divide the wontons and bok choy among bowls, ladle the hot broth over them, and garnish with green onions.

recipes.photoCredit: Sumit Surai / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pork_Steamed_Wontons.jpg

recipes.title: Wonton Wrappers
recipes.description: Wonton wrappers are thin pasta-like wrappers used for wontons. They are suitable for wonton soup. Oversize (7-inch / 45 cm square) wrappers may be used as egg roll wrappers. Round wrappers are best for making potstickers.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Sift flour and salt into a large bowl; create a well-like indentation in the center.
Beat egg lightly, pour into indentation in the flour and mix well.
Sprinkle with cold water, wet your hands, and knead the mixture into a smooth dough.
Place dough in a bowl and cover with a damp cloth, refrigerate for 30 minutes to an hour.
Sprinkle a wide work area or board with flour. Roll out the dough until it is paper thin and its edges are even in thickness. The wonton skins will be partially transparent.
Cut dough in 2–3-inch (5–7.5 cm) strips, flour lightly, then stack one on top of the other and cut the strips into 2–3-inch (5–7.5 cm) squares.
Place skins on tray and cover with a damp cloth until ready to use.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: Sumit Surai / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pork_Steamed_Wontons.jpg

recipes.title: Yakisoba (Stir-Fried Noodles)
recipes.description: Chewy wheat noodles stir-fried with pork, cabbage, and carrots in a tangy-sweet yakisoba sauce, a favorite at Japanese festivals.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 3 (5 oz) packages fresh yakisoba or chukamen noodles
6 oz thinly sliced pork belly or pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tbsp aonori (dried green seaweed), for garnish
2 tbsp pickled red ginger (beni shoga), for garnish

steps.text: Whisk the Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, and sugar together in a small bowl.
Rinse the noodles briefly under hot water to loosen them, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 3 minutes until browned.
Add the onion and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Add the noodles and green onions and toss for 2 minutes until heated through.
Pour the sauce over the noodles and toss continuously for 1 to 2 minutes until evenly coated.
Serve topped with aonori and pickled red ginger.

recipes.photoCredit: Quercus acuta / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yakisoba_-_01.jpg

recipes.title: Yakitori (Grilled Chicken Skewers)
recipes.description: Bite-size chicken thigh and green onion skewers grilled over high heat and brushed with sweet-savory tare sauce.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
6 green onions (white and light green parts), cut into 1-inch lengths
12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes

steps.text: Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, and green onion tops in a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until reduced by about a third and slightly syrupy, then discard the onion tops.
Thread the chicken and green onion pieces alternately onto the soaked skewers.
Preheat a grill or broiler to high, about 450°F (230°C), and brush the grates or pan with oil.
Grill the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side until lightly charred.
Brush the skewers generously with tare and grill for 1 minute more per side, repeating two or three times to build a glaze.
Check that the chicken is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Serve hot with extra tare and a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi.

recipes.photoCredit: 竹麦魚(Searobin) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cooking_yakitori.jpg

recipes.title: Yellowman
recipes.description: A crunchy golden honeycomb toffee from Northern Ireland, famously sold at the Ould Lammas Fair in Ballycastle.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1/2 cup golden syrup or light corn syrup

steps.text: Grease an 8-inch square pan with butter.
Combine the sugar, syrup, butter, vinegar, and water in a large heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Raise the heat and boil without stirring until the mixture reaches 300°F (150°C) on a candy thermometer, the hard-crack stage, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat and immediately whisk in the baking soda; the mixture will foam up dramatically.
Pour at once into the prepared pan without spreading it, so the bubbles stay intact.
Let cool completely for about 1 hour until hard.
Break into pieces and store in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Yeung Chow Fried Rice
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: 1/4 cup (50 g) Char siu (barbecued pork), diced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a non-stick skillet, and fry the garlic until golden brown.
Add the bacon, prawn, and char siu, then cook slightly for 5 minutes.
Add the scallion, peas, and egg, and cook until all cooked.
Stir in the rice, salt, pepper and jalapeno.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Yogurt Curry Soup (Kadhi)
recipes.description: Kadhi also known as Karhi or Gujarati Kadhi is a sweet yogurt curry, normally eaten with unleavened flat bread called roti and sabzi in India.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Combine the gram flour, curds and 3 teacups of water in a pot. Beat well.
Add the chilli-ginger paste, curry leaves, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Boil whilst stirring for a while.
Heat the ghee in a pan, add the cumin and mustard seeds, and toast until light brown. Don't let burn.
Add the asafoetida and red chilli.
Add the seasoning mixture to the curry, and boil for a few minutes.
Sprinkle coriander on top and serve hot.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Yorkshire Pudding
recipes.description: A Yorkshire pudding is a light, fluffy dish that is usually cooked and served alongside a roast dinner, traditionally made with roast meat—especially roast beef. It comes from Yorkshire, a region in the United Kingdom, and is popular across the island. The exact recipe differs from area to area, even from family to family, so the below recipe offers a generic approach to the tasty pudding.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 230°C (210°C convection)
Fill your tin(s) with a thin layer of your chosen oil, and place into the oven to heat up.
Sieve flour into a bowl, then beat in eggs until smooth.
Slowly add the milk in stages, beating as you go until well-mixed.
Season with salt and pepper. Add optional ingredients as desired.
Transfer the batter to a pouring jug. For best results, rest the batter in the fridge for 1 hour.
Being swift, but careful, remove the hot tin(s) from the oven, and evenly fill the holes with your batter.

Place the tin(s) back into the oven, and leave them undisturbed for 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden brown. Opening the oven door can upset the cooking of the Yorkshire puddings—trust the process and watch with the door closed.
Serve immediately. They can also be cooled and frozen for up to 1 month.

recipes.notes: For the best Yorkshire puddings, make sure your oil is as hot as it can be. Try a little batter first to see if it instantly puffs up.
recipes.photoCredit: stef yau from Seattle, USA / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yorkshire_Pudding.jpg

recipes.title: Yubeshi (Japanese Walnut Mochi Confection)
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.
ingredients: Cornstarch or potato starch, as needed

steps.text: Generously dust a cookie sheet with cornstarch.
Combine the sugar, soy sauce, and water in a saucepan. Simmer until the sugar fully dissolves, stirring so as not to burn.
Add the rice flour, and stir well to form a cohesive dough.
Transfer the dough to a microwave-safe container. Heat it in the microwave for 30–40 seconds, then take it out and mix well. Repeat this process until it is thoroughly brown.
Mix the walnuts into the dough.
Pat the dough evenly onto the prepared cookie sheet in a layer about 5 cm (2 in) thick. If it's too hot, let it cool a bit first.
Dust the top of the dough with additional starch. Let cool fully.
Cut the confection into pieces.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates. Number of servings is an estimate.)
recipes.photoCredit: TSK-132 / Wikimedia Commons, Copyrighted free use — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yubesi08120531.jpg

recipes.title: Zaru Soba (Cold Buckwheat Noodles)
recipes.description: Chilled buckwheat noodles served on a bamboo tray with a savory dipping sauce, a cooling summer favorite.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin in a small saucepan and bring to a simmer for 1 minute.
Cool the dipping sauce, then chill it in the refrigerator.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the soba noodles, stirring to separate them.
Cook the noodles according to the package, usually 4 to 5 minutes, until just tender.
Drain and rinse the noodles thoroughly under cold running water, rubbing gently to remove the surface starch.
Plunge the noodles into ice water for 1 minute, then drain well.
Arrange the noodles on bamboo trays or plates and top with nori strips.
Serve with small cups of the chilled dipping sauce, green onions, and wasabi to stir in to taste.

recipes.title: Zimtsterne (German Cinnamon Star Cookies)
recipes.description: Zimtsterne are German cinnamon cookies often eaten for the advent season.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Whip the egg whites until creamy.
Sift in powdered sugar, and mix into egg whites.
Set aside almost a third of the resulting mass for casting.
Stir in the remaining mass of cinnamon and almonds, or hazelnuts and lemon zest, and knead into a dough.
Roll out the dough, cut out star shapes and place on the greased baking sheet.
Mix the remaining stiff egg white with rum until a glaze mass forms.
Brush the cinnamon stars with glaze.
Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C for about 20 minutes.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Zucchini Bread
recipes.description: Zucchini bread is a sweet fluffy cake or quick bread that has zucchini in it. It is delicious. There are many different ways of making it. Here is one. This recipe was derived from the lyrics of a song by a band called Chuga Chuga, from Michigan/Washington, DC, USA. They broke up in 2006.
recipes.author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
recipes.license: Text from the Wikibooks Cookbook (en.wikibooks.org) by its contributors, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Reformatted for this app.

steps.text: Grease and flour two 8 x 4-inch loaf pans. Preheat oven to 325°F.
Sift together flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Beat eggs, oil, vanilla, and sugar together in a large bowl.
Add sifted ingredients to the creamed mixture, and beat well. Stir in zucchini until well combined.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for 40 minutes to 1 hour, or until tester inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 20 minutes. Remove from pan and completely cool.

recipes.notes: (Prep/cook times are estimates.)

recipes.title: Zwetschgenkuchen (Plum Sheet Cake)
recipes.description: A late-summer yeast sheet cake covered in rows of halved Italian plums and finished with cinnamon sugar or streusel.
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.
ingredients: 3 lb Italian prune plums, halved and pitted

steps.text: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk, egg and butter, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Grease a 12 x 17-inch rimmed baking sheet and roll or press the dough evenly into it.
Cut a small slit into the top of each plum half so it fans open slightly.
Arrange the plums cut side up in tight overlapping rows over the dough.
Let rise for 20 minutes while you preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the dough is golden and the plums are juicy.
Brush with melted butter, sprinkle with the mixed cinnamon and sugar, and serve warm or cool with whipped cream.

recipes.photoCredit: Frank Vincentz / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Plum_cake2_ies.jpg

recipes.title: Zwiebelkuchen (Onion Tart)
recipes.description: A savory autumn tart of slow-cooked onions, bacon and caraway in a creamy custard, traditionally served with new wine (Federweißer).
recipes.author: Recipe Box Kitchen
recipes.license: Original recipe written for Recipe Box. Free to share.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the milk and butter, and knead into a soft dough; cover and let rise for 45 minutes.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet until it renders its fat, then add the butter and onions.
Cook the onions over medium-low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and golden; let cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a 10 x 15-inch rimmed baking sheet or a 12-inch tart pan.
Roll the dough out and press it into the pan, forming a small rim.
Whisk the sour cream, eggs, caraway, salt and pepper, then stir in the onion mixture.
Spread the filling evenly over the dough.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the filling is set and golden brown, then let rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
